[107] Working for a safe society

[108] Norway is one of the world's safest countries to live in

[109] We have a stable and democratic society with a low level of conflict

[110] We are nevertheless experiencing serious incidents that can have catastrophic consequences for the individual, and on June 18, 2015, the Storting passed the following resolution (resolution

[111] The Storting asks the government to present a new report to the Storting on societal security and preparedness by the end of

[112] Parliament 10 2016–

[113] Risk in a safe society consequences for society

[114] Powerful storms destroy houses, damage important infrastructure, and in the worst case can lead to loss of life

[115] Large landslides regularly affect local communities

[116] People who want to harm others and create fear can affect us

[117] The terrorist acts of July 22, 2011 are a tragic reminder of this

[118] Societal security is influenced both by developments in our own society and global trends

[119] The world is becoming increasingly interconnected

[120] Developments and conflicts in other parts of the world have consequences for our own security

[121] The digitalization of society creates new solutions, but also dependencies and vulnerabilities that cut across sectors, areas of responsibility and national borders

[122] No sector, and few countries, can currently control their digital vulnerability alone

[123] Cyberspace" is global and makes it possible for "anyone" to attack electronic targets "anywhere" in the world

[124] A hacker can be thousands of kilometers away and steal sensitive information from Norwegian users

[125] Critical societal functions, such as energy supply, electronic communications and financial services, depend on long, digital value chains that make us vulnerable

[126] An accident in a server park in Sweden could create serious problems for Norwegian businesses

[127] The long-term plan for the defense sector provides a picture of how the security policy situation has changed in a relatively short time

[128] We are experiencing a buildup of forces in the high north, and greater security challenges in our immediate areas than just a few years ago

[129] The combination of overt and covert military and non-military instruments, so-called hybrid instruments, challenges the distinction between peace, security crisis and armed conflict

[130] It can be challenging to determine whether a threat situation is of a civil or military nature

[131] Targeted cyber operations in social media can influence a population, and are an example of actions that challenge established defense thinking

[132] Open and trust-based societies can be vulnerable when faced with crises in the gray area between war and peace

[133] Conflicts and unrest in other parts of the world have consequences for our own national security

[134] Destabilized states and conflicts in North Africa, the Middle East and Southwest Asia are creating humanitarian crises

[135] These are tragic for those affected, can cause migration and provide fertile ground for violent extremism also in Europe and Norway

[136] Globalization means that the flow of people and goods in the world is increasing

[137] We travel more, and we travel further

[138] The risk of Norway being affected by serious infectious diseases that occur in other parts of the world is increasing

[139] Not least, the occurrence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria poses serious challenges to our modern healthcare system

[140] Crime in Norway is also affected by globalization and technological development

[141] Measured in number

[142] offenses, traditional profit-making crime has decreased in recent years

[143] At the same time, other types of crime have become more important, such as ICT crime and cross-border financial crime

[144] If serious crime becomes widespread, it can weaken citizens' trust in the state and, over time, constitute a threat to societal security

[145] A changing climate could result in more and more serious natural events in Norway, not least floods, landslides and extreme weather

[146] Areas that were previously considered safe may become more vulnerable

[147] Climate change can also have indirect effects, for example, melting of the polar ice cap could open up new shipping routes between Northeast Asia and Europe, with the emergency preparedness challenges this entails

[148] Globally, severe natural events can contribute to water and food shortages, more frequent disease outbreaks, political unrest, crime and migration

[149] Developmental trends are often interrelated and can reinforce each other

[150] Such connections increase uncertainty about what changes will occur and how hard they may affect us

[151] A resilient society

[152] The authorities have a special responsibility for the safety of the population, and public resources and efforts form the core of public safety work

[153] However, a society's ability to prevent and manage crises depends on more than public resources and efforts

[154] Contributions from private businesses, voluntary organizations, local communities and individuals are also important

[155] Norway is a society rich in material, economic and human resources

[156] This provides a good foundation for work on societal security

[157] Trust between authorities and citizens is high in Norway compared to many other countries

[158] It is also important for societal security that citizens experience that the authorities are capable of solving fundamental challenges facing society

[159] Developments in several countries in recent years show that this is not something we can take for granted

[160] Trust must be created through an active and solution-oriented policy

[161] Local knowledge, local creativity and local networks have often proven important in handling large and unforeseen events

[162] The foundation is good neighborliness, solidarity and care for each other

[163] It is important to maintain and develop preparedness and the ability to withstand crises and stress

[164] Risk in a safe society at the local level

[165] Both individuals and businesses share responsibility for their own safety

[166] We must all take responsibility for how our own actions can affect the safety of others

[167] Cross-sectoral, risk-aware and value-based

[168] Social security is largely cross-sectoral

[169] A flood, a prolonged power outage, a serious gas explosion or a terrorist attack cannot be handled within one sector alone, or at a single level of administration

[170] The work requires coordination and cooperation across sector boundaries and between authorities at local, regional and central levels

[171] At the same time, the work on social security is broad-ranging

[172] We will prevent and handle incidents that occur, and we will implement measures that can restore damage caused by incidents

[173] We must learn from what has happened so that we are better prepared the next time an incident occurs

[174] An important prerequisite for good public safety is that we understand the specific challenges that working with public safety presents us with

[175] Societal safety is about working systematically with possible events that it is uncertain whether will ever occur

[176] We must be able to adapt measures to changes in the risk and vulnerability picture

[177] A vigilant and risk-aware culture is important

[178] Daily work, through learning from exercises and events, is crucial to success

[179] We must be able to "change pace" when the crisis occurs

[180] Good planning and good routines are the foundation of emergency preparedness work

[181] At the same time, we must prepare ourselves for the fact that crises are about the surprising and demanding

[182] We must stimulate attitudes and a culture that enables us to solve tasks even under unforeseen circumstances

[183] With today's society and challenges as a backdrop, work on societal security will be further developed

[184] The work involves weighing up different values ​​and considerations

[185] For example, we want to prevent serious crime, but we do not want a society based on pervasive surveillance of public or private spaces

[186] We want to prevent pandemics and sources of infection from gaining a foothold in Norway, but we do not want to restrict people's right to travel

[187] The work on social security also revolves around the kind of society we want to develop and live in

[188] The dilemmas are there, and they often cannot be removed

[189] We need to take a position on them and how they should be handled

[190] The future will bring with it unwanted events that we can hardly foresee

[191] It is likely that the unlikely will happen, and it is economically and practically impossible to eliminate all risk

[192] We do not want a society that is permeated with security measures

[193] It is not compatible with a free and open society like Norway

[227] Risk in a safe society

[228] The report presents the government's policy for work on social security in Norway in a four-year perspective

[229] What is social security

[230] Societal security is society's ability to protect itself against and handle incidents that threaten fundamental values ​​and functions and put life and health at risk

[231] Such events can be triggered by nature, be the result of technical or human errors or deliberate actions

[232] The work on social security involves municipalities, county governors, directorates, national professional bodies, ministries and the government

[233] The four fundamental principles of responsibility, equality, proximity and cooperation form the basis of the work

[234] They clarify the responsibilities of actors and set guidelines for collaboration and handling of incidents

[235] Community safety work consists of several links, often referred to as a chain

[236] The chain includes knowledge building, prevention and preparedness for incidents, handling and recovery from incidents, and learning from incidents and exercises

[237] Chapter 3 provides an introduction to the field of public safety

[238] Living with risk

[239] The work on societal security is about identifying, assessing and managing risk

[240] There are, however, limits to how far the work can and should be extended

[241] It is not possible to eliminate all risk – a residual risk will always be there

[242] It is also not desirable to create a 100 percent secure society

[243] Measures may conflict with fundamental values such as self-determination, personal freedom, legal certainty and privacy

[244] The costs of security measures may also exceed the benefits we estimate the measure will provide us

[245] Being aware of and preventing such possible effects is an important part of the work on societal security

[246] A society rich in material, economic and human resources will have a greater overall ability to prevent and manage incidents, and it will be less vulnerable if a single resource is put out of action

[247] It will be easier to maintain and, if necessary, rebuild important societal functions

[248] Norway therefore has good prospects for being a resilient society

[249] The Government will contribute to the debate on the fundamental challenges and dilemmas of living with risk

[250] Chapter 4 is therefore devoted to this theme

[251] The government will: – work for a safe society

[252] At the same time, there is a limit to security measures, and risk must be accepted to a certain extent. Chapter

[253] Our ability to handle incidents As a society, we must be prepared to handle incidents when they occur

[254] Such management requires coordinated efforts from many actors, ranging from emergency services, municipalities, government agencies, to voluntary organizations and private businesses

[255] A police force with greater capacity, a more professional fire and rescue service, a better emergency reporting service, better communication during crises and a strengthened rescue service are important goals for the work

[256] The government will: – follow up

[257] The local police reform to ensure a police force with good capacity and professionalism in emergency response and crisis management – ​​that the police districts should have cooperation agreements, instructions and exercises that ensure operational management and capacity across district borders – ensure that the geographical areas of responsibility for the emergency reporting service for the fire and rescue service (110 centres) are adapted to the areas of responsibility of the new police districts – strengthen fire training by establishing a new training model for fire and rescue personnel Report

[259] Risk in a safe society – assess new requirements in the regulations that are adapted to greater fire cooperation and a new education model – strengthen the emergency service by, among other things, implementing measures in the “Program for improving the emergency service”, so that citizens receive rapid and best possible assistance in emergency situations – continue the co-location of the emergency service centres for the fire and rescue service (110 centres) and the police operations centres (112 centres) – strengthen preparedness by facilitating more emergency and preparedness actors to become users of Nødnett – complete the interconnection of Nødnett and the Swedish emergency network RAKEL, so that cooperation across national borders can be strengthened and made easier – facilitate good communication solutions for the emergency and preparedness agencies – work towards a future-oriented Civil Defence – facilitate and plan for the reception of 16 new rescue helicopters, the first of which will be received in 2017 and put into operation in 2018 – have a close dialogue with the voluntary rescue and emergency response organizations on framework conditions and measures that can strengthen interaction between the volunteers and other actors in the rescue service – request

[261] Digital vulnerabilities and ICT security

[262] Norway is one of the world's most digitalized countries

[263] The benefits of ICT are significant for society as a whole, and digital development is a crucial part of our value creation and growth

[264] Digitalization has also changed society's risk picture

[265] Businesses and individuals must have confidence that systems and networks function as they should and protect the privacy of individuals

[266] Good ICT security is a prerequisite for achieving this trust

[267] In addition, we must have sufficient national capacity to detect and handle digital attacks

[268] In this report, the main recommendations from the Digital Vulnerability Committee (Lysneutvalget) have been considered in particular

[269] In 2017, the Ministry of Justice and Public Security will submit a separate report to the Storting on the follow-up to the Lysne Commission's recommendations

[270] The Government will: – consider establishing a national framework that provides uniform and cross-sectoral regulation in the area of ICT security

[271] The work will be seen in the context of the EU directive on measures for a common level of security in network and information systems (NIS Directive), and assessments from the Security Committee – preparing a new national strategy for ICT security

[272] The strategy shall state the government's goals and strategic priorities within the ICT security area

[273] In addition, an action plan will be prepared – to increase ICT security competence in the sectoral authorities

[274] The National Security Authority (NSM) shall establish a common arena where sectoral authorities can coordinate planned supervisory activities and exchange experiences within the ICT security area – developing and maintaining a good and accessible knowledge base that enables individuals, businesses and authorities to take appropriate measures

[275] For this purpose, among other things, NSM's report

[276] The overall ICT risk picture is further developed – strengthen ICT security in state administration and support the digitalization of the public sector – further develop the national ability to detect and handle digital attacks, by further developing the alert system for digital infrastructure (VDI) and establishing a national framework for digital incident management – facilitate the long-term development of ICT security competence, by preparing a national competence strategy for ICT security

[277] The measure also involves awareness-raising activities aimed at the population and businesses – strengthening the security and robustness of electronic communications networks (ecom networks

[278] The Norwegian Communications Authority (Nkom) will assess vulnerability-reducing measures related to the dependence on Telenor's core infrastructure, and how different transport networks and international connections can be combined to increase overall national capacity and security

[279] Digital vulnerability – secure society

[280] Risk in a safe society – clarify which authorities are responsible for safety within Norwegian space activities

[281] Most critical societal functions depend on satellite-based services, and it is crucial that the security aspect is taken care of – revise national crypto policy

[282] Encryption is of great importance for ICT security and supports secure electronic communication – participate and contribute internationally to solving common issues within ICT security across nations – prepare a report to the Storting on the follow-up of the Lysne Commission's recommendations with an overview of short-term and long-term priorities in the follow-up work, as well as the status in affected sectors

[283] Every year, natural events such as floods, landslides and storms destroy large amounts of valuables

[284] This costs the individual and society significant sums

[285] Climate change will most likely lead to continued warmer and wetter weather in Norway

[286] The challenges posed by natural events will therefore likely become greater in the years to come

[287] Good preventive work and active adaptation to a changing climate are important to handle the challenges as best as possible

[288] The Government will: – contribute to ensuring that municipalities’ work on social security in social and spatial planning is of high quality in order to reduce the consequences of serious natural events, including by completing a national digital elevation and terrain model – improve society’s ability to manage flood and landslide risk – make it easier for municipalities to take social security and climate change into account in their long-term planning, by contributing guidance and research-based knowledge – expand the natural damage insurance scheme to include land costs – contribute actively to the EU and UN’s work on social security and follow up on the UN’s Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030 programme

[289] Crime is constantly changing

[290] A common feature of today's developments is that crime is becoming increasingly technologically advanced, organized and global

[291] Radicalization and violent extremism, intelligence against Norway and Norwegian interests, ICT crime, money laundering, terrorist financing and workplace crime are areas of crime that can threaten societal security

[292] The government will: – follow up on the measures in the government’s action plan against radicalization and violent extremism and develop new measures in line with the risk picture in the field – strengthen the analytical capacity of the Police Security Service (PST), so that the agency is better able to combat terrorist acts on Norwegian soil – facilitate the PST to target its threat assessments to a greater extent on those actors who have responsibility for and authority to implement measures during a crisis situation – make it easier to deny potential foreign fighters passports – establish secure and efficient identity management based on biometrics, so that secure passports and national ID cards with eID are issued – continue to work to strengthen cooperation between government agencies and the business community in order to be better equipped against state or non-state digital attacks against Norway and Norwegian interests – follow up and further develop

[293] The Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness' strategy against ICT crime: – ensure that a special, joint threat assessment for ICT crime is prepared annually in the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness' area of expertise – build a highly competent professional environment within the police that will strengthen the fight against ICT crime – strengthen the police districts' basic competence and professional environments within ICT crime – strengthen the police's basic education and continuing and further education within ICT crime – implement the measures in the action plan against human trafficking – strengthen the work against money laundering and terrorist financing, by implementing the government's strategy against money laundering and terrorist financing and preparing a National Risk Assessment in the area – strengthen cooperation between the police and the supervisory authorities, including by further developing inter-agency intelligence and analysis functions – develop the rules on confidentiality so that it contributes to better information exchange and communication

[297] Infectious diseases and dangerous substances – better CBRNE preparedness Increased global travel, international trade in plants, animals and food, climate change and increased incidence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria can increase the risk of the spread of infection and disease outbreaks in Norway

[298] A serious pandemic could result in many sick and dead people, and would challenge the capacity of infection control, health services and other important societal functions

[299] Antibiotics are a prerequisite for a well functioning, modern healthcare system, and resistant bacteria represent a significant risk

[300] A number of substances that industry, business, the transport sector and agriculture are completely dependent on can pose a danger

[301] Accidents or intentional actions can have serious consequences

[302] Better preparedness against serious incidents involving chemical substances (C), biological agents (B), radioactive substances (R), nuclear material (N) and explosives (E) is necessary

[303] The government therefore published a national strategy for CBRNE preparedness in the autumn of 2016, which is an important basis for the government's work going forward

[304] The Government will: – strengthen national preparedness against biological incidents by establishing a cross-sectoral collaborative arena for preparedness against biological incidents at directorate level and establish a national preparedness plan against serious infectious diseases, following up on the experiences from the efforts against Ebola in West Africa 2014–2015 and other incidents – further develop efforts against pandemic influenza in line with the National Preparedness Plan against Pandemic Influenza, through international and national work to improve prevention, surveillance, warning, management and continuity planning – intensify work against antibiotic resistance by reducing and more appropriate use of antibiotics, improving the knowledge base and by being a driving force in international work – that the Ministry of Justice and Public Security shall establish a “Collaborative Area for Chemical and Explosives Preparedness” to contribute to cross-sectoral, comprehensive and coordinated work with CE preparedness at directorate level and provide good professional advice to local, regional and central level – implement measures to improve the prevention of chemical and explosive incidents and assess whether some fire and rescue services should develop special capacities to handle CE incidents – strengthen international cooperation, especially to prevent illegal access to weapons, explosives and explosive precursors – that the Ministry of Justice and Public Security should assess the need and possibilities for establishing a chemicals institute to assist local, regional and central levels and strengthen research and development – ​​formalise the function of the Defence Research Institute as a receiving laboratory for unknown CBRE samples – develop civil-military cooperation within bomb preparedness and explosive ordnance disposal – expand the planning basis for nuclear preparedness with a scenario that includes the use of nuclear weapons near or on Norwegian territory, and prepare measures for such an event

[305] Civil-military cooperation and total defense

[306] The security situation in our part of the world is more demanding than it has been in a long time

[307] In order for the Norwegian Defence Force to be able to carry out its tasks, cooperation with public authorities and private actors within the framework of total defence is necessary

[308] Civilian crisis management and societal security will, in turn, benefit from the Armed Forces' assistance

[309] Mutual civil-military cooperation has become increasingly relevant and must be strengthened in the years ahead, both nationally and within NATO

[310] The Government will: – ensure that plans are established for civilian support to the Armed Forces in crisis and armed conflict, including for allied reinforcements – continuously assess whether existing prioritization mechanisms between military and civilian needs are sufficient – ​​adapt relevant cooperation and emergency response bodies to challenges in connection with security crises and armed conflict, in order to be able to support both known and unforeseen needs – ensure that civilian support to the Armed Forces becomes an increasingly integrated part of exercise activities and is included in both civilian and military exercise programs as well as in national emergency planning 2016–

[311] Risk in a safe society – prepare new instructions for the Armed Forces' assistance to the police. – ensure adequate counter-terrorism preparedness exercises – complete the police and the Armed Forces’ plans for securing all objects reported by the police to the Armed Forces, as well as practice securing the objects within available resource limits – prepare an instruction on the Armed Forces’ assistance to public authorities other than the police – consider better infection control transport with rescue helicopters and the Armed Forces’ transport aircraft for military and civilian needs – cooperate more closely on plans that include civil-military cooperation, prioritize mutual civil-military support and cooperation in exercise arrangements, and where appropriate, cooperate on procurement – ensure that developments in NATO are reflected in the continuous development of our preparedness plans – contribute civilian expertise from both the public and private sectors to NATO’s work on civil preparedness – establish a program to further develop total defense and follow up on NATO’s seven basic expectations for resilient critical societal functions – strengthen cooperation with allies to protect national interests in the digital space – contribute to NATO's work to further develop political dialogue and practical civil-military emergency preparedness cooperation in the Nordic region

[312] Attitudes, culture and leadership for good societal security

[313] Professional management and good leadership are important in the work with societal security

[314] The government is working to strengthen management support and coordination of social security work

[315] There is a need for a better culture at all levels of the social security chain

[316] The work must be based on an updated understanding of risk and vulnerabilities

[317] Good crisis management requires more from leaders and organizations than everyday life – it requires a “change of pace.”

[318] Clarified responsibilities, good understanding of roles and well-thought-out routines

[319] is created through practical experience, exercises and reflection on one's own and others' practice

[320] Dialogue, division of responsibility and understanding of roles must be good both across levels in the crisis management apparatus and between the actors

[321] The Government will: – build a stronger culture of collaboration, results and implementation in the administration, including through the Programme for Better Governance and Management in the State – actively use emergency preparedness conferences in the Government, regular meetings of the Government Security Committee and active coordination by the Crisis Council to ensure that public safety issues are continuously handled and anchored in the Government – devote the necessary attention to the special challenges in public safety work, through active use of collaborative arenas at all levels in the administration – set clearer requirements for leaders and ensure that public safety work is anchored in management, through, among other things, changes in planning, supervision and follow-up of exercises – develop a police force that creates good results in a culture characterised by openness and trust, where management is prominent in all parts of the agency, from the service out on patrol and to the police's national leadership group – stimulate good cooperation at municipal, regional and national levels, between the emergency services, with emergency response actors more generally and with business and voluntary actors – work to improve the safety culture in businesses and in society in general, including through competence-raising measures and better risk recognition – work for good crisis management and the ability to “change pace” during crises, where good understanding of roles and responsibilities is clarified and understood, both between levels and across involved actors and sectors – that the Norwegian Police College further develops joint continuing and further education for the emergency and emergency response agencies Chapter

[350] St. 10 Risk in a safe society What is societal security

[351] An introduction

[352] As citizens of Norway, we want to be able to shape our own lives, including through choosing education, profession, family life and leisure activities

[353] The freedom to make one's own choices is a fundamental good in our society

[354] Some choose to take a risk by starting an entrepreneurial business, while others prefer a more secure professional career

[355] While many people choose to spend their vacation on the beach, others use their vacation to go base jumping

[356] At the same time, we have a responsibility for choices that affect our own safety and the values we want to protect

[357] We can secure loose objects when a storm is approaching

[358] We can wear seat belts and adjust our speed to the conditions when driving

[359] We can install antivirus software on the PC

[360] Doing these things can reduce the likelihood of an adverse event occurring

[361] However, some dangers and threats are so great or unforeseen that we as individuals have no way of protecting ourselves against them

[362] We need the help of the wider community to protect us from floods, landslides, pandemics, terrorist attacks and similar events

[363] We need a police force, a fire and rescue service, a health service, a defense force and a number of other services that can help us on the day things really go wrong

[364] We must also have an administration that has a driving role and primary responsibility for creating a safe society

[365] Security and a stable society are fundamental prerequisites for us to be able to live good lives

[366] An important purpose of the work on societal security is to create this security and stability

[367] In this message, the following definition of the term social security is used

[368] Society's ability to protect itself against and manage events that threaten fundamental values ​​and functions and put life and health at risk

[369] Such events can be triggered by nature, be the result of technical or human errors or deliberate actions

[370] The concept of social security is widely used

[371] It covers protection against all serious situations across the entire spectrum of challenges, from accidents in peacetime to situations that threaten the security and independence of the kingdom

[372] The work on social security is complex and divided between a number of actors who carry out different tasks

[373] Among other things, municipalities must conduct good spatial planning to avoid housing being built too close to industrial activities or where they could be affected by floods or landslides

[374] Grid companies must consider the risk of extreme weather when planning power lines

[375] Emergency services must be prepared to deal with a variety of different incidents, from major accidents, rescue operations, floods and acute pollution to school shootings and terrorism

[376] The departments and directorates must develop overall plans, strategies and regulations that help us utilize society's resources in the best possible way

[377] Societal security is influenced by three factors: – the values we are to protect and their vulnerabilities – the dangers and threats we face – our ability to prevent and manage

[378] Awareness of values ​​is central

[379] We need to know what to protect

[380] Social security work consists, among other things, of defining which social functions are critical for safeguarding fundamental values, and planning to be able to maintain these functions regardless of stress

[381] Knowledge of dangers and threats is important in order to secure valuables

[382] We are threatened by natural events, accidents and people who want to harm individuals or society

[383] Serious natural events can be, for example, storms, floods and landslides

[384] Accidents can typically be major fires or transport accidents

[385] Actions carried out by people who wish to harm society, often referred to as intentional undesirable actions, include acts of terrorism, espionage, sabotage and military attacks

[386] The authorities must both prevent unwanted incidents from occurring and enable society to handle those incidents that do occur

[387] At the same time, we must have the ability to cope with the unexpected

[388] There may be rare and large messages

[389] Parliament 10 2016–

[390] Risks in a safe society are events that require extraordinary effort

[391] As a society, we should also be able to quickly return to normal after being exposed to a crisis

[392] The continuous work of creating this ability can be divided into several "links", which together form a chain, see chapter

[393] The four principles of social security

[394] In Norway, work on societal security is based on four fundamental principles

[395] responsibility, equality, closeness and cooperation

[396] They apply to all types of crises, from natural events and accidents to security crises and armed conflict

[397] The responsibility principle means that all organizations that have day-to-day responsibility for a professional area also have responsibility for public safety in the area, regardless of the type of incident

[398] The responsibility involves identifying which threats and incidents may affect the organization, preventing incidents, preparing crisis and emergency plans, establishing a crisis organization if necessary, and implementing security and emergency measures

[399] This responsibility also includes a balancing of acceptable risk, see chapter

[400] The responsibility principle applies to all ministries within their own sector, directorates and other government agencies, municipalities and county authorities

[401] For the state, the principle of responsibility is rooted in the government's constitutional responsibility and the distribution of responsibilities between ministers

[402] The responsibility principle implies an obligation to maintain important functions and tasks within one's own organization if an extraordinary event occurs

[403] Most challenges within societal security cut across sectors and levels of administration

[404] In many cases, there are therefore several responsible authorities and actors

[405] Coordination is therefore necessary to ensure that different goals, activities, instruments and resources are seen in context and are prioritized, weighed and adapted to each other

[406] Coordination in this context is about clarifying responsibilities, distributing tasks and ensuring necessary clarifications and decisions

[407] Sufficient and good coordination with others with adjacent areas of responsibility is part of the responsibility principle

[408] For the state, it is ultimately the government's collective responsibility to find the solutions that are best overall when challenges cut across each individual minister's area of responsibility

[409] The constitutional responsibility of the Council of State does not stand in the way of appropriate coordination

[410] In addition to its sectoral responsibility, the Ministry of Justice and Public Security has been assigned a general coordination role on the civilian side for public security

[411] The principle of similarity means that the organization during a crisis should be as similar as possible to the daily organization

[412] People and organizations master their tasks best when they know and have trained in them

[413] Experience and knowledge about responsibilities, roles and resources that are acquired through daily work are therefore a good starting point for effective crisis management

[414] However, the principle of equality is a starting point and must be weighed against the needs that arise, especially during major incidents

[415] The principle should not prevent organizations that need it from establishing and practicing their own, reinforced crisis organization

[416] This is especially true for handling large boxes

[417] Basic principles for working with societal security

[418] “Emergency preparedness work is based on four fundamental principles

[419] The responsibility principle, which means that the organization that is responsible for a subject area in a normal situation is also responsible for the necessary emergency preparations and for handling extraordinary events in the area. The similarity principle, which means that the organization one operates with during crises should initially be as similar as possible to the organization one has on a daily basis

[420] The principle of proximity, which means that crises should be handled organizationally

[421] at the lowest possible level

[422] The principle of cooperation, which means that authorities, businesses or agencies have an independent responsibility to ensure the best possible cooperation with relevant actors and businesses in the work of prevention, preparedness and crisis management

[427] Paths to coordination in Norwegian administration

[428] St. 10 Risk in a safe society and complex crises where the daily organization, and the resources at its disposal, are insufficient

[429] The subsidiarity principle means that crises should be handled at the lowest possible level

[430] What is the lowest possible level depends on the type of crisis

[431] The goal is to ensure rapid and effective handling of the crisis by actors who have the necessary knowledge and have the necessary resources, material and expertise

[432] Most often, these are emergency response actors geographically close to the incident, such as the local emergency services, the health service and the municipalities

[433] In a crisis, it is often an advantage to have short command chains

[434] However, the subsidiarity principle should not prevent actors from requesting help and support

[435] This may be because resources are insufficient, or because needs dictate that crisis management be elevated to a higher management level

[436] The lowest possible level may, for certain types of crises, mean a central authority level, as crisis management may require special professional expertise and decisions that must be made at a central level

[437] Such crisis management will require that emergency response actors at regional and local levels also take action

[438] One such example is nuclear preparedness, where a separate crisis committee has been established

[439] The committee shall provide expertise to handle nuclear incidents and ensure that measures are implemented quickly

[440] Another example is situations where our territorial integrity and national sovereignty are threatened

[441] Security crises and armed conflict have clear consequences for national security and a political, military and international dimension

[442] This requires overall management and coordination from a central government level

[443] The principle of cooperation specifies that responsible authorities, businesses and agencies shall ensure the best possible cooperation and collaboration with all relevant actors in the work of prevention, preparedness and crisis management

[444] The intention is for agencies, private and voluntary organizations to use their resources and expertise to solve tasks together

[445] This means developing good forms of collaboration with the actors with whom it is necessary to collaborate, clarifying and taking into account mutual dependencies, and viewing resources as a whole

[446] Joint emergency preparedness preparations in the form of plans, training, exercises, evaluation and learning are of utmost importance

[447] Good collaboration requires understanding, trust and knowledge of each other's resources, expertise, organization and culture, and a willingness to make resources available

[448] Good collaboration is achieved where the parties meet with an open attitude towards the perspectives and expertise of others, and where attention is directed towards ensuring that the task is solved in the best possible way overall

[449] Social security as a chain

[450] Work on social security must be systematic

[451] Different parts of social security work are interrelated, and how good we are at one part affects other parts of the work

[452] If we are good at prevention, we will have fewer incidents that we have to deal with

[453] If we are good at learning after an incident, we will handle the next incident better

[454] It is therefore natural to view the work on social security as a continuous chain

[455] The figure below illustrates this

[456] In working with societal security, it is important to have knowledge of our strengths and weaknesses within all “links” in the societal security chain

[457] This makes the work more targeted and efficient

[458] Below is a brief description of the various links in the chain

[459] Work on societal security should be knowledge- and experience-based

[460] We must seek knowledge about which measures, based on experience, work best, and prioritize these

[461] We must develop and use good methods that give us knowledge about the challenges that threaten our values, so that we know what to base our work on societal security on

[467] We must have knowledge about our critical societal functions, that is, which functions society must maintain at all times for the sake of societal safety

[468] We must also have knowledge about the interdependencies between the various critical societal functions

[469] For example, there is little in our society today that functions without electricity and electronic communication

[470] Community safety work should be a natural part of business planning and management in every organization

[471] Knowledge of local conditions, the specific nature of organizations and their own risk assessments, together with analyses and guidance as mentioned above, should provide a knowledge base that improves the quality of work with societal security

[472] This is discussed in more detail in chapter

[473] Prevention is all work that can reduce the possibility of an undesirable event occurring, or reduce the consequences of a possible event in advance

[474] Prevention can be protective measures, regulations, standards or awareness-raising work

[475] Examples of preventive measures are spatial planning that takes into account hazards, anti-racial measures, work to counter radicalization, use of anti-virus programs, access control, and securing buildings and computer systems

[476] There may also be the establishment of dual or alternative solutions (redundancy), so that, for example, a power outage can be replaced with power supply from another source

[477] Preventive measures should be in place before incidents occur, and are therefore part of the normal state

[478] Wearing a bicycle helmet prevents possible head injuries, even if you have never been, and perhaps never will be, involved in a bicycle accident

[479] Preparedness Having good preparedness means being well prepared

[480] Emergency preparedness is planned and prepared measures that enable us to handle incidents and reduce the consequences of what has occurred

[481] Examples of preparedness include having updated plans, procedures and collaboration routines that provide clear instructions on what to do if a crisis occurs

[482] There may be technical aids to support crisis management, such as management systems, situation and operations centers, and communication systems, which enable us to effectively communicate, instruct, and manage during a crisis

[483] Preparedness also means having operational resources and materials available that can help handle the incident

[484] It is important that preparedness is practiced, and that everyone with tasks has participated in exercises

[485] Exercises provide knowledge about one's own skills, procedures, resources and how other actors work

[486] It is also important for good collaboration, see Chapter 12 Better learning after exercises and incidents

[487] Good management requires good preparedness and that those who will handle the crisis have the necessary powers

[488] Handling includes observing, analyzing, deciding, communicating, allocating resources and, if necessary, securing evidence

[489] Handling includes both handling of incidents that have occurred and handling of acute danger of such incidents

[490] When the handling of an incident comes to an end, the task becomes gradually to restore normalcy

[491] It can either be to restore the situation as it was before the incident, or to re-establish a new normal state, if there are considerations that indicate that something should be changed, because we have learned something from the incident

[492] Recovery involves mapping damage and implementing measures that will have an effect both in the short term and in the longer term

[493] What gives events and exercises value is that we can learn from them

[494] However, there is no automaticity in our learning from events and exercises; we must have a conscious attitude towards this

[495] Learning involves evaluating incidents and exercises with the aim of identifying, among other things, DSB's crisis scenarios, NSM's comprehensive ICT risk picture, the E-Service's assessment of current security challenges and PST's annual, open threat assessments

[496] DSB publishes several guides, including for risk and vulnerability analyses

[497] NSM has published the Risk Assessment for Security manual

[498] A guide to counter-terrorism has also been published by [Organisation name], PST and NSM in collaboration

[499] For more information, see in particular DSB's report Critical Functions of Society, which will be completed by the end of

[501] Who is responsible for public safety

[502] Central to the work on societal security are operational resources

[503] They make an effort where the events occur

[504] These are fire and rescue personnel, police personnel and ambulance personnel who are first at the scene of an accident and save lives

[505] There are personnel in hospitals, the Civil Defense, the rescue helicopter service and voluntary organizations who carry out rescue operations and assist people in need

[506] Together with the Armed Forces, these operational resources form the spearhead of the work on societal security

[507] In addition to these operational resources, societal security also depends on a number of other resources

[508] First in line among these are the municipalities

[509] Municipalities are responsible for identifying risks within their boundaries and planning accordingly

[510] The municipality's work will be compiled into a comprehensive risk and vulnerability analysis

[511] Municipalities are charged with a number of duties, such as crisis management, spatial planning, health preparedness and operation of the fire and rescue service

[512] Through the statutory municipal emergency preparedness obligation, municipalities must ensure that risk and vulnerability in the local community are reduced as far as possible

[513] In a crisis situation, municipalities must ensure that the various resources are coordinated so that they can collectively contribute to keeping the extent of damage as small as possible

[514] The County Governor is the state's representative in the counties, and is responsible for following up on decisions, goals and guidelines from the Storting and the government

[515] The county governors are the link between the state and the municipalities, and have a special responsibility for coordinating and supervising the work on social security in the county

[516] They shall also be a driving force and guide for municipalities in their work with social security

[517] The county governors shall prepare a risk and vulnerability analysis for the entire county (county ROS

[518] The county governors have a coordinating role in handling crises

[519] The directorates and national professional bodies are the state's professional bodies, often with responsibility for important operational resources (the police, the health service, etc

[530] Box 3.2 Public-private collaboration

[531] Where private actors have a significant responsibility for societal security, for example by being owners of critical infrastructure, legal regulation, licensing conditions and other forms of government governance are necessary to ensure societal security

[532] However, the government is concerned that cooperation between the public and private sectors should also be used to achieve good social security

[533] Public-private cooperation refers here to all types of arrangements in which the public sector interacts with the private sector to solve tasks in the area of public security

[534] Current forms of cooperation include: – sharing information to gain a common understanding of risks in daily life, as well as a common situational understanding during crises – identifying available resources for crisis management and recovery – entering into letters of intent – joint training and exercises – permanent liaison arrangements – established communication channels and guidelines – representation of private actors in crisis teams/operations centers – manned emergency response centers in private companies

[535] Among the established schemes for public-private collaboration in Norway, the following can be mentioned: – the rescue service, which is based on collaboration in which private actors have a central role – the alert system for digital infrastructure (VDI) – a public-private collaboration related to the detection, prevention and handling of ICT incidents

[536] NSM organizes and operates a sensor network for both public and private actors to detect and verify attempted attacks against Norwegian infrastructure

[537] NSM has established several forums related to this type of problem – Ekomsikretsforum – a forum for the exchange of information between authorities and private actors within ekom – the cooperation agreement between Kripos and the Norwegian Business Security Council on combating ICT crime in and against the business sector – NorSIS – an independent organization that works to increase knowledge about and understanding of information security (a "Safe Traffic" within ICT, which receives grants from the Ministry of Justice and Public Security) – CCIS – Center for Cyber and Information Security, a collaboration between public and private actors to increase society’s competence and skills in handling ICT-related crime – cooperation agreements with distributors/wholesalers on food distribution – cooperation with the Norwegian Shipowners’ Association on a preparedness secretariat in the association that carries out tasks for and in collaboration with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries – the Armed Forces’ agreements with private actors

[538] Some of these agreements can also be made available to civil authorities, for example the agreement with SAS on air evacuation

[539] Private actors can be both private and state-owned enterprises (businesses), voluntary organizations, foundations and in certain cases also private individuals

[541] Risk in a safe society

[542] The ministries must work systematically to have an overview of risk and vulnerability, and be the facilitator and driver of preventive and preparedness measures in their own sector

[543] They must ensure the correct use of instruments, including the development of regulations

[544] Many challenges cut across the ministries' sectoral responsibilities, and the Ministry of Justice and Public Security has general, overarching coordination responsibility on the civilian side and is to ensure national and comprehensive public security work

[545] The Government, as a body, has the ultimate responsibility for societal security

[546] Businesses with responsibility for critical societal functions are also of great importance

[547] These include, for example, the food distributors who ensure that we have access to food, the energy companies that provide our power supply, and the telecommunications companies that ensure that we have functioning telephones, mobile phones, and access to the internet

[548] These companies' emergency preparedness tasks are regulated by legislation or in agreements with the authorities

[549] Furthermore, these are in turn dependent on a number of commercial companies that provide important services related to operations and maintenance

[550] There is a responsibility on individuals and private businesses in society as a whole

[551] Some duties of importance to social security are enshrined in law

[552] For example, all private individuals are obliged to install fire alarms in their homes and to exercise caution in traffic

[553] All businesses are obliged to provide a safe working environment for their employees, and businesses within hazardous industries are subject to strict requirements for safe operation and are regularly inspected

[554] From the authorities' perspective, it is desirable that individual citizens and businesses – in addition to acting based on statutory obligations and self-interest – also act based on how one's own actions can affect others in society

[555] A good fire safety culture in one house can reduce the risk of surrounding houses being affected by fire

[556] Similarly, high ICT security in one company can reduce the risk of criminals abusing the company's systems to attack other businesses

[557] Everyone must take responsibility for ensuring that overall social security is good

[558] A common understanding of concepts, or knowledge of each other's use of concepts, is a prerequisite for understanding each other and being able to interact, whether during incidents or in other contexts

[564] Below is a scenario that describes how handling would theoretically take place in an imagined crisis situation

[565] The purpose of the example is to illustrate crisis management mechanisms; it does not describe how the incident would necessarily have unfolded in reality

[566] Forest fire – What happens when the fire and rescue service receives the first call

[567] During a forest walk in Eastern Norway, Gunnar notices heavy smoke a few kilometers ahead of him

[568] As he gets closer, he sees that the smoke is coming from a forest fire

[569] It has been hot summer weather for several weeks, and the forest is scorching dry

[570] Gunnar immediately calls the emergency number 110 for the fire and rescue service

[571] The operator at the emergency call center realizes the seriousness of the situation and notifies several local fire and rescue services

[572] Due to the extent and rapid development of the fire, the operators simultaneously notify the police operations center and the emergency medical communications center

[573] Not far from the fire is a town, and the fire is spreading downwind towards the settlement

[574] It turns out that an industrial area on the outskirts of the town houses a company that stores large quantities of toxic substances, including chlorine and ammonia

[575] The police chief in the district believes that there may be a danger to life and health here that will require immediate action from several partners, and the Joint Rescue Service (JRCC) is therefore notified

[576] HRS agrees that this is considered a rescue operation, and the police chief must therefore take on the role of head of the local rescue center (LRS

[577] Due to the potential of the incident, the Chief of Police chooses to call in the members of the rescue management team; representatives from the Armed Forces, the Directorate of Health, the Civil Defence, Avinor, the fire and rescue service, the County Governor's Emergency Response Organisation and voluntary organisations

[578] When the rescue team is called in, it leads and coordinates the rescue

[580] Risk in a safe society the operation at a higher level, but it is still the operations manager in the police operations centre who is responsible for the direct coordination of the rescue operation, on behalf of the rescue management

[581] Other local and relevant emergency response resources are also called in as advisors, including a representative from the local industrial safety service (the rescue force in the industrial area, consisting of employees in the company

[582] At the same time, the municipality is implementing its crisis plan, including creating shelters for 1,200 residents whom the police have begun evacuating

[583] However, the public does not know which chemicals are located at the industrial company in question, and uncertainty arises as to whether the local emergency room is prepared for any injuries related to chemicals

[584] The municipal administration learns from the police chief that experts from the CBRNE Center at Oslo University Hospital have been notified, and that industrial safety has provided detailed information about the substances at the company

[585] The firefighting efforts at the scene are led by the local fire chief, who receives assistance from other fire and rescue services, the Civil Defense, industrial protection and private individuals

[586] Within a short time, several hundred people participate in the extinguishing work

[587] The fire chief realizes that the efforts will not be sufficient, and calls the 110 emergency center and requests assistance from a forest fire helicopter

[588] The 110 center contacts HRS, which coordinates the use of forest fire helicopters on behalf of DSB

[589] The main rescue center has followed the development closely, but has delegated the coordination of the efforts to the LRS, which is usually done for land rescue operations

[590] Now HRS ensures that the forest fire helicopter gets into the air in a short time

[591] In parallel with the forest fire helicopter taking off, the person on duty in the forest fire management support scheme contacts the local fire chief to follow up on the forest fire helicopter assistance

[592] On this day, a fire chief from the Midt-Hedmark Fire and Rescue Service is on duty in the management support scheme, on assignment from DSB

[593] The crisis support unit in the Ministry of Justice and Public Security is monitoring the situation

[594] The Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness leads the handling at a central level, and coordinates with the other ministries

[595] Updated reports from the firefighting efforts and news from the media are compiled and continuously presented to the Minister of Justice and Emergency Preparedness

[596] The Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness calls a meeting of the Crisis Council, where various scenarios are discussed, particularly with regard to possible extensive and dangerous gas emissions

[597] The situation reports from the field show that the right resources have been involved by LRS

[601] Such incidents may be triggered by nature, be the result of technical or human errors or deliberate actions – State security

[602] To safeguard the existence, sovereignty and integrity of the state, as well as to ensure political freedom of action

[603] The capacity and intention of an actor or actors (state, group, individual) to carry out intentional, undesirable actions

[604] Conditions that can lead to unintended adverse events – Vulnerability

[605] Inability to resist an intended unwanted action or unwanted event, as well as the inability to resume functioning

[606] A product of the probability of an event occurring and the consequence if it occurs

[607] An undesirable situation with a high degree of uncertainty and potentially unacceptable consequences for the individuals, organizations or states affected – Crisis management

[608] The sum of measures taken when a crisis has occurred, to limit the damage and bring the crisis to an end – Prevention

[609] Measures to reduce the possibility of an undesirable event, or to reduce the consequences of a possible event in advance – Emergency preparedness

[610] Planned and prepared measures that enable us to handle undesirable events so that the consequences are as minimal as possible – Critical functions for society

[611] Functions whose loss would threaten the basic needs of the population and society – Critical infrastructure

[612] Facilities and systems that are necessary to maintain or restore society's critical functions For prevention and emergency preparedness, an adverse event covers both an intentional, undesirable action and an unintentional, undesirable event

[628] Risk in a safe society Living with risk

[629] The work on societal security is about more than identifying and assessing risk, preventing and handling unwanted incidents

[630] It is also about what kind of society we want to develop and live in

[631] For example, we want to prevent serious crime, but we do not want a society based on pervasive surveillance of public or private spaces

[632] We want to prevent pandemics that can spread more quickly due to increased travel, but we do not want to restrict people's right to travel

[633] The dilemmas are there, and they often cannot be removed

[634] In a developing society, we must constantly consider the dilemmas we face in our work with societal security, and how they should be handled

[635] The government will work towards a safe society

[636] At the same time, there is a limit to security measures, and risk must be accepted to a certain extent

[637] Uncertainty and risk

[638] The work on societal security involves managing uncertainty

[639] It can be challenging to assess which incidents will occur and how serious they will be

[640] There will be uncertainties in the assessments we carry out, for example in the figures used or in our understanding of which factors can trigger a particular event

[641] Events can occur that are completely surprising based on the knowledge one has at the time of the event, but which can still be explained in retrospect

[642] It is probable that the improbable will happen, stated Aristotle (384–322 BC

[643] The statement holds up just as well today

[644] Today, such surprising events are often referred to as "black swans", see box 4.1. Investing in social security means investing in something with uncertain returns

[645] The benefit of public safety work lies in our ability to prevent an incident, or to handle an incident better and reduce the damage it causes

[646] But we will not be able to prevent all events – “black swans” will occur

[647] This does not mean that the work on social security has failed

[648] It may have prevented other incidents, reduced the scope of the incident, or improved our ability to handle the incident

[649] To identify, assess, prevent and manage

[650] Risk is a central part of the work on social security

[651] Risk can be defined as "a product of the probability of an event occurring and the consequence if it occurs

[652] The development picture as presented in chapters 5 to 10 shows a wide range of potential threats and risks, from accidents via natural events to incidents that are the result of an intentional act, such as terrorism

[653] Demanding trade-offs

[654] Society faces many different threats and risks

[655] Considerable resources can be spent on “Black Swans”

[656] In 1696, a Dutch expedition to Australia discovered black swans on a river where the city of Perth is located today

[657] The observation came as a complete surprise because black swans had not been seen in Europe before, and were therefore convinced that they did not exist

[658] In retrospect, the term “black swans” has been used to describe major events that come as a complete surprise

[659] In 2007, the term was introduced by the risk analyst

[660] He used it to describe events that are characterized by: – they lie outside what is considered possible and therefore occur completely unexpectedly – ​​they have extreme consequences – despite the fact that such events lie outside what is considered possible, it is believed that they can be explained in retrospect and that they could have been predicted based on knowledge that was available at the time of the event, but the significance of which was not realized Taleb, N. N
