[664] St. 10 Risks in a safe society identify and assess these, and to prevent and manage possible incidents

[665] There are, however, limits to how far work on social security can and should be extended

[666] It is neither desirable nor practically possible to eliminate all risk and create a 100 percent safe society

[667] Work on social security must take place within the framework of fundamental democratic values

[668] Norway will continue to be an open and transparent society

[669] We must protect values such as self-determination, personal freedom, legal certainty and privacy

[670] Social security work must also be in line with the principles on which the Norwegian welfare state is built, and it must not undermine the Norwegian social contract

[671] Norway is, and will continue to be, a society built on trust between people, and with public institutions that deserve the trust of citizens

[672] Weighing the costs and benefits of measures is an essential part of the work on societal security

[673] Within the transport sector, for example, calculations are routinely made of how many lives can be saved by a given investment in improved road standards

[674] In areas prone to landslides, the costs of avalanche protection measures will be weighed against the value of the increased safety the measures provide

[675] Balancing cost against benefit can be challenging in the area of public safety, because the benefit can be difficult to determine

[676] The benefit is partly about how effectively the measure prevents an incident or reduces the consequences of the incident

[677] The benefit must also be assessed against how likely it is that the event will occur

[678] When it comes to intended undesirable acts, such as terrorism and armed conflict, the threat landscape can change rapidly

[679] however, the roofs must be planned over a long period of time

[680] When investments in security measures are to be assessed, the benefit must, as far as possible, be assessed in the usual way, that is, based on an assessment of cost-benefit compared to alternative uses of the funds

[681] Uncertainty about future developments, a possible long investment period and the fact that measures can also have a preventive effect, present particular challenges in assessing the cost-benefit of many security measures

[682] Such specific challenges must be taken into account when measures are assessed

[683] Measures may have effects that are difficult to assess in monetary terms

[684] Examples could be how they affect people's perception of safety, or citizens' trust in public authorities

[685] When costs and benefits are to be weighed against each other, we must take such effects into account

[686] In Kristiansand, the municipality and residents of the Posebyen area, an old wooden housing estate, have collaborated since 2006 to make the estate fire-safe through an automatic warning system

[687] It is challenging to assess in terms of money what value the increased security provides to residents in the area

[688] It is also not easy to appreciate the cultural value that protecting the City of Banks provides

[689] In addition, there are incidents that we spend significant resources on preventing and preparing to handle, even though it is very uncertain whether and when they will occur

[690] Terrorist attacks are the most prominent example

[691] It can pose a fundamental threat to individuals and institutions that may be affected, and to our open, democratic society

[692] Therefore, we prioritize spending significant resources on our ability to prevent and handle such incidents, even though statistically they occur far less frequently than a number of other types of incidents

[693] Box 4.2 The social contract The “social contract” is a term used to describe fundamental questions about the organization of a society and the legitimacy of authorities vis-à-vis the individual

[694] Trust between citizens, and between citizens and the authorities, is absolutely crucial for a social contract to be established and maintained

[695] The starting point for the idea of ​​a "social contract" is the recognition that people, faced with various challenges, are best equipped as a community

[696] This community takes the form of a state with elected authorities

[697] It is the population, i.e. the citizens as free individuals, who have the right to decide how the state will be governed and by whom the citizens will be governed

[698] Citizens enter into a “contract” with their elected leaders

[699] The contract gives all citizens rights, and it gives the leaders the right to impose duties on citizens, such as paying taxes

[700] Rights and obligations must be distributed fairly, and there must be equal treatment of all those covered by the social contract

[701] The social contract also implies that the state, under certain, specific conditions, can use necessary means to arrest and prosecute citizens, as well as maintain peace and order

[702] Parliament 2016–

[703] Risk in a safe society

[704] Some risks are there because we choose to live with them

[705] They are often linked to activities we want in society, most often because they can provide a profit

[706] For example, Norway supports an open, free and independent internet because it is good for communication, value creation and our prosperity

[707] However, it also means that we expose ourselves to risk, because the internet exposes ICT systems to digital attacks

[708] Measures to reduce digital vulnerability must therefore be weighed against how they can reduce the positive effects of access to and use of the internet

[709] Acceptable risk and residual risk

[710] Recognizing risk is a prerequisite for being able to prevent, reduce and manage it

[711] It involves more than observing that the risk exists

[712] It also requires considering the consequences it could have and how it should be handled. The absence of risk recognition can lead to failure to implement measures that should have been implemented

[713] Risk is the risk we accept to live with in a given situation

[714] A risk may be acceptable because it is small, i.e. either because there is little probability of the event occurring and/or because the consequences are small, or because we see it as expedient to take such a risk

[715] In addition, there are risks we must accept because we have no way to reduce them

[716] When assessing risk, the values that may be exposed to risk must be weighed against the economic and social costs of risk-reducing measures

[717] Securing public buildings is an example

[718] A wide range of security measures are possible here

[719] Video cameras can monitor the inside and outside of the building

[720] Roadblocks may restrict vehicle access to the building

[721] Security gates can provide control over employees and visitors entering and exiting the building

[722] Windows can be made bulletproof and strengthened so that they can withstand the pressure of a bomb

[723] But which of these security measures should be chosen

[724] Should they be selected based on the most extreme events imaginable, regardless of the probability of their occurrence

[725] What weight should the costs of protection have in the choice of measures

[726] And how much weight should we give to the desire for an open society where public buildings do not appear like fortresses

[727] Such questions cannot be answered solely based on a risk analysis

[728] Professional assessments of threat, risk and vulnerability levels, and of the assumed impact of risk-reducing measures, must be combined with value-based boundary drawing

[729] Dilemmas arise

[730] They are partly about professional assessments, but ultimately about political and value-based choices

[731] In some cases, we have limited ability to decide which risks we will accept

[732] In an open and free society like Norway, for example, there will always be vulnerabilities that individuals or groups of people can exploit to cause harm

[733] The terrorist attacks in Norway in July 2011, in Paris in November 2015 and in Nice in July 2016 are examples of this

[734] We can do a lot to avoid such incidents, but we will never be able to protect ourselves completely

[735] The limits of acceptability

[736] Risk is not constant

[737] They can vary from person to person, over time, between groups of people, and different types of events

[738] We know from research that we are more likely to accept risks that we are used to and that we can control ourselves, than risks that are unknown and over which we have little control

[739] Subjective perceptions of risk do not necessarily always coincide with more objective assessments

[740] Weighing different perceptions of risk against each other can be demanding

[741] The conclusion must nevertheless be that in our work on societal security, we must use resources to the greatest extent possible where the risk, based on our best estimates, is greatest

[742] When we decide which risk reduction measures to implement, we also decide which risks we will accept

[743] If the only security measure at a public building is access control through an entrance gate, this means that the building is not protected against the risks that the gate cannot reduce, such as a car bomb attack

[744] Thus, we indirectly accept these risks, because we do not protect ourselves against them

[745] There may be good reasons for this, for example because the threat of an attack is considered so small that it is not considered necessary to protect against this threat

[746] Such choices should be the result of conscious assessments of the risks one is exposed to, which of these are acceptable and which are not

[747] There should also be an awareness that prioritizing one security measure may in reality mean downgrading another measure for which one does not have the resources

[748] Decision-makers must make decisions based on sound risk assessments, and communicate risks clearly to relevant, affected actors

[749] This in itself can have a risk-reducing effect

[750] Rescue helicopters, for example, will have a limit on how far they can fly over the ocean before they have to return to Slovic, P

[751] The perception of risk

[752] Risks in a safe society

[753] The closer a ship is to this limit, the greater the risk that the crew cannot be rescued if the ship is in distress at sea

[754] Knowledge of this limit can be important for choosing a sailing route

[755] Actors who adopt risk-reducing measures should therefore carefully consider which other actors may need information about the measures

[756] Residual risk is the risk that remains when we cannot implement or are willing to prioritize additional risk-reducing measures

[757] A residual risk will always exist

[758] This is due, among other things, to financial limitations on which measures can be implemented, the balancing of risk-reducing measures against other considerations, and uncertainty in risk assessments

[759] Black swans" also contribute to the fact that there will always be risks that we cannot eliminate

[760] Assessment of acceptable risk should also include assessment of alternative uses of the resources that may be used for a risk-reducing measure

[761] If extensive measures are taken against a particular risk, this may reduce the resources available to implement measures against other risks

[762] Thus, measures in one area may weaken the possibility of measures in another area

[763] Resilient societies

[764] A society's ability to manage risk depends on more than public resources and efforts

[765] Contributions from private businesses, voluntary organizations, local communities and individuals are important

[766] A society rich in material, economic, human and organizational resources will have a greater overall ability to prevent and manage incidents, and it will be less vulnerable if a single resource is put out of action

[767] In the international debate on societal security, this is often referred to as resilience, see box

[768] Norway has good conditions for being a resilient society

[769] Building a safe and resilient society requires collaboration

[770] To promote ICT security and protect critical infrastructure, for example, the public sector will often depend on collaboration with private industry as developers and owners of the infrastructure

[771] Another example is the efforts that both voluntary organizations and individuals often contribute to managing and limiting the harmful effects of major floods

[772] Here, the ability to take responsibility and initiate measures, in combination with knowledge of local conditions, has often proven to be crucial in limiting harmful effects

[773] Society's resilience also depends on our ability to mobilize quickly in the event of incidents

[774] The faster we react, the less damage will normally be caused, and the faster society will be able to function normally

[775] The ability to respond quickly is influenced by the culture we have for taking responsibility and contributing to the community

[776] Norway is a society where the spirit of volunteerism is strong, and in many Norwegian communities, residents know each other well and are used to helping each other if something happens

[777] This helps to strengthen society's resilience

[778] Building society on values ​​such as openness and trust is important

[779] It lowers the barriers for local communities and individuals to take the initiative to handle incidents

[780] Such contributions have proven particularly important in the event of large, complex and unexpected events

[781] Then improvisation, collaboration, and the ability and willingness to contribute can be important for the overall handling of the incident

[782] As citizens and individuals, we have a responsibility for our own safety and a shared responsibility for the resilience of society

[783] This involves seeking knowledge about what risks we may be exposed to, how we can prevent and reduce them, and what we should do if an incident occurs

[784] Traveling in an area prone to landslides means exposing yourself to risk

[785] Even though the public contributes information about the avalanche danger level, it is ultimately up to the individual whether and how they choose to travel in such terrain

[786] Box 4.3 Resilience The concepts of resilience and resilient societies have received increasing international attention in recent years

[787] Resilience is used to describe a society's ability to withstand and handle major events, restore important functions after events have occurred, and, if necessary, adapt to changing conditions

[788] The discussion about resilience and resilient societies extends beyond public efforts

[789] The importance of strong local communities is central

[790] Strong local communities are important in handling incidents and rebuilding afterwards

[791] Resilience is also about residents' responsibility for their own safety and their ability to contribute when incidents occur

[792] Not least, there is concern about how the public sector can create conditions for everyone to take responsibility and contribute what they have to contribute

[822] St. 10 Risk in a safe society In some events, resilience will involve seeking to restore society to where it was before the event

[823] This means that the functions that are affected can be resumed as quickly as possible and that necessary replacements can be found for any damaged equipment

[824] In the event of larger and more demanding events, robustness could mean that society finds a new normal state in which it attempts to preserve important elements of what characterized society before the event, for example a free and open society

[825] At the same time, lessons can be learned and changes can be made as a result of the incident, for example through new security measures

[826] Knowledge and experiences from community safety work must be shared between public actors, with citizens, voluntary organizations, local communities and private businesses

[827] It will stimulate the confidence that society's resilience

[828] Community resilience cannot be established once and for all, and it is not constant

[829] It can vary geographically and over time

[830] One local community may have good experience in handling incidents and helping each other, while in another the tradition for this may be weaker

[831] Resilience can be increased through learning from exercises or events, and through awareness of the risks that surround us

[832] Resilience can decline if we are not aware of the risks surrounding us, or if our knowledge of incident management weakens

[833] The work of developing and strengthening society's resilience is therefore a continuous process

[839] Challenges and government policy

[843] It is crucial that those participating in crisis management can communicate effectively with each other

[844] This is especially important in the case of large and rare incidents, which can challenge the way rescue workers, emergency services and authorities usually work

[845] In such situations, particularly high demands are placed on both management and cross-functional cooperation to ensure coordination and an overall overview

[900] On June 10, 2015, the Storting adopted the local police reform

[901] As part of the reform, the number of police districts was reduced from 27 to 12 as of 1 January 2016. The overall goal of the reform is a local police force that is more operational, visible and accessible, and that has the capacity to prevent, investigate and prosecute criminal acts, and ensure the safety of citizens

[902] A more competent and effective local police force must be developed where the population lives

[903] At the same time, solid professional environments must be developed that are equipped to meet the crime challenges of today and tomorrow

[904] This overall objective of the reform is specified in six impact objectives

[905] A more accessible and present police force with good local roots and interaction

[906] A more unified police force that delivers more equal and better quality police services across the country

[907] A police force with more targeted efforts on prevention, investigation and emergency preparedness

[908] A police force with better competence and capacity, which shares knowledge and learns from experiences

[909] A police force that creates better results in a culture characterized by openness and trust, through good leadership and active employee engagement A police force that works more effectively by adopting better methods and new technology

[910] The government has proposed to allocate NOK 140 million specifically for the implementation of the community policing reform

[946] The Government will ensure that municipalities have professional and effective fire and rescue services, with good ability to handle larger and more demanding incidents

[947] The fire and rescue service is the municipalities' most important rescue and emergency response resource

[948] Today, there are just under 300 fire and rescue services, and it has long been considered a challenge that there are large variations between them

[949] It varies how they are organized, how good their professional environments are, and how good their ability is to prevent and handle fires and other incidents

[950] Investigations have determined that the education offered to fire and rescue personnel is inadequate

[951] To improve fire and rescue preparedness, the government is working to: – establish a new education model for fire and rescue personnel – facilitate a new organization of the fire and rescue service – ensure systematic and risk-based fire prevention work – assess new requirements in the regulations that are adapted to greater fire cooperation and a new education model

[967] Fire Chief Nils-Erik Haagenrud of the Midt-Hedmark Fire and Rescue Service IKS has handled a number of different critical situations over many years in service

[968] But there is one incident he remembers better than the others

[969] The Åsta accident is an incident of national importance that has affected the fire and rescue services in the region

[970] On January 4, 2000, the unthinkable happened in Osterdalen on the Roros Line

[971] – When the message came in to the 110 center about sparks and a possible fire on a train, all resources were sent to the scene

[972] Here we were met with something completely different than what we were prepared for

[973] Two trains had collided at high speed on the Røros Line in Åmot municipality, which had resulted in a fire in the train set with many fatalities and injuries, says Haagenrud

[974] Joy in tragedy The challenge for the emergency services upon arrival at the scene was to gain an overview of the extent of the accident, so that they could make the right priorities and, not least, have a strategy that could save as many lives as possible

[975] There were far too few resources and equipment at the start

[976] There were also problems with the communication, which made it problematic to provide time-critical information

[977] – There were people trapped in a crushed train carriage in flames, and it was very difficult to free the trapped people before the fire spread

[978] This resulted in us not being able to save all those trapped

[979] The joy in the tragedy was that after several hours of intense work, we managed to rescue a woman with minimal injuries from the crushed train car, says Haagenrud

[980] Gradually, more resources arrived at the scene of the accident and the cooperation between the actors worked very well

[981] – The incident has subsequently left its mark on my thinking about how the fire and rescue service should be organized, so that we can help those involved in an accident in the best possible way with the right user focus

[982] Haagenrud believes that developments are heading in the right direction with larger and more robust fire and rescue services, better expertise, better equipment and some regional solutions

[983] – We still have some way to go to put in place a robust organization, which will require larger expertise environments and regional solutions to be able to handle major incidents, says the fire chief

[1097] Rescue service

[1098] What is the rescue service

[1099] When an emergency occurs on land, at sea or by aircraft, the part of Norwegian civil protection called the rescue service is mobilized

[1100] The rescue service provides immediate efforts to save people from death or injury as a result of acute accidents or dangerous situations

[1101] The rescue service is not a single organization in the same way as, for example, the police or the Civil Defense

[1102] The rescue service is a term for a collaboration between various agencies and organizations, both public, voluntary and private

[1103] This cooperative is organized and financially supported by the state, and is developed to fulfill a function that no individual organization has the capacity to fulfill on its own

[1104] The rescue service is administratively coordinated by the Ministry of Justice and Public Security

[1105] Which actors are mobilized in each search and rescue operation depends on the type of incident and which resources are needed and available in the area

[1106] Operationally, rescue operations are led and coordinated by the country's two main rescue centers (HRS) and subordinate local rescue centers (LRS

[1107] one in each police district including Svalbard local rescue centers

[1108] HRS is located in Bodø, and in Sola outside Stavanger

[1109] Rescue from sea and air is organized, led and coordinated by HRS, while management and coordination of land rescue operations is generally delegated from HRS to LRS

[1110] The reduction in the number of police districts will lead to a corresponding reduction in the number of LRSs since the activities there generally take place from the police districts' operations centers

[1111] The operations centers in the new police districts will be put into operation according to a set progress plan

[1112] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security has established a transitional arrangement that means that the existing LRS will be maintained with the current composition until new LRSs can be established in the new police districts

[1114] Box 5.4 Interview with Øyvind Aadde

[1115] Øyvind Aadde

[1116] Photo: private Øyvind Aadde has been a rescue leader at the Central Rescue Center in Northern Norway for almost ten years

[1117] He also has extensive experience as a police officer, and has participated in two different UN missions – both as a police officer and as a soldier

[1118] What actually happens from the moment you receive an emergency message

[1119] – The very first thing we do is determine the severity

[1120] Usually, the content of the message itself will be sufficient in itself

[1121] In situations where this is not enough, weather information, contact with other units in the area, relatives or other sources can help us

[1122] We then need to find the exact position of the place where the incident took place

[1123] Perhaps the person in distress can provide sufficient information themselves, but tracking via the AIS system or mobile phone tracking can also be helpful

[1124] Here we have several technical aids, and we can also get assistance from our regular partners

[1125] Then we must clarify which resources are best suited to provide the right assistance

[1126] A resource can, for example, be anything from a small fishing boat to a vessel from the Coast Guard or the Rescue Service

[1127] Once the right resource has been designated, we assign tasks to the individual unit

[1128] This occurs either in the form of calling out our own resource, the Sea King rescue helicopter, or by requesting assistance from other units

[1129] Because the rescue service is organized as a collaboration between volunteers, professionals and private actors who make their resources available, we can use the entire “toolbox” of society when it really matters

[1130] The actual efforts in the incident are organized according to rehearsed plans adapted to the environment in which the incident takes place

[1131] “A very important part of our service is keeping track of available and relevant resources in our area of responsibility,” Øyvind explains

[1132] – We are completely dependent on knowledge of what resources the wider community can provide in order for us to be able to do the best possible job

[1133] Not least, we are dependent on legitimacy and trust from society at large

[1134] The public must be able to be confident that the rescue service has one purpose, namely to save lives

[1135] When our people arrive at a disaster site, they represent an organization that is founded on respect for human life and solidarity with those in need of help

[1136] The responsibility for investigation and accountability lies with other authorities

[1137] – Something that is perhaps special about our organization is that we regularly establish efforts that cross traditional boundaries between ministries, institutions and agencies

[1138] We draw resources from one, which we make available to the other

[1139] We offer overall coordination and management, and we take on administrative challenges afterwards

[1140] – It is important to highlight that we experience great goodwill from all organizations and agencies on a daily basis, says Øyvind

[1141] – Finally, I would like to point out the importance of exercises, concludes Øyvind

[1142] — We rehearse regularly with many actors at different levels

[1143] Both volunteers and professionals at home and abroad

[1144] This provides good knowledge of the actors in the different units with whom we will collaborate in real incidents

[1145] – A very important part of the training activities takes place in the handling of less serious incidents on a daily basis

[1146] It gives us local knowledge, routines for using and calling out resources and, not least

[1147] Knowledge of the people who will step in during the events where life is really at stake

[1148] Risk in a safe society

[1149] A clearer rescue service

[1150] A new organizational plan for the rescue service was adopted by the Cabinet on June 19, 2015, and entered into force on November

[1151] The starting point for the work on the new organizational plan was that the rescue service functions well

[1152] Therefore, the main features of the organizational plan for the rescue service in Norway from 1980 were continued

[1153] This means that the basic principles of collaboration, responsibility, integrated service and coordination have been established and continued

[1154] The new organizational plan establishes the rescue service's organization and routines for cooperation, management, coordination, responsibility and tasks

[1155] The aim is to maintain an integrated rescue service based on national volunteer work and collaboration between public, voluntary and private actors

[1156] Integrated rescue service means that it includes all types of rescue operations related to land, sea and air rescue services

[1157] There have been clearer lines of management, responsibility, notification and reporting in the rescue service

[1158] The police chiefs in South-West and Nordland respectively have been given an additional function as head of the main rescue centers and rescue management

[1159] The same applies to the police chiefs in the local rescue centers and the rescue management, that is, here too the function as head of the individual rescue center is in addition to the role as head of the police district

[1160] The main rescue centres have had their special driving responsibility for maintaining and further developing cooperation within the rescue service on a daily basis clarified

[1161] The rescue management at the main rescue centers in Sola and Bodø has gained several new members, both public and private actors

[1162] Adjustments have also been made to the composition of the rescue teams at the local rescue centers

[1163] This means that the rescue management has been given a composition that reflects the current need for collaboration between relevant actors

[1164] The rescue management's role in contributing to developing the collaborative rescue service between incidents has been specified in the new organizational plan

[1165] All agencies, businesses and voluntary organizations that have a role in the rescue service or in other emergency situations in peacetime should participate in formalized cooperation

[1166] Therefore, rescue and emergency preparedness councils must also be established in all police districts

[1171] Rescue helicopters are a very important resource for the rescue service

[1172] In December 2013, the government signed a contract with AgustaWestland (now Leonardo Helicopters) for the delivery of 16 new rescue helicopters

[1173] The contract also includes an option for an additional six helicopters, with associated spare parts and equipment, as well as training and training aids

[1174] The acquisition involves a significant improvement in rescue capacity in Norway, and is important for ensuring that Norway has a satisfactory rescue helicopter service

[1175] The new helicopters will replace the current twelve Sea King rescue helicopters that were acquired in the early 1970s

[1176] The helicopters' task in peacetime is to carry out search and rescue missions, air ambulance missions and other socially beneficial missions as quickly and safely as possible following orders from the main rescue centers

[1177] The new helicopters will have higher speed and significantly better range than the current Sea King, see

[1178] The cabin will be large and flexible, and can accommodate several people

[1179] The cabin is also better suited for medical treatment

[1180] Better navigation and search equipment will enable people to be tracked down faster and more efficiently

[1181] The helicopters will provide greater year-round safety for people in the Norwegian rescue area of ​​responsibility at sea, in impassable terrain and in situations where other resources are insufficient

[1182] The first new rescue helicopters have been completed and are undergoing extensive testing in the UK

[1183] The Norwegian Armed Forces will conduct testing and evaluation in 2017 and 2018 on the first helicopters

[1184] It must then be assessed whether the helicopter and equipment are functioning as intended or whether changes need to be made

[1185] The helicopters are scheduled to be put into service at the rescue helicopter bases in the period

[1186] The Sea King helicopters will be gradually phased out as the new helicopters take over the emergency response

[1223] Voluntary organizations – a pillar of preparedness and rescue

[1224] Norway is a long country with a dispersed population, and resources can often be far apart

[1225] It is therefore absolutely crucial that we have voluntary rescue and emergency response organizations that ensure the organization of the local commitment that exists around the country

[1226] Every day, ordinary people perform life-saving first aid and rescue people at sea, on land and in the mountains

[1227] When it comes to searching for missing persons, rescuing people from the terrain, and responding to avalanches, volunteers are the primary resource our society can rely on

[1228] This places great demands on the responsiveness, training, equipment and practice of the voluntary rescue organizations

[1229] Historically, the rescue service has always been based on neighbor helping neighbor when someone is in need

[1230] Today, it is the voluntary rescue organizations that largely manage this spirit of volunteerism

[1231] The volunteers also contribute a number of resources such as rescue boats, small aircraft, off-road vehicles, rescue dogs, etc

[1232] It is not without reason that voluntary organizations are often referred to as a pillar of the Norwegian rescue service

[1233] The Government will facilitate the continuation of voluntary rescue organizations as a central part of basic preparedness in Norway

[1234] The Government wishes to help voluntary organizations maintain and strengthen their position within Norwegian rescue preparedness

[1235] At the same time, there should be a clear distinction between public and voluntary resources so that we preserve the fundamental motivation of the individual when it comes to contributing to emergency preparedness work

[1236] The government believes that volunteering should primarily be built from the bottom up, and within organizations

[1237] However, it is important to have close contact between the voluntary organizations and public resources

[1238] There are high demands for competence and predictability, increasing demands for technology and a constant need for joint training

[1239] Among other things, it will be important to have a dialogue regarding the framework conditions for the voluntary rescue organizations

[1240] Such a dialogue will not only be limited to questions about subsidies from the public sector, but also measures that can strengthen the interaction between volunteers, the main rescue centers and the police, the health service and other actors in the rescue service

[1241] These may include matters related to training, exercises, overview of resources, notification procedures, operational implementation of rescue missions, learning from experience and financial matters

[1242] When new police districts are established, it is important, for example, to see

[1257] Vegard Standahl Olsen, volunteer rescuer at Norwegian People's Aid Tromsø, has 15 years of experience from search and rescue operations in Troms

[1259] – Troms county is hard hit by many avalanches every year

[1265] All of this requires time, often several hundred hours a year in practical emergency preparedness work

[1268] In today's time pressure, every minute the volunteers take becomes very important

[1269] The time and effort invested must go into continuous practice and training, because that is what provides the foundation for effective rescue in the field

[1326] Risk in a safe society planning system

[1327] The National Emergency Preparedness System (NBS) consists of the Civil Emergency Preparedness System (SBS) and the Defence Sector Emergency Preparedness System (BFF

[1328] Both are built according to the same structure as NATO's crisis management system

[1329] The scope of activity is cross-sectoral crises in peacetime caused by serious intentional incidents or threats thereof, and crises with a security policy dimension and armed conflict or threats thereof

[1330] Unintended events, such as natural disasters, pandemics, etc., do not fall within the scope of the operation and are handled in line with relevant civil emergency plans

[1331] Revised versions of both SBS and BFF were established by royal decree on 10 April 2015, and are rated Limited. The plan is subject to annual revisions

[1332] All ministries and subordinate agencies must prepare their own emergency preparedness plans based on the NBS

[1333] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security is responsible for coordinating SBS on the civilian side and providing guidelines for updating and publication, while the Ministry of Defence manages BFF

[1334] Competence-building measures have been implemented for ministries and subordinate agencies regarding NBS

[1335] The County Governor, who is responsible for coordinating underlying planning at the regional level, has also participated in this

[1336] The Directorate for Civil Protection and Emergency Preparedness revised its emergency plan

[1337] In 2015, the government adopted revised instructions for the county governor's work on social security, and has given clearer requirements for the county governor's work on social security and follow-up of municipalities than previously

[1338] The county governor's emergency plans must be revised annually, and the same applies to the overall emergency plan in the municipalities

[1339] Current regulations provide clear guidelines that emergency preparedness plans for the county governor and municipalities should be prepared on the basis of risk and vulnerability assessments that highlight local and regional emergency preparedness challenges

[1340] The police have their own emergency preparedness system that describes the police's responsibilities and roles, including work with public safety in general and handling acute unwanted incidents in particular

[1341] The police's planning includes unwanted and/or extraordinary incidents, particularly in the main areas of accidents, natural disasters and terrorist attacks

[1342] The plan is designed in line with overarching governing documents and legislation, and relates to both SBS and BFF in its structure

[1343] Follow-up of planning is an ongoing process

[1344] The local police reform involves coordinating plans from previous police districts with updated plans applicable to new police districts

[1345] The police have an electronic reference work where plans are published according to a uniform and recognizable structure

[1346] The database provides the opportunity for searches and postings across police districts, which leads to sharing of expertise and cooperation within planning and emergency preparedness work and which in turn raises the level of cooperation in the event of incidents that cross police districts

[1347] The Norwegian Police Directorate supports the work on planning for the new police districts by facilitating the electronic reference system, so that it facilitates their work in preparing new plans within the various main areas

[1348] The Norwegian Police Directorate will begin work to assess and, if necessary, revise the planning assumptions for the police's planning work in 2017, which take into account the changes brought about by the Community Policing Reform

[1349] Furthermore, there are a number of more scenario-specific plans where an incident could cause consequences that involve actors across ministries and agencies

[1350] Examples of such planning may include national plans for pandemic influenza, nuclear preparedness or acute pollution

[1416] Need for long-term planning within emergency and preparedness communications

[1417] The Government is responsible for ensuring that emergency and preparedness actors have access to good and secure communication solutions in their daily work and in crises

[1418] With Nødnett, emergency and preparedness actors have a satisfactory solution for secure voice communication and for some data transfer

[1419] For high-speed data, emergency and preparedness actors must currently use commercial networks, because the data capacity in Nødnett is limited

[1420] The development of the threat landscape, technological developments and changing working methods give reason to believe that emergency and preparedness actors' need for secure mobile communication solutions will increase in the coming years

[1421] To meet society's need for communication solutions for emergency and preparedness purposes, work must be cross-sectoral, strategic and long-term

[1422] Emergency networks must be kept up to date so that users can trust the system

[1423] Due to rapid technological development, changing user needs and processes related to frequency management that follow set time frames, it is important to plan for the future

[1424] The use of computer communication, such as images, maps and video, can contribute to better and more efficient task solving

[1425] and emergency response actors' need for communication tools that they can rely on in every context, including for data, may require new solutions

[1426] One can imagine the state establishing a completely new infrastructure reserved for critical societal functions

[1427] An alternative is to upgrade commercial mobile networks to meet the needs of emergency services

[1428] A combination of the two is also a possibility

[1429] Regardless of whether and how one chooses to develop the area of emergency communications, the state must still take responsibility for providing satisfactory frameworks and services for this purpose

[1430] Solutions for secure and robust mobile broadband services for emergency and preparedness purposes will require significant involvement, resources and expertise from the government

[1431] This applies regardless of whether the needs are to be met over the commercial mobile networks, through a dedicated network or through a combination solution

[1452] Risk in a safe society 5.7 Crisis communication – the population must know what is happening In the event of extraordinary events, the population will have an acute need for information

[1453] People are wondering what is happening, what the authorities are doing, and how they should respond

[1454] The government is concerned with good crisis communication

[1455] If many people in society are experiencing unrest or fear, effective communication will be of great importance

[1456] If large parts of the population are reached with a preventive message, it will also strengthen the individual's preparedness

[1457] During an incident, communication from the authorities must be coordinated

[1458] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security annually updates a joint plan for how the ministries will coordinate their crisis communication

[1459] Work is also underway to achieve better coordination of crisis communication at directorate and agency level

[1460] The work on better coordination of communication during crises has been, and is, a priority task for the government

[1461] DSB will facilitate the strengthening of the authorities' ability to handle communication challenges in crises

[1462] Among other things, a joint arena for communication managers at directorates, regional and local authorities was established in the autumn of

[1463] Such an arena can provide increased expertise to the individual authority

[1464] It can also strengthen cooperation between sectors and authorities during crises

[1465] This will also provide valuable expertise to many businesses that initially have few specific resources for crisis communication

[1466] A prerequisite for successful crisis communication is that the authorities and others are well prepared and that they have sufficient expertise and capacity

[1467] Practice is essential to becoming good at crisis communication

[1468] The government has strengthened its work with exercises at a central level in the ministries

[1469] Crisis communication is an integral part of large and small exercises, both at the central level of government, and at the regional and local levels

[1470] Increasingly, so-called discussion exercises are also being conducted specifically aimed at communication managers

[1471] It is a characteristic of today's society that citizens have continuous access to information from a wide range of sources, including social media

[1472] The quality of this information is variable

[1473] Clear, accessible, open and accountable information from the authorities to the population is therefore more important than ever

[1474] At the same time, it is no longer the case that the public is informed only through established news media

[1475] There are many examples of various businesses using SMS notifications in their communication with citizens, for example, several water utilities have used SMS to notify affected residents of poor water quality

[1476] Social media is also becoming increasingly important for staying in touch with citizens during a crisis

[1477] All ministries are present on Facebook, and many are on Twitter, Instagram and several other platforms

[1478] The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, for example, used Twitter to communicate about the unclear situation in Turkey after the coup attempt in July

[1479] All police districts in Norway have had success using Twitter to inform residents about various ongoing events

[1480] It is crucial that communication is constantly adapted and developed in line with societal and technological developments

[1481] More and more people are searching for information online and making their own assessments

[1482] In communication between public emergency response actors and the public, it is therefore important to make information from the public sector easily accessible, so that individuals can decide for themselves how to act in a given situation

[1488] Risks in a safe society Digital vulnerabilities and ICT security

[1489] Norway is one of the world's most digitalized countries

[1490] The benefits of ICT are significant for society as a whole, and digital development is a crucial part of our value creation and growth

[1491] Increased digitalization is not a choice; it is a prerequisite for a modern society

[1492] To ensure efficiency through increased digitalization of Norwegian society, ICT solutions and digital services must be sufficiently secure and reliable

[1493] Businesses and individuals must have confidence that systems and networks function as they should and protect the privacy of individuals

[1494] Good ICT security is a prerequisite for achieving this trust

[1495] In addition, we must have sufficient national capacity to detect and handle digital attacks

[1496] ICT security encompasses both technical and administrative security measures, and involves the protection of both ICT systems and the information contained therein

[1497] ICT security is therefore about protecting “everything” that is vulnerable because it is connected to, or otherwise dependent on, information and communication technology

[1498] The term ICT security is used in this message synonymously with the term cybersecurity

[1499] This chapter deals with ICT security and digital vulnerabilities in society

[1500] Preventive safety under the Safety Act is discussed separately in Chapter

[1501] The Internet is becoming an increasingly important part of everyday life for most Norwegians, both at home and at work

[1502] The number of services offered and the number of devices connected to the internet is increasing sharply

[1503] The ability of society and businesses to exploit the opportunities offered by the internet will be an important part of future value creation

[1504] There is a clear trend that public agencies are increasingly using the internet for critical services

[1505] For example, the introduction of smart electricity meters will provide consumers with better information about electricity consumption and prices, as well as facilitate useful additional services

[1506] At the same time, the introduction will make the power system more exposed to software errors and internet-related threats

[1507] In many areas, digitalization has contributed to a safer and more secure society

[1508] People can more easily get in touch with each other and get quick access to information

[1509] Modern communication solutions enable better cooperation between emergency services, making rescue operations more efficient

[1510] Satellite-based services give us completely new opportunities to monitor unstable mountain masses

[1511] Digitalization has changed society's risk picture

[1512] No sector, and few countries, can currently control their digital vulnerability alone

[1513] For example, failures in telecommunications networks can lead to road tunnels having to be closed and doctors not being able to access patient records

[1514] In addition, many ICT services are operated across national borders

[1515] A large proportion of unwanted incidents affecting ICT systems are unintentional

[1516] Errors and failures in ICT systems can occur due to human error, software errors, equipment failures, as a result of natural events, or a combination of these

[1517] Human errors can often be related to inadequate competence and understanding of networks and systems, inadequate security culture or poor internal controls

[1518] Intentional adverse events are a growing problem

[1519] These are threats that can be challenging to map, but which can ultimately pose a threat to important Norwegian interests

[1520] The goal of the attackers may be to commit crimes, destroy or alter information or functionality

[1521] It may also involve obtaining information about state and trade secrets, research results or technological innovations from commercial companies

[1522] Cybercrime and ICT crime occur daily

[1523] Criminals go where there is value to be gained, the issues are often global and the risk of punishment and consequences is low

[1524] From a state and societal security perspective, the greatest threat is those actors who See, for example

[1529] In this category we find, among other things, state actors, especially other countries' security and intelligence services

[1530] These actors place great emphasis on secrecy, seek out our weakest points, and their activities can be difficult to detect

[1531] New technology has created major changes in how the population manages information

[1532] Information about ourselves, our communication, social circle, travel habits, etc. is being registered more often, cross-linked, and the volume is increasing

[1533] This challenges our ability to protect information

[1534] This also challenges privacy

[1535] ICT security is a prerequisite for good privacy protection

[1536] The need to increase the population's awareness of security threats and increase our user competence is becoming increasingly relevant

[1551] Around 225,000 customers were affected

[1552] The reason was that an actor illegally gained access to the regional power distribution company's computers and control systems

[1553] Analyses of the attack show that email addresses of employees at power plants/distribution centers were first mapped

[1554] Then emails containing malware were sent

[1555] Some recipients activated malware that eventually gave the attacker further access to the control systems

[1556] This took a long time (about half a year

[1558] It was a major job to get the system working again

[1561] This is to assess whether something similar could have happened to the Norwegian power grid

[1602] Responsibility for ICT security

[1603] Roles and responsibilities within ICT security are regulated by a number of laws and regulations

[1604] ICT security is primarily a corporate responsibility

[1605] Business managers are responsible for conducting risk assessments and, based on this, implementing adequate measures

[1606] In addition, each individual minister has overall responsibility for ensuring ICT security in their own sector

[1607] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security has coordination responsibility for preventive ICT security in the civilian sector

[1608] The Ministry also has responsibility for ICT security, which falls under the Civil Security Act, and a general coordination responsibility for society's civil security

[1609] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security hereby has coordination responsibility for ICT security in the civilian sector, both within and outside the Security Act

[1610] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security has the national responsibility for formulating the government's policy for ICT security in the civilian sector, including establishing national requirements and recommendations in the area of ​​ICT security for both public and private enterprises

[1611] Requirements must, to the necessary extent, be based on law and regulations

[1612] Relevant ministries, authorities and the business community will be involved in this work

[1613] The Ministry of Defence is responsible for ICT security in the defence sector

[1614] The Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness shall involve the Ministry of Defence in matters within civil ICT security that affect ICT security in the defence sector, and together with the Ministry of Defence, contribute to ensuring that civil-military challenges and needs are seen in context

[1615] NSM is the national expert community within ICT security, and is the national alert and coordination body for serious computer attacks against critical infrastructure or other important societal functions

[1616] NSM is subordinate to the Department of Defence

[1617] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security has the authority to instruct the NSM in matters within the Ministry of Justice and Public Security's area of ​​responsibility

[1618] The Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation is responsible for coordinating the government's ICT policy

[1619] The Ministry also has a special responsibility to work towards a strengthened and more holistic approach to ICT security in the state administration

[1620] The digitalization work in the state administration, and in the public sector as a whole, must adhere to the guidelines that follow from the national ICT security policy

[1621] The Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation shall, in consultation with the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, facilitate the digitalisation of public administration and society in general in a responsible manner

[1622] The Directorate for Administration and ICT (Difi) supports the Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation in their work to ensure that the digitalisation of the public sector meets the necessary requirements for ICT security

[1623] The Ministry of Transport and Communications is responsible for ICT security related to electronic communications networks and services, including the Internet

[1624] As a government agency under the Ministry of Transport and Communications, Nkom has a special responsibility related to security and preparedness in electronic communications networks and services

[1625] The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has overall responsibility for Norwegian foreign and security policy, including coordinating Norway's efforts and positions in international arenas where global challenges in the digital space are discussed

[1626] The Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness, together with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, will contribute to ensuring that international work in the area of ​​ICT security is handled well across ministerial areas in the civil sector

[1627] All ministries in the civil sector are responsible for following up on requirements and recommendations given by the Ministry of Justice and Public Security for their own activities and in their own sector

[1628] The ministries must involve

[1629] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security in processes where ICT security considerations are of national importance, especially in the event of major technological and structural changes in society

[1630] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security has a central role in further developing civilian authorities' work with ICT security and the use of instruments

[1631] Transfer of coordination responsibility for preventive ICT security from the Ministry of Innovation, Administration and Church Affairs to the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness

[1632] Distribution of responsibility for preventive security services and the National Security Authority. Royal Resolution

[1633] Instructions for the ministries' work on civil security and emergency preparedness, the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness' coordination role, supervisory function and central crisis management

[1636] Appropriate and secure lines of communication for both public and private enterprises are a key issue, including in digital incident management

[1640] Preventive ICT security work

[1641] There is a need for a holistic and systematic approach to work on preventive ICT security

[1642] The work must be adapted to the different needs of the public sector, the business sector and the individual citizen

[1643] The Government will work towards better coordination and a common understanding of the situation

[1644] Norwegian businesses must comply with various regulations regarding ICT security

[1645] Some regulations are sector-specific, while others are cross-sectoral

[1646] The different organizations have different purposes and considerations, and often use different concepts and methods

[1647] The Security Act provides, among other things, provisions for the handling of information that must be protected for reasons of national security

[1648] However, there is a great deal of information in unclassified systems that can also be sensitive and important to society, in addition to the fact that the unclassified ICT systems themselves can be important

[1649] The Security Committee had as part of its mandate to identify any need for harmonization of legal regulation within the ICT security field

[1650] The committee was also to consider issues related to the protection of information in unclassified ICT systems

[1651] The committee submitted its recommendation in the autumn of 2016, see chapter

[1652] In 2013, the European Commission launched the EU Cybersecurity Strategy

[1653] As one of several measures to achieve the goals of the strategy, the European Commission launched a proposal for a directive on measures for a common level of security of network and information systems in the EU (NIS Directive

[1654] The directive was adopted in the EU on July

[1655] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security is responsible for coordinating the follow-up of the NIS Directive in Norway, see box

[1656] Legislation regarding the protection of personal data within the EU/EEA is being strengthened

[1657] The EU's current data protection directive, which is implemented in the Norwegian Personal Data Act, is being replaced by a regulation on the processing of personal data

[1658] The regulation is EEA relevant and must be implemented in Norwegian law

[1659] It is planned that the regulations will be implemented in Norway

[1660] This could lead to changes in Norwegian regulations that contain specific requirements for information security when processing personal data

[1661] For example, the regulation introduces an obligation, under specific conditions, to notify the supervisory authority within 72 hours of a breach of ICT security

[1662] This applies where the breach leads to the destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure of or access to personal data

[1663] The Government will consider establishing a national framework that provides uniform and cross-sectoral regulation within the ICT security area

[1664] The work will be seen in the context of the EU's NIS Directive, and assessments from the Security Committee

[1665] This concerns a set of regulations outside the scope of the Security Act

[1666] The Lysne Committee points out in its report that the requirements for ICT security in the public sector are often function-based and have defined overall goals

[1667] The committee recommends that the Justice and Emergency Preparedness Act be amended by the Storting in June

[1674] Risk in a safe society

[1675] The Ministry has a strategic approach to how they can contribute to standardization work

[1676] Using security standards can streamline work on ICT security

[1677] It provides a framework and guidelines to work by for businesses that are within best practice

[1678] In addition, it facilitates common terminology, which in turn helps to simplify collaboration across sectors

[1679] At the same time, it provides authorities with a tool for assessing the safety of businesses

[1680] Difi recommends that central government use ISO27001 and ISO27002 when establishing an information security management system

[1681] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security wants Norway to be present in international arenas where standards within ICT security are developed

[1682] The Ministry has therefore provided grants to Standard Norway to strengthen this work

[1683] New national strategy for ICT security

[1684] A leading document for work on ICT security is the National Strategy for Information Security

[1685] The strategy was adopted

[1686] The national strategy sets priorities for the authorities' work and is supported by an action plan that describes how the priorities will be followed up

[1687] Recently, goals have also been set for work on ICT security in Meld

[1688] St. 27 (2015–2016) Digital agenda for Norway, in Prop

[1689] S (2015–2016) Combat power and sustainability, as well as in the Action Plan for Information Security in the Central Government (2015–

[1690] A lot has changed

[1691] The spread of new technologies (for example, cloud services), changing user habits, the importance of the "Internet of Things" and the digitalization of society are creating changing security needs

[1692] At the same time, the threat and risk picture has changed

[1693] Society's increased dependence on the internet provides greater opportunities for successful digital attacks

[1694] Authorities in different countries are establishing different strategic frameworks to manage this development

[1695] The strategies often have different structures and use different definitions

[1696] Despite this, there are still three areas that remain

[1697] The first is private-public partnership

[1698] Both infrastructure and services in the digital domain are largely developed and managed by the private sector

[1699] This can have many positive aspects, including for safety

[1700] Innovation, investment capacity and flexibility are factors that make private enterprises well suited to addressing ICT security concerns

[1701] At the same time, public enterprises manage important information and shape national policy

[1702] It is important for the public and private sectors to be able to collaborate and share information

[1703] An example is the Ekomsikkerhetsforum where private ekomsikkerhet providers and security authorities share relevant information

[1704] Another example is that in 2017, NSM will develop an arena for the transfer of experience between private and public enterprises related to advice and guidance in the area of ICT security

[1705] The other common denominator is international cooperation

[1706] Most countries point out that ICT security-related problems cannot be solved by the individual state alone

[1707] However, international cooperation is often difficult

[1708] One reason for this is that the area is close to security policy

[1709] Sharing information between nations must be balanced against the need for confidentiality

[1710] The third common denominator is that many nations place high value on fundamental values such as privacy, freedom of expression and the free flow of information

[1711] These values ​​are important underlying premises in the strategies

[1712] The government will prepare a new national strategy for ICT security

[1713] The strategy shall state the government's goals and strategic priorities within ICT security

[1714] In addition, an action plan with specific measures must be prepared

[1715] The Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness and the Ministry of Defense will lead the work

[1716] Relevant ministries, agencies and authorities shall be included in the development of the strategy and specific measures therein

[1717] Stakeholders in academia and the private sector will also be involved in the work

[1718] To the extent that measures require expenditure increases above the state budget, the government will return to this in connection with the annual budget proposals

[1719] Supervision in the area of ​​ICT security

[1720] Several government inspectorates are tasked with evaluating the state of ICT security in businesses

[1721] Most of these are sector-specific and, within the framework of their supervisory authority, check that the businesses have a management system or an internal control system in place

[1722] Good sector knowledge is in many cases necessary to be able to carry out targeted and effective supervision of ICT security

[1723] ICT security and the emphasis on risks associated with ICT can be a professional challenge in several sectors and for some sectoral supervisors

[1724] Several of the supervisory authorities need to build up additional expertise in order to be able to conduct full-fledged supervision and provide good guidance on ICT security in their sector

[1725] This will take time

[1726] At the same time, it is unclear whether there is sufficient expertise for all supervisory bodies to build their own ICT security environments

[1727] Risk in a safe society

[1728] In 2017, NSM will work to establish a common arena where sector supervisors can coordinate planned supervisory activities and exchange experiences within ICT security

[1729] As part of the work, NSM, together with the sector supervisors, will consider establishing a central capacity with ICT security expertise to be used as a resource for the supervisory authorities

[1730] This central capacity can consist of people from the supervisory authorities, and it can also be assessed whether there are commercial offers that can remedy any lack of competence

[1731] The Government will strengthen NSM's ability to supervise technical ICT security measures within the framework of the Security Act

[1732] NSM will also further develop methodologies and tools for its ICT security inspections

[1733] ICT security in government administration

[1734] Digital communication should be the main rule for communication within and with the administration

[1735] The population, the business community and the administration itself must have confidence that digital services in the government sector are secure and reliable

[1736] For example, several government registers are used as the basis for services provided by commercial enterprises

[1737] Risk management is at the core of all work on ICT security in government administration

[1738] Government agencies must have a good understanding of risk and work systematically with risk assessments

[1739] ICT security should be part of any digitalization project in government administration from the start, and throughout the system's life cycle

[1740] ICT security should also be part of business management, and a topic that employees, based on their role, should have knowledge of

[1750] Society's overall ability to detect and handle digital attacks

[1751] Intentional unwanted actions against ICT infrastructure include everything from youth pranks to advanced targeted attacks from other states

[1752] Attackers have different motives for their actions, and the methods used vary

[1753] To be well-equipped against a major digital attack, roles and responsibilities between actors must be clarified, businesses must have sufficient expertise and capacity, and they must be able to collaborate

[1754] Uncovering digital attacks

[1755] The ability to detect digital attacks depends on interaction between authorities, sector communities, and public and private enterprises, as well as between military and civilian actors

[1756] NSM is responsible for organizing and operating a national digital infrastructure (VDI) alert system

[1757] VDI is a network of sensors located at both public and private enterprises that own critical infrastructure

[1758] VDI is currently one of the most important tools Norwegian authorities have for detecting digital attacks against Norwegian critical infrastructure

[1759] The ability to detect attacks through VDI is improved through the exchange of information with national and international partners

[1760] The development of new detection technologies is ongoing in order to meet changes in the threat and risk landscape, particularly related to the capabilities of threat actors

[1761] The government proposed in Prop

[1762] S (2015–2016) Combat power and sustainability, that NSM in the long term will improve its ability to detect and analyze serious digital attacks, including by upgrading the sensor technology in VDI

[1763] Participation fees from private businesses are included as part of the financing of VDI

[1764] Affiliation with VDI is based on voluntary participation and is offered after a detailed assessment of the business's importance to critical infrastructure

[1765] It is therefore not a given that VDI sensors are deployed where they are most needed

[1766] The Government will therefore investigate future financing solutions for VDI

[2019] Challenges and government policy Norway's landscape and climate influence how we build and live

[2020] Throughout history, nature has produced dramatic events such as the Gauldalsskredet in 1345 with approximately 500 fatalities, and the quicksand landslide in Verdal in 1893 with 116 fatalities

[2021] Since 1900, more than 1,200 lives have been lost in avalanche accidents in Norway; about 700 of these as a result of avalanches

[2022] Most recently, in November 2016, three people died in a quicksand landslide in Sorum

[2023] Internationally, some natural events have also made a lasting impression on us over the past few decades

[2024] Among them is the tsunami in Southeast Asia in 2004, which took about 230,000 lives, of which 84 were Norwegians

[2025] Serious natural events are events that are triggered in nature and that pose a danger to human life and health or significant material assets

[2026] Serious natural events can also be triggered by humans, as we see, for example, with forest fires, where nine out of ten forest fires are caused by humans

[2027] In Norway, we are particularly exposed to storms, storm surges, floods, and landslides

[2028] Storms are the natural event that causes the greatest economic costs in Norway

[2029] Both storms and floods often affect large areas and many people

[2030] Different types of landslides cause the most injuries and deaths

[2031] The fewest natural events in Norway take human lives

[2032] However, every year natural events cause large amounts of damage

[2033] Homes, workplaces and infrastructure are destroyed

[2034] Of the specific incidents in recent years, the most notable is storm Dagmar in December 2011, where 570.000 people lost power, and 35,000 were without power for over 24 hours

[2035] In addition, the storm led to the loss of internet and telephony for many thousands of customers

[2036] Dagmar also created major problems with closed roads, ferry connections and railway lines

[2037] Natural damage compensation from insurance companies related to storms, storm surges, floods and landslides amounted to approximately ten billion kroner in the period 2000 to

[2038] However, this figure does not give a complete picture of the costs

[2039] In addition, there are payments through other insurance schemes, such as business interruption losses, as well as costs for crisis management, clean-up and repair of damage to public infrastructure

[2040] For example, natural damage insurance payments amounted to NOK 410 million after the flood in Eastern Norway in 2013, while it has been estimated that the flood caused overall material losses, including damage to infrastructure, of more than NOK 1.1 billion

[2041] In addition to the purely economic costs, there are the socio-economic costs resulting from closed roads, power outages, loss of electronic communications (e-com), lost employment

[2042] Such costs are more difficult to calculate

[2043] As society's dependence on electricity and e-com increases, the vulnerability to outages also increases, see Chapter 6 on digital vulnerabilities and ICT security

[2044] Natural events can also lead to other potentially dangerous secondary events

[2045] The most serious example of this is Fukushima in 2011, where a nuclear power plant was flooded by water after a tsunami, causing an uncontrolled nuclear accident

[2046] Storm Katrina in the USA in 2005 is another example, where the flooding caused large and serious chemical releases

[2047] In addition to the economic and environmental consequences, natural events can cause concern and unrest

[2048] Losing one's home or livelihood is a personal tragedy for those affected

[2049] Uncertainty about flood and avalanche risks can have negative health effects as a result of anxiety and insecurity

[2050] Population growth, climate change, economic growth and greater dependence between different societal functions are contributing to the growing potential for damage from natural events

[2055] The Government will: – contribute to ensuring that municipalities’ work on social security in social and spatial planning is of high quality in order to reduce the consequences of serious natural events, including by completing a national digital elevation and terrain model – improve society’s ability to manage flood and landslide risk – make it easier for municipalities to safeguard social security and climate change in their long-term planning, by contributing guidance and research-based knowledge – expand the natural damage insurance scheme to include land costs – contribute actively to the EU and UN’s work on social security and follow up on the UN’s Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030 programme

[2056] Planning that strengthens public safety 7.2.1 The Planning and Building Act as a key instrument Proper spatial planning and public planning are fundamental for better prevention related to serious natural events

[2057] Such planning is an effective means of preventing damage from floods, storm surges, landslides and stormwater

[2058] Good spatial and community planning should therefore be prioritized

[2059] The Planning and Building Act is the central tool for ensuring good planning

[2060] The law requires municipalities to “prevent the risk of loss of life, damage to health, the environment and important infrastructure, material assets, etc.”, and to ensure that risk and vulnerability analyses (ROS) are carried out when preparing development plans

[2061] Municipalities shall, where necessary, establish consideration zones that place restrictions on the use of areas that represent danger, risk or vulnerability

[2062] Planning must, among other things, take into account the vulnerability of critical societal functions

[2063] Where it is not possible to avoid building in hazardous areas, measures must be implemented to ensure sufficient safety

[2064] In Norway, precipitation has increased by about 20 percent over the last 100 years, and the strongest increase has occurred in the last 30 years

[2065] The temperature has been steadily warmer

[2066] than normal since 1985 until today, with a tendency for continued warming

[2067] In Norway, it is expected that in the years ahead there will be more intense and frequent torrential rain episodes, larger and more frequent floods, and that sea levels will rise

[2068] Climate change also poses a very complex and unclear risk globally

[2069] It may be a "risk amplifier" that has indirect consequences for societal security in Norway

[2070] For example, melting the ice opens up new shipping routes between Northeast Asia and Europe, but also represents a risk for Norway as a coastal nation

[2071] Climate change could globally affect food production and access to clean drinking water

[2072] Sea level rise can threaten low-lying areas and small island states

[2073] These effects of climate change will help to intensify the challenges countries already face, and will particularly affect the least developed countries

[2074] Climate change could lead to more natural disasters, more outbreaks of infectious diseases and increased competition for water, food and land

[2075] This in turn can contribute to instability and conflicts in regions where there are already major challenges, such as in the Middle East and North Africa
