[2278] Today's compensation and support schemes

[2279] There are currently three schemes for compensation after natural disasters, and one scheme for assistance with security measures

[2280] Private fire insurance that covers natural damage (natural damage insurance scheme) – All buildings and movable property that are insured against fire damage are automatically also insured against natural damage

[2281] This follows from the Natural Disaster Insurance Act

[2282] In addition to the ordinary insurance premium, a premium is calculated for natural damage

[2283] The natural disaster premium is currently 0.07 per thousand of the fire insurance sum

[2284] The natural disaster premium is set aside and used to pay compensation for natural disasters

[2285] In 2015, NOK 1.47 billion was paid out in compensation for natural damage

[2286] Examples of damaged objects are private roads and bridges, forests, quays and breakwaters, as well as cultivated land

[2287] The injured party reports the case to the sheriff, who assesses the damage (sheriff's assessment) and sends the case to the board of the State Natural Disaster Fund

[2288] In 2015, NOK 186 million was paid from the State Natural Disaster Fund in discretionary funds to municipalities and county municipalities following natural damage

[2289] – Both the Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation and the county governors can provide discretionary funds to municipalities that have been exposed to unforeseen events and incurred extraordinary expenses

[2290] The funds mainly go towards compensation for damage to municipal and county infrastructure after floods, landslides and other natural events

[2291] The money comes from the framework grant to the municipalities and county councils. The scheme involves assistance to municipalities for planning, designing and implementing preventive measures to protect existing buildings against damage from floods and landslides

[2292] The recipient of the support must normally pay a co-payment (district share) of 20 percent of the costs of the security measure

[2293] No deductible is required for emergency measures that must be implemented quickly to avoid an acute risk of damage

[2294] In 2015, the ordinary allocation for the prevention of flood and landslide damage under the auspices of NVE was approximately NOK 260 million

[2295] The Natural Disaster Scheme is administered by the Norwegian Natural Disaster Pool with Finans Norge as the business manager

[2296] For more information, see www.naturskade.no

[2307] Better preparedness against forest fires – helicopter and management support The main elements of preparedness against forest fires are the state helicopter preparedness and the management support scheme, both of which are administered by DSB

[2308] The forest fire helicopters are on standby from April to August

[2309] These are heavy-lift machines that lift approximately three tons of water, unlike smaller helicopters with approximately one ton lifting capacity

[2310] The helicopters are rented from commercial operators, and during the emergency period, one heavy-lift machine is always on standby, normally located at Torp

[2311] In recent years, the government has strengthened helicopter preparedness, making helicopters a more predictable resource for the country's fire and rescue services

[2312] In the 2016 state budget, the fixed budget for flight time was increased from three to five million kroner

[2313] This has increased the ability to quickly deploy multiple helicopters simultaneously

[2314] It has also made it possible to increase preparedness during periods of high fire danger through the deployment of several forest fire helicopters in various parts of the country

[2315] It has also made it possible for helicopters to be used in the training of fire commanders and other ground crews

[2316] Emergency network radios have been installed in two heavy-lift helicopters

[2317] In addition to the civilian helicopters, the Norwegian Defence Force can also be requested to assist with its resources in the event of a forest fire

[2318] First and foremost, assistance from the Armed Forces' Bell helicopters, the Home Guard and the Coast Guard is needed, but other resources will also be able to assist, depending on the circumstances

[2319] The Armed Forces also have air tactical units that can control the airspace if there is a need to coordinate flights with multiple helicopters in the same area

[2320] This was used during the fire in Froland

[2321] DSB's management support scheme provides local fire and rescue services with support for the effective use of the state's forest fire helicopter

[2322] Selected fire and rescue services and their leading fire commanders are on standby to provide support to local fire chiefs who are given responsibility in the event of a forest fire

[2323] The costs of this support are covered by DSB

[2328] Climate change and its impact on forestry

[2329] Stormwater is surface runoff resulting from precipitation or meltwater

[2330] Dense surfaces such as asphalt and roofs cause precipitation to quickly run off surfaces in cities and towns, and collect in low points in the urban space

[2331] Damage caused by stormwater is rarely life-threatening, but the extent is increasing as a result of climate change and people living in ever closer proximity

[2332] Changes in climate, see text box 7.1, mean that torrential rain episodes may become more intense and occur more frequently

[2333] The committee that investigated stormwater in cities and towns estimates in NOU

[2334] that total insurance payments for water intrusion in recent years have been approximately NOK 600 million per year, and will increase in the future

[2335] The committee estimates that the total damage from stormwater, direct and indirect, will amount to between NOK 45 and 100 billion over the next 40 years, if new preventive measures are not implemented

[2336] Traditionally, flooding has not been commonly referred to as a serious natural event, but the economic damage potential of this phenomenon suggests that it should be treated together with the more traditional natural events

[2338] Risk in a safe society helicopter overall is the most suitable resource in Norway

[2339] Airplanes require a greater length of water surface, as they cannot retrieve water vertically

[2340] In Norway, it is generally a short distance to small lakes and ponds, and potentially a longer distance to larger bodies of water

[2341] Norwegian topography and geography thus make helicopters more suitable

[2342] Aircraft are also very expensive to purchase (a Canadair 415 CL costs about NOK 200 million), and require an extensive operation and maintenance program to be operational

[2343] It is also difficult to find other uses for such aircraft

[2344] Even in collaboration with other Nordic countries, there will be so little demand for such capacity that the use of resources cannot be justified

[2346] Emergency management manager Svein Oskar Wigestrand and his colleagues in Eigersund municipality were put to the test when the extreme weather Synne caused major flooding in the heart of the municipality

[2347] This is how they handled the situation in an exemplary manner. On December 15, 2015, at 8:52 p.m., the Meteorological Institute reported that the extreme weather phenomenon Synne was in full swing in Agder and Rogaland

[2348] Unusually large amounts of rainfall fell and led to flooding of several rivers

[2349] Among these were the Hellelandsvassdraget and the Bjerkreimsvassdraget, both of which flow into the center of Eigersund

[2350] The municipality won DSB's public safety award for its handling of the incident

[2351] Wigestrand says that understanding roles in the municipality is essential for good crisis preparedness

[2352] – In many municipalities, the mayor is the head of emergency preparedness in a crisis situation

[2353] This should not be the case, because it makes the boundaries between administration and politics blurred

[2354] The mayor should rather represent the municipality externally and have contact with the public and the press, similar to daily operations

[2355] The councilor should lead the operational emergency response work, says Wigestrand

[2356] The Hellelandsvässdraget, which runs along the E39, was four meters above normal water level

[2357] There were areas in the municipality that were completely isolated, roads were closed, power was out, and telecommunications and emergency networks had failed

[2359] The emergency response manager highlights five criteria that should form the basis for dealing with unforeseen events: strong and early focus on ongoing information

[2360] This applies both internally and externally in all phases; before, during and after

[2361] Short updates and quick responses show acceptance and understanding that preparations are being made, measures are being implemented and staff are being assigned at an early stage

[2362] Then in some cases it will turn out that it was not necessary

[2363] The weather forecast is not always correct

[2364] It is not wasted money, but must be seen as extra training and good local knowledge

[2365] About watercourses, catchment areas, river courses and vulnerable areas

[2366] It is also important to have good local knowledge of buildings, roads, mobile phone masts and power supply, as well as knowledge of what relevant resources are available, internally and externally with collaboration partners

[2367] This must be maintained and shared through personal relationships internally and externally between the various partners and the municipality, with the necessary tools in place before it is needed

[2368] This means plans and equipment such as concrete barriers, sandbags, and support tools

[2369] As well as tools for population alerting such as Varsling

[2370] Flood zone map, planned and tested operating room premises, backup power and backup communications

[2374] Preparedness against storm damage to forests

[2375] It is important that relevant emergency response organizations and the forestry industry enter into closer cooperation to meet the challenge of forest destruction as a result of storms

[2376] The Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness has therefore decided, in consultation with the Ministry of Agriculture and Food, that the current “Forest Fire Committee” will be expanded to also be a forum for preventing storm damage to forests

[2377] Since 1985, the Forest Fire Committee has been a forum with participation from both state and private actors, and has worked to increase the level of knowledge about forest fires and forest fire fighting

[2379] The forum will, among other things, discuss roles and collaboration, and create a common understanding between actors

[2380] Forest roads can contribute to reduced vulnerability

[2381] Transport infrastructure and communications are central elements in preparedness related to adverse events

[2382] The road network has important societal functions in the flow of people, goods and services

[2383] According to Statistics Norway, there are approximately 94,500 km of public roads in Norway as of January

[2384] The forest road network built in the period 1950 to 2015 amounts to approximately 104,000 km

[2385] Of this, about 48,000 km are forest roads and about 56,000 km are tractor roads/winter roads

[2386] Forest roads connect large areas of forest and open space to public road networks

[2387] This makes the forest road network significant in the context of emergency preparedness, especially the forest roads

[2388] This may be in connection with forest fires, storms or rescue operations

[2389] Forest roads can also be used in some cases if the public road network has to be closed, or in emergency situations

[2390] Forest roads are mainly private roads and knowledge of the characteristics of these roads is important in a preparedness context

[2391] The county governor's agricultural departments and the municipalities have specialist expertise and mapping material that can be of great importance for effective cost-benefit assessments and prioritization of measures in the event of an unwanted event

[2392] Investments in the forest road network contribute to reduced vulnerability to climate damage and are thereby positive emergency preparedness and prevention measures

[2394] international Climate adaptation and societal security in the EU and the UN With future changes in climate, serious natural events will likely occur more frequently

[2402] The framework will promote societal security locally, nationally, and internationally through cross-sectoral cooperation

[2403] This is operationalized through seven sub-goals

[2404] reduce mortality from incidents and disasters by 2030 reduce the number of people affected by incidents and disasters globally by 2030 reduce economic losses as a share of GDP by 2030 reduce the loss of critical infrastructure and critical societal functions, including education and health, by 2030 increase the number of countries that have national and local strategies for social security by 2020 increase international development cooperation through appropriate and sustainable assistance such as the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030 http://www.preventionweb.net/files/eld

[2423] Risks in a safe society Serious crime

[2424] Norway is an open society with significant trust between individuals, between different institutions, and between citizens, businesses and the public sector

[2425] Serious crime can threaten the foundations of the welfare state

[2426] If citizens experience high crime rates, it could create a feeling of insecurity

[2427] It can weaken citizens' trust in the state, a trust that is a prerequisite for our social order and our democracy

[2428] Over time, serious crime could pose a threat to the stability, security and quality of the society in which we live

[2429] Serious crime can also form a financial foundation for ideological or religious forces that wish to direct attacks against individuals, social institutions, government bodies or our governance systems

[2430] Violent extremism, intelligence against Norway and Norwegian interests, ICT crime, money laundering and terrorist financing, and workplace crime are serious areas of crime that are addressed in this report

[2431] A common feature of several of these forms of crime is that they have become more technologically advanced, organized and global than before

[2432] At the same time, crime is changing according to what yields the greatest and fastest possible profit, and represents the least possible risk of criminal repercussions

[2433] The flexibility and adaptability of criminals must have consequences for the fight against crime

[2434] A better understanding of the challenges is needed, and the need for effective preventive measures is increasing

[2435] We need appropriate police methods and strengthened cooperation across sectors of society and between government agencies

[2467] Prevent radicalization and violent extremism

[2468] Radicalization is a process in which a person increasingly accepts the use of violence to achieve their political, ideological or religious goals, see box

[2469] Terrorism is the ultimate consequence of radicalization and violent extremism

[2470] PST considers that extreme Islamism constitutes the greatest terrorist threat in Norway, but also points out that the threat from right-wing extremist groups is increasing

[2471] Radicalization processes can occur within all types of views, political orientations and ideologies

[2472] Preventing radicalization and violent extremism is an important societal task, for which many sectors have a responsibility

[2473] It is important to have early preventive efforts and a good ability to identify people who are at risk as early as possible

[2474] A broad-based approach with efforts and cooperation between a number of actors is necessary: in municipalities, schools, child welfare and the police, and by involving local communities and voluntary organizations

[2475] The challenges must be met with knowledge about the phenomenon and about factors that can lead to radicalization and violence

[2476] It is also important to have a clear understanding of what should be done if there is suspicion or concern about radicalization

[2477] The government's action plan against radicalization and violent extremism is central to this work

[2478] The action plan was presented on June 10, 2014 and is aimed at all forms of extremism

[2479] The plan originally had 30 measures, all with specific follow-up responsibility in one or more ministries

[2480] The action plan is dynamic, which means, among other things, that several new measures have been developed as part of the continuous work in the field

[2481] A comprehensive and systematic process has been implemented to obtain input for new measures in line with societal developments and changes in the threat landscape

[2482] The process includes all affected sectors in the public sector, as well as broad involvement of voluntary organizations, clubs and associations

[2483] A number of measures have been implemented

[2516] Radicalization, violent extremism and hate crime

[2517] Radicalization is understood here as a process in which a person increasingly accepts the use of violence to achieve political, ideological or religious goals

[2518] A radicalization process that leads to violent extremism is characterized by: – a cognitive development towards an increasingly one-sided perception of reality, where there is no room for alternative perspectives – secondly, a further development in which the perception of reality is experienced so acutely and seriously that acts of violence are necessary and justified. Violent extremism is understood here as the activity of individuals and groups who are willing to use violence to achieve their political, ideological and religious goals

[2519] Hate crime is understood here as criminal acts that are wholly or partly motivated by negative attitudes towards a person or group's actual or perceived ethnicity, religion, political affiliation, sexual orientation, gender expression or disability

[2520] Violent extremism is the most extreme form of hate crime

[2525] Preventing and combating terrorism

[2526] Terrorism is a serious crime that undermines both our democratic form of government and human rights

[2527] Section 131 of the Criminal Code therefore sets out some limits for which acts are to be considered terrorism

[2528] A key characteristic of terrorist acts is that they create fear in a population, often with the intention of achieving political goals

[2529] The Government considers the prevention, deterrence and investigation of such acts to be central to Norwegian authorities being able to safeguard the safety of citizens

[2530] There are several actors with different political, religious or ideological beliefs who can carry out terrorist acts in Norway

[2531] PST considers extreme Islamism to constitute the greatest terrorist threat to Norwegian interests

[2532] The threat is particularly linked to the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL), and to a somewhat lesser extent to al Qaeda

[2533] ISIL has repeatedly threatened Western countries that are part of the coalition against ISIL, and encourages sympathizers in these countries to carry out attacks

[2534] The threat is cross-border and primarily concerns individuals who can inspire attacks

[2535] PST assesses that the threat from the far-right environment in Norway is increasing

[2536] Mobilization around issues related to the high number of refugees and asylum seekers is a key driving force for right-wing extremist activity, radicalization and recruitment

[2537] Traditional right-wing extremism is characterized by racist, Nazi and conspiratorial attitudes that are combined with the will to use violence to achieve political goals

[2538] The Islamophobic e

[2539] There can be smooth transitions between terror as a form of crime and terrorist attacks that take forms that result in them being considered armed attacks on the nation in accordance with the UN Charter

[2540] The police have the primary responsibility for preventing and combating terrorism

[2541] The Armed Forces are responsible for handling an armed attack on Norway

[2542] It is the government that decides whether a terrorist attack should be considered an armed attack

[2543] The photo was taken on November 17, 2015 in Paris outside the restaurant "Le Petit Cambodge

[2544] This was one of several locations in Paris that was hit by terrorist attacks on November 13, 2015, in which 130 people were killed and 413 injured

[2545] Risks in a safe society The anti-immigration environment generally focuses on Norwegian and European culture and tradition, as opposed to focusing on the “white race”

[2546] Hatred of authorities and distrust of democracy are widespread in the far-right environment

[2547] The threat from the environment is primarily related to individuals, or small groups within or outside the environment

[2548] The government has strengthened PST's budget by NOK 372 million since it took office

[2549] The government is thereby ensuring increased security and meeting the challenges created by a heightened threat landscape

[2550] The government has introduced stricter criminal regulations for foreign fighters by making it a criminal offense to participate militarily outside of state forces in armed conflict abroad

[2551] Travel, preparation and recruitment for such participation have also been made punishable

[2552] Increased criminal liability has also been introduced for Norwegian citizens who participate in military operations against Norwegian and allied forces abroad

[2553] Furthermore, PST has been given the necessary coercive measures for prevention and investigation in the digital space, including by means of data scanning

[2554] PST is better able to prevent and deter terrorist acts on Norwegian soil

[2555] A new digital analysis system in PST will further enable the service to move more quickly from analysis to actions that can prevent terror

[2556] A greater degree of automation will simplify the analysis work

[2557] This will also increase efficiency and resource utilization, and will thus reduce the need for increased staffing for this type of task in the long term

[2558] The government has therefore proposed 90 million kroner for a new analysis system in PST in the state budget

[2560] The Government will facilitate PST's targeting of its threat assessments in crisis situations at relevant actors

[2561] The purpose is to help ensure that those actors who have responsibility for and authority to implement measures have a better basis for assessing which measures should be implemented

[2562] A more targeted threat assessment should result in better resource use adapted to the individual crisis situation

[2564] The proposal for amendments to the Passport Act has been put out for consultation

[2565] The intention is to be able to refuse or revoke passports if there is reason to believe that the purpose of a trip is to participate in terrorist acts, terrorist-related acts or in armed conflict

[2566] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security is working on following up on the hearing

[2567] ID work will be strengthened in 2016 through increased use and storage of biometrics

[2568] In 2016, the Storting adopted amendments to sections 100 and 100a of the Immigration Act, which provide authority to routinely record and process biometric personal information in the form of fingerprints and facial photographs of all third-country nationals applying for a residence permit and visa to Norway

[2569] In the 2017 state budget, the government proposes NOK 81 million for the police and the Norwegian Directorate of Immigration (UDI) to strengthen the control of the identity of persons entering and residing in the kingdom, as well as to prevent and combat illegal residence and crime based on false ID and misuse of ID

[2570] This also includes expanded use of biometrics, more mobile handheld devices that enable identity verification, establishing a loss and verification system for public and private actors, as well as preparing national ID cards for foreign citizens and verification of foreign ID documents

[2571] Together with the infrastructure for passports and national ID cards, an environment for issuing eIDs together with national ID cards will be established

[2574] Intelligence activities against Norway and Norwegian interests

[2575] Most states have intelligence services that collect information and knowledge about other countries to secure their own national interests

[2576] Foreign states' intelligence activities in Norway involve legal and illegal information collection

[2577] Norway is an open society where foreign states have access to a lot of information legally

[2578] At the same time, in recent years there has been a significant development in the capacity of foreign intelligence services to conduct covert information gathering

[2579] Technological developments in recent years have also increased society's vulnerability to intelligence activities in the digital space through, among other things, so-called network operations

[2580] This development has also made it more challenging to distinguish state intelligence activities from traditional industrial espionage or eco

[2581] Parliament 10 2016–

[2582] nomic crime

[2583] Several states also use their intelligence services as a means to strengthen their own country's business development and competitiveness

[2584] Theft of sensitive information and influencing decisions and decision-making processes weakens competitiveness, and can, overall and over time, weaken the economic foundation of the welfare state, our security and preparedness

[2585] Both legal and illegal intelligence activities have significant potential for harm, but only the illegal collection of information is punishable under the Criminal Code

[2586] The legal collection must nevertheless be prevented in order to safeguard Norway's central social interests

[2587] In the Open Threat Assessment 2016, the PST states that intelligence activities in and against Norway are high

[2588] Norway is attractive to several intelligence services

[2589] We have a strategic location, are managers of large natural resources, are a member of NATO, have cutting-edge technological expertise, participate in peace and human rights work and occasionally become involved in various conflict areas

[2590] The National Security Authority (NSM) has, through several reports in recent years, described an increasing trend related to cyber espionage, particularly from 2007 onwards and at an accelerating rate in the last two years

[2591] The most extensive and potentially most harmful threats we see on the internet are mainly related to espionage

[2592] The E-service writes in its report, Focus 2016, that intelligence operations against Norway and Norwegian interests in the digital space appear to be technically advanced and targeted

[2593] Some intelligence services work very offensively, and they use a wide range of methods

[2594] Extensive and increasingly sophisticated digital

[2595] Online intelligence activities are therefore combined with more traditional forms of espionage

[2596] Intelligence officers located in Norway will have various forms of deck positions

[2597] Their main task is to establish personal and confidential contacts who can provide important information

[2598] Often, such contact activities will develop carefully and gradually, and may take place over several years

[2599] An increasing number of Norwegian citizens and people residing in Norway originate from states with which Norway does not have security policy cooperation

[2600] An increasing number have positions within sectors with access to sensitive and confidential information, such as national computer systems and registers

[2601] To the extent that foreign intelligence services achieve cooperation with these, either voluntarily or through pressure or coercion, they will be able to gain access to information with great potential for harm to Norway

[2602] Intelligence services also carry out information, influence and propaganda operations

[2603] The purpose is often to weaken trust in the authorities in a given country, or to create contradictions between ethnic groups or regions

[2604] Rumors, allegations and extensive campaigns can arise on social media without it being possible to determine who is behind them

[2605] Particularly in periods of security policy tensions, such instruments may be used, and this is something Norway must also be prepared for

[2606] Much of the intelligence against Norway and Norwegian interests aims to uncover classified and sensitive information about Norwegian defense, security and preparedness

[2607] The targets of intelligence activities are often ministries, public agencies, institutions and companies that manage or have information about critical infrastructure, political, economic and military matters

[2608] Foreign states attempt to obtain information about Norwegian political processes in order to influence or undermine them to their own country's advantage

[2609] There are also examples of what is termed “refugee espionage”, where states monitor their former citizens in Norway and exert pressure against them or their families in their home country

[2610] The purpose will often be to neutralize or reduce political opposition in the home country

[2611] It can often be difficult to link the harmful effects of intelligence activities to specific operations

[2612] Causal chains are challenging to identify, and it is difficult to prove that financial loss or other damage occurs as a direct result of a specific recovery operation

[2613] Often, there are long processes and many small pieces of information that, taken together, provide an intelligence gain

[2614] If we look at security policy harmful effects, the real damage will only become apparent in a situation where important national interests are at stake, such as in a crisis or a security policy incident

[2615] To the extent that foreign security and intelligence services succeed, this will be detrimental to Norway and Norwegian interests – whether it concerns covert information gathering to get ahead of Norway and Norwegian actors, covert influence to ensure that Norwegian decisions coincide with the interests of the foreign state, or covert manipulation or sabotage to disrupt the very decision-making and crisis management capacity

[2616] Preventing and deterring harmful intelligence against Norway and Norwegian interests is a state responsibility

[2617] At the same time, it is important that the general public, businesses, public and private enterprises are aware of the threats and risks we face

In relation to the traditional forms of espionage, the most important preventive measure is personnel security

[2623] Personnel security consists of measures, actions and assessments to prevent people who could pose a safety risk from being placed or being placed in a way that increases the risk

[2624] In Norway, this measure is taken care of by ensuring that personnel who will have or may have access to sensitive information are security cleared

[2625] As of today, there are 42 clearance authorities in Norway with varying sizes and expertise

[2626] To strengthen preventive work, the government has begun work on reducing the number of clearance authorities

[2644] ICT crime ICT crime is increasing in scope

[2645] The costs to society are significant

[2646] More and more crimes leave digital traces, while crime in the digital domain itself is increasing

[2647] ICT crime is incidents that are criminalized under Norwegian law, and is often divided into crime directed against the ICT systems themselves, and criminal acts committed using ICT as an essential tool

[2648] Examples of ICT crime may include computer attacks, illegal modification of data, illegal interception or reading of data communications, identity theft, online banking fraud, or the sale of drugs and other illegal products on the internet

[2649] Child abuse images and other abuse material are other examples of ICT crime

[2650] ICT crime is largely international

[2651] Criminals can reside in one country, use software located in another country, and commit crimes in a third

[2652] The criminals do not need to be physically close to the victim, they can attack many targets at the same time and have a good chance of not being detected

[2653] ICT crime is committed by very different types of perpetrators, from those in the "boys'/girls' room" to organized criminal groups

[2654] A particular challenge is professional criminals who sell services to other criminals

[2655] They either provide tools or carry out crimes on behalf of others

[2656] Due to the international dimension, it is often difficult to prevent and combat ICT crime

[2657] When several countries are involved, the differences in legislation between the countries will complicate the fight and prosecution

[2658] It also makes it challenging for information from Norway to be stored in Norway's Meld

[2659] Parliament 10 2016–

[2661] The government is committed to ensuring that Norway is safe and secure, also in the ICT area

[2662] Those who commit ICT crimes should not be able to prepare or carry out criminal acts without significant risk of being discovered and prosecuted

[2663] The work on ICT crime is also linked to the work that the government is doing to strengthen ICT security in society

[2664] Chapter 6, “Digital vulnerabilities and ICT security,” discusses both challenges and measures related to ICT security

[2665] To strengthen the fight against ICT crime, the Ministry of Justice and Public Security launched its first strategy against ICT crime in June

[2666] The strategy sets out the direction and priorities for the work of the judicial authorities, as well as 15 specific measures

[2667] The measures are aimed at strengthening expertise and capacity, building knowledge and strengthening research, identifying technological solutions and strengthening international cooperation and national legislation

[2668] A broadly composed reference group has been established to continuously provide input for future revisions of the strategy

[2669] Some of the measures in the strategy may have budgetary consequences

[2757] A well-functioning business and working life is a pillar of society

[2758] It is important for efficient task solving and service provision, for financing welfare benefits, and it is crucial for securing employment and wages for workers

[2761] Workplace crime is an act that violates Norwegian laws on wages and working conditions, social security, taxes and fees, that exploits employees or distorts competition and undermines the social structure

[2764] Workplace crime often includes serious violations of working hours regulations and other wage and employment conditions, tax and contribution crime, corruption, social security fraud, money laundering, undeclared work and human trafficking

[2815] Infectious diseases and dangerous substances – a better CBRNE preparedness

[2816] Infectious diseases are something we have to live with

[2817] The Norwegian population is generally in good health and has a good starting point for tolerating new health-related stresses

[2818] However, there is a risk that Norway could be affected by more serious outbreaks of infectious diseases

[2819] In recent years, several international outbreaks of serious infectious diseases have required major preparedness efforts in Norway

[2820] In addition, the Norwegian health service has had to deal with several domestic outbreaks of serious diseases that are rare in our country

[2821] Examples include outbreaks of Ebola virus, E. coli bacteria in food, legionella bacteria spread in the air, and the parasite

[2822] Giardia lamblia through water supply

[2823] A serious epidemic or pandemic could result in many people getting sick and dying

[2824] It can also have a number of serious consequences, such as many people being absent from work at the same time due to their own illness, so that important social functions are weakened or, in the worst case, collapse

[2825] We will experience an overstretched capacity in the health service

[2826] In scenario analyses of serious incidents that could affect Norway, a pandemic is considered one of the most likely scenarios, and one with the greatest consequence

[2827] Internationally, there are reports of an increase in patients infected with bacteria that are resistant to all available antibiotics

[2828] Antibiotic resistance is a rapidly growing global problem, and according to the World Health Organization, constitutes one of the greatest threats to global health

[2829] We risk a future without effective antibiotics, where infections that are today considered harmless can once again have fatal outcomes

[2830] Although there has been an increase in infections in Norway in recent years, the problem is currently significantly smaller than in most other countries

[2831] However, the problem is global, and developments in Norway are closely linked to developments internationally

[2832] There is a strong connection between the health of humans, terrestrial animals and fish, and the environment with regard to the development of antibiotic resistance

[2833] Bacteria and resistant genetic material are exchanged between different environments

[2834] High consumption of antibiotics in animals and fish will lead to the development of antibiotic resistance, which will also affect humans

[2835] Norway is among the countries in Europe with the lowest consumption of antibiotics for animals

[2836] Although Norwegian livestock farming and food production are in a good situation, serious forms of antibiotic resistance have also been detected in Norwegian production animals such as poultry and pigs

[2837] Our modern society is completely dependent on a variety of chemicals, explosives and radioactive sources in industry and business, the transport sector and agriculture

[2838] A number of these are toxic or pose a fire and explosion hazard

[2839] Damage to the population, the environment or material assets can result from accidents during the transport of dangerous goods, industrial accidents, fires involving chemicals, explosions, environmental crime, releases of toxic substances and explosive accidents

[2840] Intentional acts such as sabotage or terrorism cannot be ruled out either

[2844] About 2,000 people were evacuated for four days until experts from Swedish industry helped empty the tanks

[2845] The bomb in the government quarter on July 22, 2011, was equivalent to about one ton of TNT

[2846] This tragic act showed how serious damage a homemade bomb can cause

[2904] Risk in a safe society: learning from CBRNE incidents

[2905] To achieve this objective, the government has established a National Strategy for CBRNE Preparedness (hereinafter referred to as the CBRNE Strategy

[2906] The CBRNE strategy has been published by the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, the Ministry of Health and Care Services and the Ministry of Defence, and provides goals, main priorities and measures to further develop CBRNE preparedness in Norway. The measures in the CBRNE strategy, together with additional measures described in this chapter, provide an overall picture of the government's priorities for improved CBRNE preparedness

[2907] Prevention and management of CBRNE incidents is largely anchored in international conventions and agreements that Norway is committed to following up

[2908] Export and import controls and various non-proliferation measures help prevent unauthorized persons from obtaining access to CBRNE agents

[2909] Norway will actively contribute to international CBRNE work within the UN, NATO, the EU and other multilateral forums, but also bilaterally and in the Nordic countries

[2910] Norwegian contributions to CBRNE forums must be anchored in the responsible ministry and coordinated with national professional communities

[2911] The Government will: – strengthen national preparedness against biological incidents by establishing a cross-sectoral collaborative arena for preparedness against biological incidents at directorate level and establish a National Preparedness Plan against serious infectious diseases, which will follow up on the experiences from the efforts against Ebola in West Africa 2014–2015 and other incidents – further develop efforts against pandemic influenza in line with the National Preparedness Plan against pandemic influenza, through international and national work to improve prevention, surveillance, warning, management and continuity planning – intensify work against antibiotic resistance by reducing and more appropriate use of antibiotics, improving the knowledge base and by being a driving force in international work – that the Ministry of Justice and Public Security shall establish a “Collaborative Area for Chemical and Explosives Preparedness” to contribute to cross-sectoral, comprehensive and coordinated work with CE preparedness at directorate level and ensure good professional advice to local, regional and central levels – implement measures to improve the prevention of chemical and explosive incidents and assess whether some fire and rescue services should develop special capacities to handle CE incidents – strengthen international cooperation, especially to prevent illegal access to weapons, explosives and explosive precursors – that the Ministry of Justice and Public Security should assess the need and possibilities for establishing a chemicals institute to assist local, regional and central levels and strengthen research and development – ​​formalise the function of the Defence Research Institute as a receiving laboratory for unknown CBRE samples – develop civil-military cooperation within bomb preparedness and explosives clearance – expand the planning basis for nuclear preparedness with a scenario that includes the use of nuclear weapons near or on Norwegian territory, and prepare measures for such an event

[2912] The measures are covered within the current budget frameworks of the ministries and directorates concerned

[2913] In principle, the same applies to new measures that are to be considered for implementation

[2930] CBRNE incidents cover everything from rare and serious poisonings and infectious diseases to individual accidents involving radiation sources, dangerous goods accidents and gases harmful to health

[2947] Risk in a safe society is the ability to detect and manage both known and unknown causes of public health crises

[2948] Norway has its own emergency plans for some of the diseases that the World Health Organization has defined as the most important infectious diseases, because they can develop into global epidemics

[2949] The government will focus its efforts on two areas in particular

[2950] good preparedness against pandemic influenza and other serious infectious diseases

[2952] Preparedness against pandemic influenza and other serious infectious diseases

[2953] We know that a new pandemic will come, but not when

[2954] The 2009 influenza pandemic (“swine flu pandemic”) taught us that there will be a lot of uncertainty related to both infectiousness and severity, especially in the beginning

[2955] A pandemic spreads in different areas of the country at different speeds

[2956] Pressure from the media and the public demands a common media strategy among key players

[2957] Sectors other than the health sector are affected to varying degrees

[2958] Although the number of lives lost in the 2009 pandemic was far lower than in pandemics in the 20th century, the situation was still demanding and costly, both humanly and for Norwegian authorities

[2959] If both infectiousness and mortality are high, a pandemic could be significantly more serious than was the case in

[2960] If Norway were to be hit by an epidemic of a large scale, this would place significant demands on the infection control preparedness of society

[2961] Availability of vaccines and medicines, the possibility of transporting and isolating the sick and infected are important elements of such preparedness

[2962] It is difficult to predict the overall societal consequences of a pandemic

[2963] The Spanish flu caused over 40 million deaths and is often used as an example of a worst-case scenario

[2964] The proportion of sick people distributed over the weeks when the pandemic is at its peak will be crucial

[2965] The National Pandemic Influenza Preparedness Plan describes what we should be prepared to face and how

[2966] The recommended planning scenario describes a moderate to severe pandemic, where the estimate is that 25 percent of the Norwegian population will become ill and develop symptoms

[2967] The health and care services must then be able to handle around 160,000 to 280,000 additional inquiries, and hospitals must be able to accept up to 14,000 to 16,500 admissions, of which 1,400 to 2,800 will require intensive care

[2968] To strengthen preparedness against pandemic influenza, the authorities must: – ensure joint national preparedness planning to handle an influenza pandemic – ensure continuity planning to maintain necessary societal functions within all sectors – focus on international cooperation on prevention, plans, monitoring and warning – improve the national systems for monitoring, assessment, warning and reporting. National preparedness is strengthened by the Ministry of Health and Care Services establishing a national preparedness plan against serious infectious diseases, including vaccine preparedness, transport solutions for infectious persons and isolation

[2969] The plan is based, among other things, on the experiences from the Norwegian efforts against the outbreak of Ebola virus in West Africa in 2014–

[2970] The Ministry of Health and Care Services is establishing a cross-sectoral collaborative arena for prevention, preparedness and management of biological incidents at directorate level, administratively subordinate to the Ministry of Health and Care Services

[2971] This will contribute to better government coordination of biological preparedness

[2972] Work against antibiotic resistance The threat from antibiotic resistance cannot be eliminated, but we must take measures to reduce the development of resistance and minimize the consequences for humans and animals

[2973] If antibiotics are to remain a global common good for future generations, we must set ambitious goals for the work against antibiotic resistance

[2974] This requires good efforts within several sectors, both internationally and nationally

[2975] It is important to contribute to the development of new antibiotics and diagnostic tools

[2976] The authorities should work to ensure that antibiotics are only used where necessary, while ensuring that everyone who needs access to antibiotics should have access to them

[2977] The Norwegian health service has a low consumption of antibiotics compared to many other countries, but we can still do better

[2978] The National Strategy against Antibiotic Resistance 2015–2020 sets out the government's goals for the work in the coming years and areas of action to achieve the goals

[2984] In January 2016, the Ministry of Health and Care Services published an Action Plan against Antibiotic Resistance in the Health Service with the goal of reducing antibiotic use in the population by 30 percent by the end of the year

[2985] The Ministry of Health and Care Services earmarked NOK 6 million in 2016 to follow up on this action plan, and the government is also proposing this in the state budget

[2986] In addition, the regional competence centers for infection control have been strengthened with approximately NOK 3.5 million to assist in the implementation of antibiotic stewardship programs in the health authorities

[2987] In March 2016, the Ministry of Agriculture and Food published an Action Plan against Antibiotic Resistance within the Ministry of Agriculture and Food's sectoral responsibility, which specifies measures to reduce the use of antibiotics in livestock by at least 10 percent and the use of antibiotics in pets by at least 30 percent compared to consumption

[2988] In the proposed state budget for 2017, the government proposes to strengthen the work against antibiotic resistance by increasing the allocations to the Norwegian Food Safety Authority and the Veterinary Institute in the Ministry of Agriculture and Food's budget by a total of NOK 10 million

[2989] The most important measures are: – reduce the total use of antibiotics – contribute to more appropriate use of antibiotics – increase knowledge about what causes the development and spread of antibiotic resistance – be a driving force in international work to strengthen access to, responsible use and development of new antibiotics, vaccines and better diagnostic tools 9.4 Chemical and explosives preparedness 9.4.1 Government coordination Major chemical and explosives incidents usually have cross-sectoral consequences

[2990] Incidents involving chemicals or explosives can be unpredictable and are often characterized by great uncertainty and a great need for information among the population

[2991] Many actors have a responsibility in the chemicals area, both at local, regional and central levels

[2992] The government has decided to clarify responsibility in the chemicals and explosives area

[2993] State coordination of the chemicals and explosives area falls within the Ministry of Justice and Public Security's coordination role for public security

[2994] The responsibility does not include the arrangements established within emergency preparedness against acute pollution, where the Ministry of Transport and Communications and the Norwegian Coastal Administration have a special role in accordance with the Pollution Control Act

[2995] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security shall establish a “Collaborative Area for Chemical and Explosives Preparedness” led by the Directorate for Civil Security and Public Security (DSB

[2996] The cooperative area for chemical and explosives preparedness shall support the Ministry of Justice and Public Security's coordinating role in the area, and contribute to cross-sectoral, comprehensive and coordinated work at directorate level

[2997] The cooperative area will develop professional expertise and a preparedness network for advising responsible preparedness actors in the handling and normalization phase

[2998] The group will also contribute to ensuring that the need for professional advice and expertise at central, regional and local levels is met, and that this is included in planning and practiced

[2999] Each business and private individual who handles chemicals and explosives has a duty of care, to ensure safe handling and storage, and to prevent accidents

[3000] The authorities' means of prevention include regulations, information, guidance, supervision, research and development

[3001] National regulations in the chemicals and explosives area are largely based on directives and regulations from the EU, and for the transport of dangerous goods, based on UN recommended guidelines

[3002] The regulations should be designed so that they are easily understandable for users, and digital solutions and tools should be used to provide better information and guidance

[3003] Every day, various industries and businesses handle large quantities of chemicals

[3004] The activities are important for value creation in Norway

[3005] At the same time, society needs assurance that handling takes place without serious accidents and that chemicals and explosives do not go astray

[3006] During 2017, DSB will assess what risk society should accept and whether the current state is good enough

[3007] Based on this work, DSB will make a recommendation to the Ministry of Justice and Public Security regarding the level of security that preventive work in the chemicals and explosives area should build upon

[3008] Supervision is an important tool because the consequences of incidents can be large and very serious

[3009] Relatively few inspections focus on environmental safety in relation to the total number of inspected objects

[3010] In total, there are just over 300 businesses covered by the Major Accidents Regulations in Norway and approximately 10,000 facilities that handle hazardous substances

[3018] DSB will strengthen supervision of businesses in the chemicals sector and ensure strict sanctions for businesses that do not comply with the regulations

[3154] Risk in a safe society Civil-military cooperation and total defense

[3155] Challenges and government policy

[3156] The international security situation has become more demanding, placing increased demands on good civil-military cooperation to safeguard societal security and national security

[3157] The threat and risk picture today is different than it was a few years ago

[3158] Increased migration flows to Europe, more serious terrorist attacks, more frequent cases of extreme weather and flooding, digital attacks and a more demanding security policy development are examples that characterize the picture

[3159] One of the government's instruments for meeting many of these challenges is to further develop civil-military cooperation within the framework of the total defense concept

[3160] There is a clear division of labor with solid political and constitutional roots for what constitutes civilian and military responsibility

[3161] The government has the ultimate responsibility for safeguarding societal security and national security

[3162] Civilian authorities and actors are responsible for ensuring public safety

[3163] The primary task of the Defence Force is to assert Norway's sovereignty and Norwegian sovereign rights and defend the country against external attacks, i.e. to safeguard national security

[3164] Civil and military preparedness and crisis management are, however, mutually dependent on each other, and ongoing cooperation is therefore necessary

[3165] Civil-military cooperation is also important for making the best possible use of society's overall resources and thus contributing to a good social economy

[3166] The four fundamental principles for working with civil security are also the basis for civil-military cooperation within the framework of total defence, see chapter

[3167] The total defense concept encompasses mutual support and cooperation between civil society and the Armed Forces to prevent, plan for, and manage crises in peacetime, security policy crises, armed conflict, and war

[3168] The total defense concept is part of the broad concept of civil-military cooperation, but is limited to cooperation related to crises

[3169] In 2015, the Ministry of Justice and Public Security and the Ministry of Defence published a revised version of the publication Support and Cooperation

[3170] It describes actors, roles, responsibilities, cooperation forums and laws that fall under the concept of total defense

[3171] The long-term plan for the defense sector assumes that Norway will strengthen its ability to defend its own territory and that of allied countries, and that this will take place within the framework of NATO's collective defense

[3172] Today's challenge picture is complex, can change rapidly and may require different forms of response from the Armed Forces

[3173] The armed forces must therefore be able to react quickly and with all resources simultaneously if necessary

[3174] In order for the Armed Forces to solve the tasks, possibly together with reinforcements from NATO, extensive civilian support and cooperation with public authorities and private actors is necessary

[3175] The Government will further develop the support of civilian authorities and civil society for the Norwegian Defence Forces

[3176] The Armed Forces also depend on society functioning as normally as possible during security crises and armed conflicts

[3177] Good public safety, preparedness and robust infrastructure are therefore also important for the Armed Forces' ability to safeguard national security

[3178] The defense sector has large resources, both material and human, which can be of great use in serious crises

[3179] The police and civil authorities may, in accordance with the total defence concept, request

[3180] The Norwegian Armed Forces for assistance and support to safeguard societal security when civilian resources are insufficient

[3181] The Government will further develop the Armed Forces' support for civil society

[3182] At the same time, it must be ensured that military operational capacities are not tied to civil preparedness in a way that reduces the possibility of carrying out military tasks, unless otherwise decided

[3183] The Armed Forces' own needs will still be most important for developing the Armed Forces' structure and capabilities

[3184] For total defense to function well, it requires close cooperation

[3185] In addition to holding exercises, cooperation forums have been established at several levels

[3186] The forum with the broadest participation is the Central Total Defense Forum, which consists of representatives from the Armed Forces and a number of civilian agencies and proposals

[3192] This and other collaborative forums and meeting places are important in the further development of total defense

[3193] NATO is also placing more emphasis on civil preparedness and civil-military cooperation because it is a prerequisite for the individual country's, and thus the alliance's, overall preparedness and defense

[3194] In particular, the development of a combined use of instruments, hybrid threats and instruments, has contributed to putting this on NATO's agenda

[3195] In this context, hybrid threats and instruments refer to the threat of, or use by, state or non-state actors of, a combination of political, military and economic means of power, as well as information and civilian instruments to exploit vulnerabilities, create unrest and achieve goals

[3196] NATO member states have set themselves the goal of creating resilient societal functions and infrastructures against the full spectrum of threats

[3197] The government wants Norway to continue to be a driving force for this work in NATO

[3198] The Government will: – ensure that plans are established for civilian support to the Armed Forces in crisis and armed conflict, including for allied reinforcements – continuously assess whether existing prioritization mechanisms between military and civilian needs are sufficient – ​​adapt relevant cooperation and preparedness bodies to challenges in connection with security policy crises and armed conflict, in order to be able to support both known and unforeseen needs – ensure that civilian support to the Armed Forces will to a greater extent become an integrated part of the exercise activities and be included in both civilian and military exercise programs as well as in national preparedness plans – prepare new instructions for the Armed Forces’ assistance to the police – ensure sufficient training of counter-terrorism preparedness – finalize the police and the Armed Forces’ plans for securing all objects reported by the police to the Armed Forces, and practice securing the objects within available resource limits Figure

[3205] Civilian support for the Armed Forces

[3406] Civilian emergency preparedness work in NATO

[3407] NATO's increased emphasis on collective defense has also led to major changes within NATO's civil emergency preparedness work

[3408] Civil preparedness and civil-military cooperation have come into greater focus in NATO because it is an important element in each country's, and consequently in the Alliance's, overall preparedness and defense

[3409] Member states have a goal of ensuring resilient, critical infrastructure and societal functions, and improving civil preparedness and crisis management

[3410] Norway has worked for many years to strengthen security in critical societal functions, see Chapter 13, and is contributing strongly to driving this work forward in NATO

[3411] Norwegian civil-military cooperation and arrangements within total defense are highlighted in NATO as a good example

[3412] The National Emergency Preparedness System (NBS) consists of the Civil Emergency Preparedness System (SBS) and the Defence Sector Emergency Preparedness System (BFF

[3413] Both are built according to the same structure as NATO's crisis management system, NATO Crisis Response

[3414] The plan is subject to annual revisions

[3415] The structure for civil emergency preparedness work in NATO was changed in 2010 and today consists of four important specialist groups under the Civil Emergency Planning Committee (CEPC

[3416] In addition, there are a number of ad hoc committees and other working groups that contribute to NATO's civil preparedness work

[3417] A broad network of experts in member and partner countries has also been established who support the work of NATO individually or through participation in working groups, workshops and seminars and on international missions

[3418] All of these committees and experts are working to strengthen civil emergency preparedness cooperation

[3419] The subject groups cover many important subject areas such as transport, health, food and water, industry, energy and communications infrastructure, and the protection of the civilian population

[3420] NATO member states are calling on countries to strengthen their civil resilience, establish more robust social structures and maintain good governance

[3421] In these areas, it is civilian authorities and civilian actors who can contribute the most

[3422] NATO points out that 90 percent of all military transport is carried out using hired civilian resources or using the open commercial market

[3423] Over 50 percent of all satellite use for military purposes is provided by the commercial sector

[3424] Within host country support for NATO operations, over 75 percent of all deliveries are from local, civilian services or civilian infrastructure

[3425] These are examples of civil-military dependencies that are also highly relevant for Norway

[3426] At the NATO Summit in July 2016, member states committed to strengthening national civil preparedness and meeting seven basic expectations for resilience in critical societal functions

[3427] These are: – security of continuity in national governance systems and critical public services – robust energy supply – ability to handle uncontrolled movements of people – robust food and water supply – ability to handle mass casualties – robust communication systems – robust transport systems The Civil Emergency Planning Committee, in collaboration with civilian experts and professional groups, has specified goals for each of the seven expectations and prepared guidelines that will help member states implement measures to achieve this

[3428] National representatives and NATO experts from several sectors have participated in the work

[3429] including the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries, the Ministry of Transport and Communications, DSB, the Directorate of Health and others

[3430] Norway has thus been an active driver and contributor before the summit

[3431] The government supports the declaration from the summit and the emphasis on resilience in critical societal functions

[3432] The work will strengthen cooperation

[3436] To ensure a holistic approach to the further development of total defence and the work on NATO's seven fundamental expectations, the Ministry of Justice and Public Security is establishing a program

[3437] The goal is to further develop a total defense that is adapted to new challenges, framework conditions and assumptions by the end of 2020, as well as to strengthen the robustness of critical societal functions to increase society's resilience to crises

[3438] The program will consist of projects for each of NATO's fundamental expectations, in addition to projects for civilian support to the Armed Forces, development of Civil Defence and possibly other projects

[3439] The Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness will, in dialogue with affected ministries, clarify the various sectors' needs to be included in the program, as well as the need for projects in the various areas

[3440] NATO's expectations should be assessed against the work of other international organizations in the same areas, such as the EU and the International Energy Agency

[3441] The work on the program should be seen in the context of ongoing and relevant work in the ministries

[3442] This includes, among other things, the work on cross-sectoral coordination of social security work and the system that has been established to prepare status/condition assessments for 14 cross-sectoral socially critical functions and areas

[3443] Norway will contribute to strengthening civil emergency preparedness work in NATO, annually update and harmonize national emergency planning with NATO, and contribute civilian expertise from both the public and private sectors

[3444] Norway has actively contributed to NATO developing a civilian training and education program and guidelines for handling incidents involving the use of weapons of mass destruction, so-called minimum standards

[3445] This work will continue, contributing to strengthening the Alliance's ability to deal with the consequences of the use of weapons of mass destruction, and is a concrete area of cooperation with partner countries

[3446] Norway will continue its active participation in shaping NATO's policy in the cyber area and the alliance's overall ability to meet threats in the digital space

[3447] This is an example of how important military and civilian elements in a modern society are sought to be better protected through cooperation within NATO

[3450] Risk in a safe society Attitudes, culture and leadership for good societal security

[3451] A good safety culture in society Attitudes and culture affect safety in society

[3452] How we relate to risk and how well we are prepared for and act during a crisis is influenced by our attitudes and the culture we are a part of

[3453] Attitudes, culture and leadership in the public sector can be influenced through administration and policy

[3454] Decisions on appropriations, organizational structure, technological solutions and measures provide framework conditions for the state's development that have significance for culture and management

[3455] However, culture and good management cannot be adopted

[3456] It must be created and further developed in all organizations

[3457] An important task for the government is to develop suitable framework conditions for the administration to ensure good management and implementation

[3458] It is a management responsibility to create suitable framework conditions and practice good attitudes in daily life

[3459] It is everyone's responsibility to live up to and develop good values in practice

[3460] The work on good culture and management is an ongoing process that must be developed over time

[3461] Good collaboration requires that both technical, organizational and human prerequisites are in place

[3462] Chapters 5, 10, 12 and 13 describe various measures the government is implementing to ensure good cooperation

[3463] Attitudes, culture and leadership are also important, because it is people who interact

[3464] Collaboration and cooperation require respect for each other's roles, responsibilities and professional contributions, and acceptance that different tasks and perspectives must be weighed against each other

[3465] Professions belong to different communities with different ways of understanding and approaching a problem

[3466] An important skill in dealing with others is having knowledge and awareness of others' competence and understanding one's own limitations

[3467] If different organizations and perspectives are to work together, one is not primarily an advocate for one's own organization and one's own professional perspective

[3468] The measure of good collaboration lies in whether the tasks are solved well overall

[3469] The Government will: – build a stronger culture of collaboration, results and implementation in the administration, including through the Programme for Better Governance and Management in the State – actively use emergency preparedness conferences in the Government, regular meetings of the Government Security Committee and active coordination by the Crisis Council to ensure that public safety issues are continuously handled and anchored in the Government – ​​devote the necessary attention to the special challenges in public safety work through active use of collaborative arenas at all levels in the administration – set clearer requirements for leaders and ensure that public safety work is anchored in management, including through changes in planning, supervision and follow-up of exercises – develop a police force that creates good results in a culture characterised by openness and trust, where management is prominent in all parts of the agency, from the service out on patrol to the police's national leadership group – stimulate good cooperation at municipal, regional and national levels between the emergency services, between emergency response actors more generally and with business and voluntary actors – work to improve the safety culture in businesses and in society, including through competence-raising measures and better risk recognition – work to ensure good crisis management and the ability to “change pace” during crises, where good understanding of roles and responsibilities are clarified and understood, both between levels and between involved actors and sectors – that the Norwegian Police College further develops joint continuing and advanced training for the emergency and response agencies Report

[3471] Risk in a safe society

[3472] Better management and implementation in the state administration

[3473] Leadership and implementation capabilities in the area of ​​public safety do not occur in a vacuum

[3474] The need for coordination, uncertainty about future risk and rapid technological change are examples of conditions that make management in the area of ​​civil protection demanding

[3475] Professional management and good leadership are therefore particularly important in the work with societal security

[3476] Safety is often not the primary task for managers who are supposed to ensure good safety

[3477] For the vast majority of people in the administration, crisis management is a task they encounter through planning and exercises, and rarely or never experience in practice

[3478] Paying attention to something that might happen, when there is a desire to improve services that the population needs on a daily basis, can be a challenge for leaders and others

[3479] We must acknowledge the special challenges that social security work entails, so that we can respond appropriately to them

[3480] At the same time, work on social security is an integrated part of the administration's work

[3481] Many of the challenges are general challenges related to attitudes, culture and management in the administration

[3482] The government's focus on better governance and management in the state is therefore important, also for the work on societal security

[3542] The goal is for senior managers to take more active leadership in digital Attitudes, culture and leadership Attitudes, culture and leadership are understood and defined in many different ways in different professional traditions and contexts

[3543] In this report, culture is understood as a community of ideas, values, norms and knowledge that a group of people share, and which they have acquired through learning and adaptation

[3544] Culture involves habits, routines and ways of solving tasks

[3545] Culture is often not put into words, it is experienced, complex and can in many cases be influenced, but not decided

[3546] A good preparedness culture is open, action-oriented, cooperative, knowledge-seeking and, not least, risk-aware

[3547] Organizational culture is understood as the set of shared values, norms, and perceptions of reality that develop in an organization when members interact with each other and their environment

[3548] The organizational culture shows what is expected and what the success criteria are in a workplace

[3549] Attitudes are about the attitude we have towards something

[3550] Attitudes include what we believe is right, but also what we feel and how we are inclined to act

[3551] Attitudes consciously or unconsciously influence how we act, as individuals or organizations

[3552] If attitudes are shared in an organization, they will influence how people in the organization perform their tasks

[3553] Managers are responsible for both management, meaning exercising leadership, and governance through creating results in line with the goals that have been set

[3554] Developing good leaders must take place both by developing the leaders' leadership skills and their ability to solve tasks in an effective manner, by achieving results and reaching defined goals

[3563] Better leadership and governance in the area of ​​civil protection

[3564] Increased attention and coordination within the government

[3565] Continuous work on societal security and good collaboration in societal security work is a high priority for the government

[3566] The government regularly holds its own emergency preparedness conferences dedicated to public safety issues

[3567] This ensures that the government has sustained attention to security issues and ensures progress on priority issues

[3568] The government has on several occasions requested reports from all ministers in their areas of responsibility on topics related to societal security

[3569] The reviews by the ministers have given the government the opportunity to see vulnerabilities and the need for measures across the government councils' areas of responsibility

[3570] The government has particularly emphasized that complex cases should not have unclear responsibilities

[3571] One department with primary responsibility for critical societal functions has been an important step

[3572] The Government Security Committee (RSU) is chaired by the Prime Minister and is the government's body for discussing and making decisions on important, classified security and emergency preparedness issues

[3573] A separate RSU secretariat has been established at the Prime Minister's Office with representatives from several central departments

[3574] The secretariat shall assist in the preparations and follow-up of the meetings of the RSU, with the aim of ensuring more systematic implementation of decisions in the area of security and emergency preparedness

[3575] This will strengthen the government's work on security and preparedness and ensure good coordination with responsible ministries

[3576] The Crisis Council is the highest coordination body at the administrative level

[3577] The Council has five permanent members: the top management at civil service level at the Prime Minister's Office, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, the Ministry of Health and Care Services, and the Ministry of Defence

[3578] The Council shall maintain and ensure strategic coordination

[3579] This means, among other things, assessing issues regarding lead ministries, ensuring coordination of measures implemented in different sectors, ensuring coordinated information to the public, the media and others, and facilitating that issues that require political clarification are quickly presented to the departments' political leadership or the government

[3580] By giving the Crisis Council a fixed core of members, experience transfer and learning from handling previous crisis situations is ensured

[3581] Those members of the council who are not directly affected by the crisis in question will have an important function as advisors in strategic decisions

[3582] If necessary, the crisis council can be expanded to include all other ministries, possibly also with representatives from underlying agencies and special expertise groups

[3583] The Crisis Council also meets when there is no crisis, through regular administrative meetings

[3584] The aim is to discuss and anchor overall emergency preparedness and crisis management challenges, and to review relevant incidents and exercises

[3585] The Crisis Council also conducts and participates in exercises

[3586] The Crisis Council is a central arena for coordination, where important issues are raised to the highest administrative management level

[3587] This contributes to good and coordinated presentation of cases to the government, and ensures that relevant emergency preparedness matters receive the necessary attention and are handled

[3588] The civil emergency preparedness system is revised annually

[3589] A key change that has been implemented is that more decisions during incidents have now been delegated from the government to lower levels of administration

[3590] It has also been made clearer that decisions can and should be made at a lower level, for example at directorate level or by the police chief

[3591] Fewer matters must therefore be decided by the government

[3592] This should result in more effective decisions, clearer delegated authority and also implies an expectation that managers make the necessary decisions at the appropriate level

[3593] The coordinating and driving role of the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness

[3594] There is increased activity in various coordination bodies at the central level

[3595] A significant number of cases are brought forward for discussion or processing in joint bodies

[3596] There is great awareness of the importance of working systematically and not letting disagreements stop processes

[3597] The Minister of Justice and Public Security is keen to take an active role in coordinating important matters, and perceives that there is increased legitimacy within the administration related to the role that the National Emergency Preparedness System consists of the Civil Emergency Preparedness System and the Emergency Preparedness System for the Defence Sector
