[3711] Mørk is a police superintendent in the West Police District

[3712] She was one of many from the emergency services who responded after the serious helicopter accident on Turøy on April 29, 2016. – To successfully handle a demanding incident, I believe it is crucial to have good, clear and present leadership from the police

[3713] Good interaction with other emergency services and good interaction with the municipality means a lot

[3714] It is also important that there is a staff that works well from the start

[3715] A lot of learning in exercises

[3716] – We had a large exercise in Øygarden municipality a few months before the helicopter accident on Turøy

[3717] The municipalities, fire department, health, crisis teams, police and Civil Defense participated

[3718] During this exercise, we saw the importance of municipalities arranging for food, rooms for evacuees, relatives' centers, crisis management, etc

[3719] We gained a lot of good experiences that we greatly benefited from during the helicopter accident

[3720] Important qualities in leadership – When handling major incidents, a good overview of the situation and clear leadership are crucial

[3721] It is equally important that managers are good at delegating tasks to their employees, and not least trusting that everyone does their jobs

[3722] The ability to interact with others – both with your own colleagues and with other emergency response actors – is also important

[3723] It is important to have a good understanding of the tasks and responsibilities of other agencies

[3724] – Personal qualities, such as the ability to stay calm and not get stressed, matter a lot

[3725] The fact that the police chief was concerned about what we were doing and how we crews were doing was a good support during the handling of the helicopter accident

[3726] The manager's presence contributed to good management – even if it was perhaps a little indirect

[3727] He arrived at the scene the night of the accident and was present in the office when the crews came in after a long shift

[3728] He was also present at the relatives' center and was concerned about both the relatives and those who worked there

[3729] Daily collaboration comes in handy during crises

[3730] — I also found that the interdisciplinary collaboration we have had between four municipalities (Fjell, Sund, Askøy and Øygarden) was useful to have with us during the crisis

[3731] Even though it is not directly linked to emergency incidents, we have long had regular police councils, and we have good coordination of local crime prevention measures (the so called SLT scheme

[3732] This has meant that the local police are close to crisis teams, child welfare and mental health services, among other things

[3733] This collaboration was particularly useful in following up on relatives who lived in our municipalities

[3734] Cooperation between the police and municipalities ensures good and comprehensive follow-up

[3740] Better preparedness through cross-sectoral development projects

[3741] Where the challenges are the same and joint solutions make sense, it is important that the tasks are solved jointly, often through joint projects

[3742] Several major development projects are underway, or have recently been completed, where collaboration and joint problem solving have been a prerequisite for success

[3743] Some key projects are

[3744] – The development of the Emergency Network

[3745] The development was a collaboration between the justice and health sectors

[3746] The project was led by the Directorate of Emergency Communications and has taken place in close collaboration with the three emergency services that are core users of the network

[3747] The emergency network became nationwide in 2015, see chapter 5.5.1 – “National emergency reporting project” was established by the government in 2014 to investigate the Norwegian emergency reporting service

[3748] The project was established across the justice and health sectors and also involved the municipal sector, affected directorates and professional communities

[3749] The work has been continued in the Program for improving the emergency notification service, see chapter 5.2.3 – National procedure for emergency services cooperation in the event of ongoing life-threatening violence – PLIVO was developed by the Directorate of Health, POD and DSB jointly in 2015, see chapter

[3750] – The introduction of new rescue helicopters that the government decided to acquire in December 2013 is a collaboration between the defense and justice sectors

[3751] Future operations and management require cooperation and interaction at many levels

[3752] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security is the responsible ministry, see chapter

[3753] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security has identified some significant learning points and success factors in relation to cross-sectoral projects: – the project must be well-established by management at the right level among the participants and management signals must be coordinated between the sectors and clearly communicated – the project must be widely established among those affected by the changes – a common understanding of the current situation must be created – working methods and process management are important, with broad participation to ensure anchoring, legitimacy and implementation – common goals across agencies and sectors are crucial and require a willingness to compromise – benefits, both short-term and long-term, must be identified and made visible – those involved must pay attention to the realization of benefits over time If a cross-sectoral project is to succeed, management support at the right level is required

[3754] Management must clearly stand behind the project, prioritize the work, and see the value in the fact that the measures are cross-sectoral

[3755] It is important that the management signals from the various departments to the agencies involved are coordinated and clearly communicated

[3756] It is important to have good coordination at all levels: both at departmental and directorate level

[3757] Management commitment is about ensuring that management in the various sectors supports the goals, that the "pace" of implementation is sufficiently similar, and that management supports and follows up on the process

[3758] It is difficult to create consensus on common goals and measures if there is no agreement on what the current situation looks like, what the desired future situation is, and the gap between these

[3759] This applies to all development projects, but becomes especially important if the projects cross agencies or sectors

[3760] A common understanding of the current situation and the needs for change must be created initially and before alternative solutions are considered

[3761] To obtain a thorough mapping of needs, for example, we chose

[3763] It is not unusual to go straight into discussions of different solution alternatives

[3800] A good culture of prevention

[3801] Prevention is about avoiding something undesirable from happening, or reducing the potential for harm from events that actually occur

[3802] A challenge with preventive work is maintaining the necessary effort, investment and vigilance over time, despite the absence of incidents that confirm the necessity of the measures

[3803] For example, it will be difficult to know whether the work against radicalization of youth has led to our avoiding terrorist attacks

[3804] Working towards a good culture of prevention is about influencing and changing knowledge, motivation, attitudes and behavior both in society and in businesses

[3805] This requires a basic understanding and recognition that safety is important

[3806] In businesses, this must permeate the entire organization

[3807] In practice, it is about management attention and priorities, and establishing a common understanding of why prevention is important and what harmful consequences a lack of prevention can have

[3808] A good safety culture is easier to create if the individual feels that it is possible to carry out the work in line with the necessary safety and preventive measures, requirements and instructions

[3809] It is about facilitation and feasibility, training and guidance

[3810] There should be openness about challenges, reporting of adverse events and continuous learning and improvements

[3811] Prevention is most successful if it becomes an integrated part of ordinary work, not a competing consideration that delays daily tasks

[3820] Digital alienation and digital carelessness What should be prevented is constantly changing

[3821] For example, technological development and digitalization provide new solutions and opportunities, but also changed and new vulnerabilities that must be addressed

[3822] Security was easier to assess and understand when what was to be secured and the security measures were something physical, tangible and stable

[3823] Lockable cabinets and other physical barriers are relatively easy to understand and assess

[3824] Many conditions that need to be prevented today can be complicated, they change rapidly and are demanding to understand

[3825] It can create attitudes and passivity that are not desirable

[3826] Digital development is the clearest example of how it is no longer intuitive what creates good security and what does not

[3827] We must accept “recipes” for how we should behave, without being able to assess for ourselves whether what we are doing is sensible

[3828] We also don't notice any immediate difference whether we follow safety routines or not

[3829] While everyone can see a door that wasn't locked properly, we don't "see" irresponsible digital behavior in the same way

[3830] With digitalization, we can, to a greater extent than before, be described as alienated when it comes to security

[3831] We no longer have the same overview of the vulnerability picture

[3832] The effect of such alienation is not unique to Norway and can be described as a digital carelessness

[3833] A combination of lack of interest and overwhelm can result in lack of attention, lack of concern and thus what may in reality be careless behavior, even if it is not intended to be so

[3835] Leadership during crises Major events come as a surprise

[3836] In many cases, there is a great lack of information about the incident, especially at the beginning

[3837] It may be unclear what kind of event it is, how it might develop and who might be affected

[3838] Nevertheless, decisions must be made about how the crisis should be handled and who should be involved in the work

[3839] The need for coordination and information exchange is great, both between the levels of the crisis management apparatus and between various actors involved in the management

[3840] Major events require more from leaders and organizations than everyday problem-solving

[3841] A "change of pace" is required

[3842] All assessments and decisions are made under greater time pressure and with greater uncertainty than in daily work

[3843] At the same time, the consequences of decisions can be significantly higher

[3844] The possibilities increase for making decisions that may later turn out to have been wrong

[3845] The pressure on leaders is increasing

[3846] The certainty of one's own responsibility, the seriousness of the incident and the possible consequences of one's own actions can lead to stress that can affect both the ability to assess the situation and to make necessary decisions

[3847] For positions that are directly related to crisis management, personal qualities that are important for good crisis management should therefore be emphasized when hiring or promoting

[3850] Both within and across organizations, it is crucial to know who is responsible for which tasks, and to understand what this means in different situations

[3853] At the same time, no two crises are alike

[3861] Good crisis management involves many people – from those who solve tasks at the scene of the incident to political leadership, often across many agencies, organizations and sectors

[3862] This creates two fundamental challenges: – A vertical challenge

[3863] to ensure that the crisis is handled well at various levels

[3864] This applies firstly to the various levels from emergency personnel where the crisis is taking place, via local and regional authorities, to central authorities, and ultimately the government

[3865] This also applies to the different levels internally within an organization, such as from the police incident commander via the operations manager to the strategic management – A horizontal challenge: ensuring good crisis management across sectors and organizations

[3866] This involves good coordination of plans, routines and clarification of responsibilities as part of the emergency preparedness work and good cooperation during incidents and in exercises

[3867] Different levels have different tasks and roles – the vertical challenge

[3868] Incident management takes place at several levels, where the different levels have different roles that together ensure good handling

[3869] It is crucial to find the balance between the need to find solutions on the spot and ensuring that the task is solved appropriately overall

[3870] The strategic crisis management is responsible for the overall handling of the incident

[3871] Strategies for incident management must, to the greatest extent possible, be determined outside of crises

[3872] This makes it easier to make good decisions when the event is a fact

[3873] Then the strategic crisis management during the incident can concentrate on strategic priorities, allocation of resources, necessary authorizations, horizontal involvement, information and communication

[3874] The strategic management has a special responsibility to assess how the incident may develop and what possible needs arise as the incident develops

[3875] If there may be a need to request assistance from other countries, for example to extinguish a forest fire, it is important to have thought about this early on, so that the mobilization of resources begins and the resources are ready in case of a possible need

[3876] The responsible government minister and strategic management need information from lower levels in the crisis management apparatus, both to ensure comprehensive and good handling of the incident and to inform the public

[3877] Communication and information to the population and the press is an essential part of the task of the strategic level

[3878] It is important that information gathering disrupts tactical and operational incident management as little as possible

[3879] It must be targeted at what the strategic level needs to know in order to solve its part of the problem

[3880] It is also important that compiled information is communicated to lower levels, so that they can act based on the knowledge available about the incident

[3881] How the challenges are perceived and understood may vary between levels

[3882] The incident commander at the scene may need resources that, in his or her judgment, are very important

[3883] For example, in the case of multiple, simultaneous events, other considerations may dictate other priorities

[3884] The understanding of an event and what is required for good problem solving will also vary between subjects, sectors and professions

[3885] Different tasks and roles can easily create tension if you do not have a good understanding of your own and others' roles, and trust that others will perform their tasks well

[3886] Actors must be aware that they should solve the challenges at their level, and not make decisions that should be made elsewhere in the crisis management apparatus

[3887] When the pressure is great, it can be demanding

[3914] Mission-based management

[3915] Good crisis management requires that the first person to arrive at an incident has the ability and authority to begin the work of handling the incident

[3916] The mission must be solved at the moment

[3917] The assessments made must be adapted to the mission, available resources and how the situation develops

[3918] It is usually the emergency personnel on site who are best able to understand the situation and assess further handling

[3919] The proximity principle is based on the recognition that those closest to the incident are in most cases best suited to handle the incident, see chapter

[3920] Therefore, those at the scene of the incident are delegated a large degree of authority in all emergency services

[3921] Those who solve a task must have a good understanding of how the task should be solved

[3922] This understanding must be shared with other parts of the crisis management apparatus, and it must be largely based on knowledge and goals set before the incident occurs

[3923] Such understanding requires good professional knowledge, experience, skills and competence that takes time to build

[3926] The need for control and coordination, and the need for forces on the ground to be able to make independent assessments and lead themselves, is greater in war and armed conflict than in most other contexts

[3927] Precisely because the Armed Forces are geared towards extreme situations that civil authorities are fortunately rarely confronted with, their experience can be valuable in civil emergency preparedness work

[3928] The Armed Forces have mission-based leadership as their management philosophy

[3929] Mission-based leadership means that the person with the best understanding of the situation should act independently, while all assignments must be completed in light of the intention of the assignment

[3930] Once the intention has been discussed, understood and the individual has gained ownership of it, a common understanding of the mission and one's own role in achieving common goals must be created

[3947] Civil and military crisis management

[3948] There are clear similarities between civilian and military crisis management, but also significant differences

[3949] The police coordinate many different actors, both authorities, private individuals and volunteers, during a crisis

[3950] Who is coordinated will vary depending on the nature of the crisis

[3951] Even if civilian authorities exercise together, the effort cannot be planned jointly in the same way that a military team can train and prepare for an effort before a mission

[3952] The time horizon is normally significantly shorter in civil crises

[3953] A military operation may be planned for a long time, and actors who will work together in the operation have been given time for joint training

[3954] In civil crisis management, there is no equivalent planning option

[3955] The actors do not know in advance which incident will be handled, which crews are on duty when the incident occurs, or which agencies will be involved

[3956] Plans and exercises form the basis for crisis management, but the specific event cannot be planned

[3957] Good civilian crisis management is based, among other things, on lessons learned and routines that arise from experiences from daily work

[3958] Civil emergency services receive a lot of relevant training through handling minor and major incidents

[3959] Good crisis management requires a combination of established procedures, professional assessments and the ability to improvise

[3960] The weighting between these must be done based on, among other things, the nature of the incident, the tasks that must be solved and the roles of the various actors

[3961] The police, which leads the interagency effort in the area of operation, have a broader area of responsibility than other agencies involved

[3962] The police must both carry out their professional police duties and have sufficient overview and situational understanding to coordinate other resources in crisis management

[3963] The police are therefore subject to different requirements than other agencies, and their tasks will vary greatly during different types of incidents

[3964] This indicates that the police must approach the task with a great degree of variation in task execution, depending, among other things, on the nature of the incident

[3965] Two experienced police response leaders have described what they believe is crucial to success

[3966] “When the very starting point for the demanding missions lies beyond what we may be familiar with, prepared for, or equipped for, it is natural to ask how one can conduct management and solve these missions

[3967] In our opinion, it is impossible to get past concepts such as improvisation, creativity and intuition

[3968] In police jargon, these concepts often fall within what we refer to as good situational assessment. Presence, experience, intuition and professional knowledge are central to good task performance

[3969] This has much in common with the emphasis on initiative, creativity and independence in task performance that is inherent in the Armed Forces' concept of mission-based leadership

[3970] Common to both civilian and military crisis management is that mission-based leadership on the ground is not enough to deal with large, serious incidents

[3971] In addition, strategic and operational management is required that enables the response team and others close to the incident to perform their part of the mission optimally

[3972] Good crisis management requires that each level carries out its mission with the specific characteristics and requirements set for that level, and with good cooperation and information flow between the levels

[4034] National procedure for emergency services' cooperation in the event of ongoing life-threatening violence – PLIVO In crisis situations, the lives of those involved may be at stake, and the efforts may be dangerous for the crews

[4036] National procedure for emergency services cooperation in the event of ongoing life-threatening violence – PLIVO was developed jointly by the Directorate of Health, POD and DSB

[4037] The procedure describes what is expected of the agencies individually and in collaboration with others

[4038] This involves clarifying responsibilities, roles and tasks at headquarters and in the task forces

[4039] The overarching principles of responsibility, equality, proximity and cooperation have formed the basis of the work, see chapter

[4040] PLIVO has strengthened cooperation between emergency services and provided common understanding and patterns of action

[4041] In the development of PLIVO, a common language and a unified approach have been central

[4042] This can be transferred to other situations and as a future working methodology, regardless of the type of incident

[4043] An important and positive side effect is that a network has now been established that strengthens cooperation throughout the country, and which can be used in other interdisciplinary projects in the emergency services

[4044] In order for emergency personnel from the police, fire and health services to be able to interact in line with these procedures, significant and sustained efforts are required in terms of training, joint training and joint exercises

[4045] This is important because actual incidents of ongoing life-threatening violence occur rarely, and because the pattern of action in this type of action in some areas deviates from normal routines

[4046] The agencies are well underway with continuous training, joint training and exercises

[4047] Emergency personnel in the police, fire and health services must train together annually to ensure good competence and response capabilities in incidents covered by the PLIVO procedure

[4053] Learning from exercises and events

[4054] Challenges and government policy Fortunately, large, serious incidents rarely occur

[4055] Therefore, we must practice to become good at handling such incidents

[4056] Learning from exercises and incidents is important to improve the ability to handle future incidents

[4057] A number of evaluations of exercises and incident handling have been carried out in recent years

[4058] A key point has been that learning points are repeated

[4059] This may indicate that there has not been sufficient ability to systematically follow up and learn from previous events and exercises

[4060] Furthermore, it has been pointed out that it is demanding to ensure learning among both individuals and organizations involved in an exercise or the handling of an incident

[4061] The report of the July 22 Commission emphasized the importance of thoroughly prepared exercises to ensure effective response

[4062] It also pointed out that in many places there had been too little practice or that not enough lessons had been learned from the exercise

[4063] The Norwegian Health Authority's inspection and the Office of the Auditor General's performance audit of the Ministry of Justice and Public Security's civil security work also pointed to the need for more systematic utilization and dissemination of the learning potential after exercises and incidents, as well as more systematic follow-up of learning points

[4064] The Government will: – introduce requirements for follow-up of findings from incidents and exercises within the area of civil security in the civil sector in the state administration – that all incidents and exercises shall initially be evaluated and findings and learning points shall be followed up through a management-based action plan – that follow-up of exercises and incidents shall not be considered completed until all points in the action plan have been followed up satisfactorily – that results of the follow-up of exercises and incidents above a certain size/severity shall be reported to a higher authority

[4065] Requirements for follow-up of learning after exercises and incidents

[4066] The government wants the greatest possible learning outcome from exercises and events

[4067] The Government will therefore introduce new requirements for following up on findings from incidents and exercises in the area of 'civil security in state administration in the civil sector

[4068] The requirements are intended to ensure that experiences and learning points are followed up at all levels in a systematic and satisfactory manner

[4069] The new requirements are based on the premise that all events and exercises should initially be evaluated

[4070] Secondly, it is emphasized that findings and learning points from evaluations should be followed up through a suitable action plan

[4071] This plan must be management-based

[4072] Furthermore, it is important that follow-up of exercises and incidents is not considered completed until all points in the action plan have been followed up in an appropriate manner

[4073] The effect of measures must be assessed, or the measures must be acknowledged through a management-based assessment

[4074] Finally, it is important that the results of the follow-up of exercises and incidents above a certain size/severity are reported to the higher authority

[4198] Different types of exercises A common division of different exercise forms is discussion exercise, game exercise, functional exercise and full-scale exercise

[4199] A discussion exercise is an exercise where participants sit together and discuss a problem or scenario

[4200] The exercise is characterized by the participants going through together how they want/can solve or handle different types of problems/challenges or tasks

[4201] The scenario or problems should be designed to challenge the participants' coping skills

[4202] A game exercise is an exercise that tests the crisis management capabilities of a number of authorities/actors based on given principles, guidelines and/or guidelines for crisis management

[4203] You can practice in a constructed environment or in ordinary premises

[4204] Everything should be carried out as if it were a real handling of a real incident

[4205] A functional exercise is an exercise that tests one or more functions of an actor, for example whether a warning system functions satisfactorily

[4206] Functional exercises are usually completed within a few hours or at most a day

[4207] Functional exercises are characterized by the participants practically implementing functions described in the emergency and crisis plan

[4208] A full-scale exercise consists of several actors at different levels from different sectors

[4209] It is practiced at both a tactical and operational level

[4210] In some cases, strategic level is also practiced

[4211] The format is often used in connection with exercises involving rescue services, police, healthcare and defense, but can also occur in other areas

[4234] Risk in a safe society As with any exercise, systematic learning is possible and important

[4237] A broad perspective on learning

[4238] The government's new requirements for monitoring learning will help identify weaknesses and deficiencies

[4239] It is a prerequisite for being able to improve

[4240] However, it is important that the learning has a broad perspective

[4241] Exercises and events can also provide important information about what works well

[4242] Knowing that something works provides security for affected actors, and can signal that these characteristics should be further strengthened

[4243] By recognizing that something was done right here, the positives can be reinforced and possibly transferred to other areas where improvement is needed

[4244] There is also important learning in being able to reflect on strengths, vulnerabilities and prerequisites for success

[4245] The learning value in the form of such a more fundamental understanding of one's own skills therefore does not depend on making changes in practice

[4246] Learning points can occur multiple times

[4247] This may be a warning of inadequate follow-up of learning points from previous exercises or events, a lack of ability to learn, or an inability to apply new knowledge in new exercises or events

[4248] It is important to find the reason why learning points may reoccur, and assess whether the reason is acceptable or not

[4249] Several reviews show that different agencies and organizations have identical or nearly identical learning points

[4250] This is because there are different organizations that rehearse or handle an incident

[4251] Exercise HarbourEx15 – an example of good learning in all phases of an exercise In April 2015, exercise HarbourEx15 was held on Sjursøya in Oslo

[4252] HarbourEx15 was the largest full-scale exercise Norway has ever had and was a combined exercise where several exercises for different professional communities were combined

[4253] The exercise was designed to test both individual and collective learning, learning across sectors, and to ensure good follow-up of findings and improvement measures

[4254] In order to carry out an exercise of this size, the planning process became very important

[4255] Working groups were established based on thematic areas and across sector lines

[4256] During the planning phase, lines of communication, coordination routines, procedures and guidelines were jointly reviewed

[4257] This led to considerable individual learning

[4258] Through the evaluation work carried out in connection with the exercise, the organizational learning is also clear

[4259] An important step was the preparation of a joint document describing the way forward after the exercise

[4260] Based on the evaluation report, an action plan was prepared that contains nine cross-sectoral measures

[4261] The document specifies a measure for solving the problem for each challenge, along with a description of the effect the measure is expected to have, who is responsible for the measure and the deadline for implementation

[4262] The measures are particularly aimed at further developing coordination, collaboration and communication

[4263] Once implemented, they will be able to increase the crisis management capabilities of the actors involved when handling major incidents

[4272] Learning for different purposes

[4273] An organization's ability to handle an incident or conduct an exercise should be independent of which individuals participate

[4274] The government therefore wants, through the introduction of the new requirements, to contribute to ensuring that exercises and events provide both individual and organizational learning

[4275] This requires that experiences gained by individuals are transferred to the organization

[4276] However, surveys conducted by DSB show that emergency personnel and others who participate in exercises and incidents gain individual experiences, but that individual learning does not necessarily foster organizational learning

[4277] When individuals participate in an exercise or the handling of an incident, they test their personal competence and gain individual experience

[4278] Translating individual learning into organizational learning requires good routines and systematics for compiling, discussing and drawing common conclusions about what has been learned

[4279] Learning points must then be incorporated into plans, routines, training programs and other formal frameworks for the business, and become part of the organization's common knowledge base

[4280] Such work must be prioritized within the organization and by management

[4281] This emphasizes that learning is an important management task

[4283] There may be several reasons for this

[4284] The more trivial explanations may be that the participants feel they are finished with the exercise and move on to other tasks

[4285] It may be that the exercise is primarily experienced as a duty or a ritual

[4286] The learning points can also be demanding to follow up on, either because they require major changes or because the challenges are about conditions that there may be resistance to doing anything about, such as cultural differences, Survey from DSB

[4287] National Exercise and Evaluation Forum DSB has established the National Exercise and Evaluation Forum (NØEF) to support the work with, and coordination of, exercise and evaluation activities within the area of civil security and emergency preparedness in Norway

[4288] With this comes a greater responsibility to strengthen overall national expertise when it comes to sharing experiences, developing methods, and collaborating on what needs to be practiced

[4289] NØEF is a coordinating and facilitating forum consisting of representatives from ministries, directorates, agencies, county governors, municipalities, owners and operators of critical infrastructure, etc. NØEF works to carry out the following tasks: – prepare guidance material for planning, implementation, evaluation and follow-up of exercises – administer the National Exercise Calendar – arrange exercise and evaluation seminars for the forum – arrange professional days in counties or selected sectors – have an overview of existing course offerings and develop competence development measures within exercise planning and evaluation – participate in Nordic cooperation in the exercise and evaluation area, including close cooperation with the ‘Central Exercise Forum’ in Denmark and the ‘National Forum for the Coordination and Coordination of Exercises’ (NAFS) in Sweden

[4290] The forum will particularly support cross-sectoral knowledge sharing, exchange of experiences and collaboration with a view to creating a common basis for the development of exercises and evaluations

[4291] The forum will initially focus on all types of exercises

[4292] However, it is emphasized that the forum will not conduct exercises or evaluations – even if individual members of the forum do this in their own businesses

[4306] Risk in a safe society

[4307] The cross-sectoral work on societal security

[4308] Challenges and government policy

[4309] A number of challenges within the field of public security are cross-sectoral

[4310] Whether we are talking about floods, fires, landslides, serious accidents, pandemics or terrorist attacks, many different sectors are affected

[4311] Such challenges cannot be handled within one sector alone, or at a single level of administration

[4312] An essential part of societal security work is identifying, assessing, managing and monitoring risks across sector boundaries

[4313] This work is a continuous process

[4314] Based on knowledge of threats and risks, it must be assessed which measures are most cost-effective and what effect they could have

[4315] Once measures have been implemented, it must be assessed whether the risk has been reduced to an acceptable level, or whether further measures are necessary

[4316] The work involves difficult trade-offs

[4317] What risks are most important for the authorities to work on reducing

[4318] What preventive measures should be implemented first

[4319] What effect do measures within one sector have on other sectors

[4320] What skills should be strengthened so that society is better equipped to handle any incidents

[4321] Risk management should provide decision-makers with a basis for prioritizing both within and across sectors

[4322] The work on societal security must also handle a complex target picture

[4323] The overarching goal is to protect fundamental societal values, see chapter 3.1, but different agencies have different goals within their respective areas of responsibility

[4324] The work on specific risks and incidents is based on the chain perspective (see Chapter

[4325] Risk management is about strategic work on societal security, i.e. how authorities at all levels can and should work to ensure effective knowledge building, make sensible priorities and develop suitable instruments

[4326] Knowledge from risk management work can contribute to the work in various parts of the chain

[4327] The Government will strengthen and further develop cross-sectoral work on societal security, and improve the instruments that form the basis for the work

[4328] The Government is particularly concerned that the work must have a good knowledge base, that actors at local, regional and central levels clarify roles and responsibilities and cooperate well, and that the necessary continuity in the work is ensured

[4329] The Government will: – establish a system in the civil sector to prepare status/condition assessments for the 14 critical societal functions

[4330] Reporting must be done for all functions within 4 years

[4331] The ministries with primary responsibility shall present the assessments in their respective budget propositions – clarify for users what is discussed in various threat, risk and vulnerability assessments – follow up on supervision of the ministries’ societal security work until all breaches of requirements and significant conditions have been rectified – evaluate the third round of supervision of the ministries’ societal security work, and use the evaluation to assess the need for changes in the Ministry of Justice and Public Security’s use of supervision as a tool – strengthen interaction between emergency actors by working towards uniform use of concepts and terminology, including by preparing a “Handbook for the Rescue Service” – ensure a better knowledge base for policy formulation and management by actively using research in the societal security field – further develop the county governor’s societal security work – appoint a committee to assess a cross-sectoral authorization provision in the emergency preparedness legislation with a view to extraordinary situations

[4351] All departments and the Prime Minister's Office participate

[4352] The Central Total Defence Forum is a meeting place at agency level for mutual orientation, coordination and overall coordination related to current issues related to total defence

[4355] Responsibilities of the ministries

[4357] The ministries' responsibilities are based on the principle of accountability, see chapter

[4359] Among the ministries' tasks are to assess and implement preventive and emergency measures, to be prepared to handle any crisis in their own sector, and to clarify their own responsibilities and roles in relation to other ministries' adjacent areas

[4377] Status and condition overview

[4378] The division into 14 critical societal functions and the placement of responsibility with a department with primary responsibility is a key instrument for strengthening cross-sectoral coordination of work on societal security

[4379] An overview of status and condition will provide an opportunity to see connections across sectors and provide knowledge about where measures are needed in areas that are critical to societal security

[4380] The Government will establish a system in the civil sector to prepare status/condition assessments for the 14 critical societal functions

[4381] Reporting for all functions must be done within four years

[4382] The ministries with primary responsibility shall present the assessments in their respective budget proposals

[4383] The Ministry of Defence and the defence sector will, within the current division of responsibilities between civil and military preparedness, have a supporting role towards other ministries and sectors in their work with status/condition assessments

[4384] Status/condition assessments within the field of societal security should be based on an overview of risk and vulnerability, inspection reports and follow-up of these, as well as objectives, measures and results within the area, based on relevant national goals and strategies

[4385] The Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness will contribute to the work with guidance and expertise on societal security issues and methods, so that assessments across the areas are as uniform as possible

[4386] Parts of the documentation and assessments may be classified or sensitive information, and if necessary, classified assessments will also be prepared for the government

[4387] DSB has worked to develop a systematic approach to an overview of vulnerabilities related to society's critical functions

[4388] The purpose is to highlight and gain an overview of vulnerability factors that, according to the directorate's professional assessment, should be prioritized

[4389] The Norwegian Defence Research Institute (FFI) assists DSB in the development work

[4390] The work must be seen in the context of the preparation of status/condition assessments in the area of civil security, follow-up to NATO's seven expectations for resilient civil functions, as well as any vulnerabilities identified in crisis scenarios prepared by the DSB

[4391] It is important to achieve good synergy and a comprehensive system for monitoring critical societal functions

[4392] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security will assess the scope of reporting and analyses as tools against the use of other tools to help the ministries and their sectors improve their preparedness capabilities

[4393] The new requirements for status/condition assessments must therefore be seen in the context of relevant established systems

[4425] Coordination with the defense sector, NATO and the EU

[4426] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security has a coordinating role for civil security and preparedness in the civilian sector

[4427] The Ministry of Defence is responsible for the defence sector's work on public security and emergency preparedness and is therefore not covered by the specific requirements in the instructions

[4428] There are good systems for condition assessments in the defense sector, such as the annual Assessment of Operational Capability

[4429] Every four years, a Long-Term Plan for the Defense Sector is also presented

[4430] These systems meet the requirement for status/condition assessment for the socially critical function "Defense", see Table

[4431] The Ministry of Defence will be able to support the ministries in the civilian sector with information and assessments from the defence sector as a contribution to their status/condition assessments

[4432] Norway has long been involved in the EU's work on civil preparedness and crisis management through the so-called "coordination mechanism

[4433] Participation entails, among other things, that Norway is obliged to conduct and make available a structured assessment of Norwegian risk management capabilities by August 2018, and every three years thereafter

[4434] As described in Chapter 10.4, NATO wants resilient societal functions, because it is a prerequisite for the individual country's and the Alliance's overall civil preparedness and defense

[4435] NATO has therefore established seven basic expectations for its member states, which were adopted at the NATO Summit in July

[4436] NATO's priority areas partly coincide with the critical societal functions that have been developed for Norwegian authorities. The Government sees it as appropriate that the work to meet NATO's expectations is seen in the context of the general work to reduce the vulnerability of critical societal functions

[4437] It will nevertheless be necessary to make adjustments to and assess the expectations that NATO places on Norway in this work, and to have more detailed follow-up from the Ministry of Justice and Public Security of these commitments

[4438] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security, together with the affected ministries and DSB, has established a program to further develop total defense and increase resilience in critical societal functions, see chapter

[4439] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security, in collaboration with affected ministries, shall ensure that the requirements for reporting to the EU and NATO in relevant areas are based on and coincide as much as possible with national work

[4440] The work should be well coordinated to, as far as possible, ensure synergies and avoid parallel processes

[4441] The status / condition assessment system constitutes a key basis for reporting to the EU under the coordination mechanism and for review and action within NATO's seven expectations for resilient societal functions

[4442] Threat and risk assessments

[4443] The Police Security Service (PST), the National Security Authority (NSM), the Intelligence Service (E-tjenesten) and the DSB make annual assessments of various conditions that may threaten Norwegian interests or values that we wish to protect, see box

[4444] In sum, the analyses encompass a broad spectrum of possible incidents, from terror and intelligence against Norwegian interests, to accidents, sabotage and serious natural events

[4445] The assessments are an important part of the work of identifying risks and analyzing the world around us

[4446] The assessments serve a two-fold purpose

[4447] They shall inform the public about matters that may threaten Norwegian interests, and they shall contribute to transparency about the agencies' work

[4448] They can also provide important input into the risk management of sectors and businesses, so that risk understanding is improved

[4449] They are in addition to ongoing assessments that the E-service, PST and NSM carry out regarding actors and activities that may threaten Norwegian interests, and which are intended to ensure that the government and other authorities implement necessary measures

[4450] DSB's crisis scenarios are more long-term, and the current situation is not affected

[4451] There is a certain degree of thematic overlap between the assessments

[4452] International terrorism, threats in the digital space and serious crime are examples of topics discussed in several of them

[4453] This can make it challenging for users to distinguish the assessments from each other, even if they are prepared in line with the agencies' respective mandates, have different purposes and different emphasis (threats, vulnerability, consequences, etc

[4454] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security, in collaboration with the Ministry of Defence, the E-service, PST, NSM, DSB and the Police Directorate, has considered various coordination measures that can make it easier for users to understand the purpose and alignment of the individual agency's assessment, as well as clarify how they differ from each other

[4455] From 2017 onwards, it will be clearer in the individual agency's assessment which mandate and assignment. Resolution in the Storting in the spring of 2014, see Prop

[4459] Since 2011, DSB has prepared scenario analyses that deal with both unwanted, unintentional events and intentional actions

[4460] The report has until now been called the "National Risk Picture" (NRB

[4461] It currently contains 22 scenario analyses

[4462] This "all hazards" approach is in line with the EU coordination mechanism and OECD recommendations

[4463] DSB assesses the consequences for important societal values under the stresses that unwanted events may entail

[4464] The scenario analyses are well received among users in departments, at regional and local levels, and are recognized abroad

[4465] The crisis scenarios have a long-term time horizon and do not reflect the current risk and threat picture

[4466] The analyses therefore do not provide a complete overview of risks and vulnerabilities

[4467] The name “National Risk Picture” may therefore seem somewhat misleading, and the name will be changed from 2016 to “Crisis scenarios (years) – analyses of serious incidents that could affect Norway”

[4468] Crisis scenarios of intentional actions must be developed in close dialogue with agencies that conduct threat, risk and vulnerability assessments, such as the E-service, PST and NSM

[4469] It is more challenging to assess the probability of intentional actions than the probability of unintentional events such as landslides or a major accident

[4470] The government will strengthen the coordination of the annual threat, risk and vulnerability assessments of the E-service, PST, NSM and DSB, to clarify for users what is discussed in each individual assessment, and to make it easier to compare across the agencies' assessments

[4471] Other measures are: – ensure closer coordination of the use of terms and communication of probability in the annual assessments of the E-service, PST, NSM and DSB – facilitate and contribute to systematic follow-up in the sectors of any risk and vulnerability identified in DSB's crisis scenarios Supervision of the ministries' civil security work

[4472] Supervision of the ministries' work on public safety is a key instrument in the Ministry of Justice and Public Security's exercise of its coordinating role, see Royal Decree 15 June

[4473] The inspections are intended to ensure that each ministry within its area of responsibility contributes to strengthening society's ability to prevent and manage crises

[4474] The inspectorates shall monitor the ministries' work within the entire social security chain

[4475] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security's implementation and follow-up of findings from inspections is based on risk and materiality

[4476] Annual threat and risk assessments

[4477] The intelligence service assesses conditions abroad and foreign threats that affect the security of Norway and Norwegian interests

[4478] This year's assessment, "Focus 2016", describes at an overall level

[4479] current conditions and security threats within different countries, regions and themes

[4480] The threat assessment of the Police Security Service deals with conditions, primarily in Norway, that could affect Norwegian security and harm national interests in the coming year

[4481] These include threats from state actors in the form of foreign intelligence services, current intelligence targets and the services' operational patterns in Norway

[4482] The assessments also address threats from non-state actors, and in particular threats of politically motivated violence from extremist groups or individuals

[4483] The National Security Authority prepares an annual report on the state of preventive security under the scope of the Security Act

[4484] In the report, NSM assesses the risk that critical societal functions and infrastructure, sensitive information and people will be affected by espionage, sabotage, terror and other serious acts

[4485] In addition, NSM prepares an annual comprehensive ICT risk assessment that aims to increase awareness of ICT security

[4486] The report describes challenges for various societal actors and measures for ICT security work in businesses

[4487] The Directorate for Civil Protection and Emergency Preparedness has published crisis scenarios

[4488] The crisis scenarios deal with risks associated with catastrophic events that could affect Norwegian society and that it should be prepared to face

[4489] The Ministry of Defence is only covered by the instructions' provisions on basic principles and central crisis management and is thus not covered by the requirements for supervision in the instructions

[4491] Risk in a safe society

[4492] The inspection reports and the ministries' follow-up plans form the basis for the ministries' work to improve prevention, emergency planning and crisis management

[4493] The supervisory regime was changed in 2014 by introducing an assessment of whether the findings involve a breach of requirements

[4494] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security follows up on the inspections until all violations of requirements and significant improvement points have been corrected

[4495] The changes from 2014 also mean that the inspection reports are public, and that the government is informed about the results and follow-up of each individual inspection

[4496] On behalf of the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, DSB has carried out inspections of the ministries in three rounds since its inception

[4497] There is increasing attention to the importance of the work, and the ministries are working more systematically with planning, exercises and follow-up of underlying agencies

[4498] All ministries have now had their social security work inspected for the third time

[4499] Three ministries had no violations of requirements

[4500] Inspections of six ministries are being followed up, and other inspections have been completed

[4501] Although most ministries have strengthened their social security work, the main findings from the latest round of inspections show that the systematic nature of the work, leadership support and overview of risk and vulnerability in several ministries should still be strengthened

[4502] The same applies to the ministries' work on planning and exercises

[4503] Findings from inspection reports show that the ministries' contingency plans should be anchored in their own overview of risk and vulnerability

[4504] The crisis organization described in the ministries is not always practiced in the event of serious incidents and crises, and there is a lack of plans and exercises for the ministries' role as lead ministries

[4505] The instruction's requirements for exercises are linked to, among other things, exercise frequency and who will practice together

[4506] Most ministries formally meet the requirements, but the exercises often have a modest format, with few participants, and are not very focused on revealing weaknesses in the emergency preparedness organization

[4507] Several ministries also have potential for improvement with regard to evaluating exercises and incidents, and in implementing changes as a result of the evaluations

[4508] One challenge is the lack of congruence between the risk picture within the department's area of responsibility and the scenarios being practiced

[4509] It is important that oversight helps to make ministries better able to uncover the real vulnerabilities within their area of ​​responsibility

[4510] However, the effect of supervision is difficult to measure

[4511] It is difficult to know whether observed improvements in the departments' work are the result of the departments knowing they are being supervised, or whether the changes would have taken place anyway

[4512] There is also a question of whether the structure of the inspections, which is system-oriented, is appropriate in the future

[4513] The introduction of breach of requirements has also led to an increased need to clarify the content of the requirements

[4514] In the autumn of 2016, an evaluation of the third round of supervision of the ministries' social security work was initiated

[4515] The inspection round has been ongoing from the fall of 2011 through

[4516] The evaluation will, among other things, assess whether the use of resources in the third round of supervision, from the planning phase up to and including the follow-up phase, is in proportion to the effect the supervision has on the ministries' social security work

[4517] It should also be considered whether other instruments than the current supervisory regime might be better suited to assessing how the ministries' social security work is functioning

[4518] The evaluation will provide the Ministry of Justice and Public Security with a good basis for further developing the inspections as a policy instrument

[4519] The Directorate for Public Administration and ICT (Difi) together with the Norwegian Defence Research Institute (FFI) will carry out the evaluation

[4520] Coordination of terminology

[4521] The use and understanding of terms can be of great importance in the work on societal security, and is important for a precise and sound professional debate within the societal security field

[4522] If different agencies and actors have different understandings of concepts, it can lead to misunderstandings, weakened interaction and ultimately affect our ability to handle incidents

[4523] Coordination of the use of terms – in the sense of promoting a common understanding of key concepts within the field of social security – is therefore desirable

[4524] Concepts are also important tools for individual agencies in their daily work

[4525] Different actors work within different professional traditions, with associated terminology

[4526] For example, the police's use of terminology is the result of many years of work, which includes the development of the police's intelligence doctrine and participation in international professional cooperation

[4527] For DSB, the conceptual framework in their crisis scenarios is based on other professional environments, nationally and internationally

[4528] Coordination of concepts must therefore be based on an understanding of the professional traditions to which different agencies relate

[4529] If different agencies are to base their work on common conceptual understandings, the concepts should also be able to be used in the professional tradition to which the individual agency relates

[4530] St. 10 Risk in a safe society

[4531] The most important concepts are those that several different agencies use and that are used most frequently

[4532] It is also important that concepts used in a critical situation, such as during an incident, are not misunderstood between actors

[4533] Chapter 3 presents key concepts within the field of social security and the understanding that underpins this report to the Storting

[4534] The Government is working towards a uniform and common understanding of the concepts most frequently used by key actors in the field of social security

[4535] This is continuous work and will take place through further development of cross-sectoral planning, instructions, routines, manuals and through training and exercises

[4536] An example is the coordination of the use of terms in threat, risk and vulnerability assessments within the justice and defense sectors, see

[4537] Another example is the recently published national procedure for the cooperation of the emergency services in the event of ongoing life-threatening violence (PLIVO) where key concepts were clarified, see chapter 11.6.6. Another important work to establish common concepts is a project that will result in a Handbook for the Norwegian rescue service

[4538] The starting points for the work are the police emergency response system, the health service's definition catalogue and the fire and rescue service's planning system

[4539] The work is led by the Norwegian Central Rescue Centre on behalf of the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Situations

[4540] Several voluntary rescue organizations are involved in the project

[4541] The Language Council is also involved

[4542] It is important to have a good process in this work, so that the different professional communities jointly arrive at concepts that can be agreed upon

[4543] In addition, conceptual clarifications and coordination of the use of terms within the ICT field are ongoing

[4544] This Box 13.3 Challenges in the work on societal security A main challenge in the work on societal security is that we do not know what will happen in the future, and what we can avoid through prevention and good preparedness

[4545] We also cannot know whether the absence of an incident is due to good preventive work, or whether the incident would not have occurred anyway

[4546] Similarly, it is difficult to know whether preparedness is good enough to handle incidents that have not occurred

[4547] The best way to deal with this is to work systematically to identify threats, risks and dangers, prevent unwanted incidents, reduce vulnerability in society, and build up good preparedness and capacity for crisis management and recovery

[4548] Measures against rare serious incidents should, to the greatest extent possible, improve society's general resilience and our ability to handle several different types of situations

[4549] It can be challenging to know what effect work on public safety at a central level has on the ability to prevent and handle incidents in a municipality or a business

[4550] A local fire and rescue service can work thoroughly and systematically to prevent tunnel fires and practice handling them, regardless of what the county governor, DSB or other state authorities have contributed

[4551] Similarly, central authorities may have developed good guidance material and good risk analyses, but local authorities and others must use the information in their planning and security measures for it to have the desired effect

[4552] Municipal surveys, inspections, etc. show that measures from central authorities are being used and contribute to strengthening public safety efforts

[4553] However, the effect on societal security is indirect, through good work by affected actors

[4554] A further challenge is related to the complexity of the field

[4555] In some areas, we accumulate considerable knowledge and experience over time, such as forest fires, floods and landslides, serious crime, etc

[4556] Even if there are not the same number of floods every year, we can develop indicators that provide a basis for assessing the effect of flood protection, whether preparedness has improved, etc

[4557] Other social security conditions are more complicated, often with many dependencies

[4558] The Digital Vulnerability Committee describes how critical societal functions have become dependent on long and confusing digital value chains, which often span many sectors and several countries

[4559] The authorities can manage risks associated with such complex chains to a lesser extent using ordinary target and performance management

[4560] We cannot be sure that a selection of indicators gives us a good picture of the robustness and vulnerability of the system

[4561] An important prerequisite for good governance is therefore the ability to commission research and studies, as well as to handle, "translate" and compile the results into knowledge that can be converted into practical policy

[4564] Research in the area of ​​societal security

[4565] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security fulfils its responsibility for research within the field of public security through funding of research and by ensuring targeted use of research and development

[4566] Similarly, it is important that all responsible sectors allocate funds for this and make use of R&D activities

[4567] It is important to ensure that we always have a good and up-to-date knowledge base for policy formulation and practical work on societal security

[4568] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security has prepared an R&D strategy for civil security for the period

[4569] The strategy highlights the following knowledge needs: – factors that strengthen society's resistance or resilience – vulnerability in complex critical societal functions – risk, risk understanding and recognition – governance, organization, culture and management of societal security work – operational cooperation and interaction – prevention of terrorism and other intentional acts with great potential for harm The goals of the strategy include improving the ability to identify and understand serious risks, threats and vulnerabilities in society, improving innovation within the societal security field, and increasing the use of R&D as a knowledge base for policy formulation and practice

[4570] The strategy has been followed up with measures within all themes, and the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness will implement the R&D strategy in the coming four-year period

[4571] Among the important measures will be to establish a strategic partnership with a research community within the CBRNE field

[4572] In addition, DSB has prepared its own R&D strategy that reflects the breadth of the directorate's administrative areas

[4600] Community safety work at the municipal and regional level

[4601] Work at the municipal level

[4602] Municipalities have been given statutory tasks related to public safety

[4603] The new Act on Planning and Building Procedures (Planning and Building Act) came into force on 1 January

[4604] This emphasizes public safety as a consideration that must be taken into account in all planning according to the law

[4605] Among other things, the law requires that risk and vulnerability analyses be carried out when developing new areas or changing land use, as a preventive measure against incidents

[4606] The Act on Municipal Emergency Preparedness, Civil Protection Measures and the Civil Defence (Civil Protection Act) from 2010 imposes a duty of preparedness on municipalities

[4607] They must have an overview of risk and vulnerability conditions that may be of importance to the municipality (holistic risk and vulnerability analysis), and follow this up through emergency planning and preventive work

[4608] Good public safety work requires professional expertise that is easier to maintain in larger municipalities

[4609] Fire and rescue services with small professional teams and part-time management can face significant challenges when the scale and complexity of the incident has exceeded ordinary handling capacity

[4610] At the same time, small communities can have qualities that are important during an incident, with an overview of local resources and a spirit of volunteerism that is important when it really matters

[4611] There need not be a contradiction between professionalizing public safety work and emergency preparedness work that builds on qualities in a local community that are important for good incident management

[4612] Both parts are important and need to be further developed

[4736] In some areas, cross-sectoral regulations have nevertheless been adopted

[4737] An example is the Act on Municipal Emergency Preparedness, Civil Protection Measures and Civil Defence (Civil Protection Act) and the Act on Industrial Emergency Preparedness (Industrial Emergency Preparedness Act

[4738] The Civil Protection Act came into force on 25 June 2010 and the responsible ministry is the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness

[4739] The Act is intended to help private and public actors, including businesses, municipalities and the Norwegian Civil Defence, implement measures to protect the civilian population in the event of unwanted incidents in war and peacetime

[4740] Municipalities are legally required to have a general emergency preparedness obligation

[4741] The duty to be prepared entails an obligation for municipalities to prepare a comprehensive risk and vulnerability analysis (ROS analysis

[4742] Through the work on the cross-sector ROS analysis, the municipality will map which undesirable events can occur, assess the probability of these events occurring, and how these events could affect the local community

[4743] The results of the ROS analysis must be followed up with a contingency plan for the municipality, specifying measures for handling crisis situations in the municipality

[4744] The County Governor supervises that the municipality meets the statutory requirements

[4745] A regulation has been established regarding municipal emergency preparedness obligations, which specifies the municipality's obligations in more detail

[4746] The authority to establish regulations has been delegated to DSB

[4747] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security has asked DSB to conduct a review of current regulations and assess the need for new regulations

[4748] A draft of a new regulation on the requisition of real property, etc. has been put out for consultation and the consultation statements are being reviewed

[4749] The purpose of the regulations is to provide further provisions on requisitions for use in handling the tasks of the Civil Defence

[4750] The regulations are intended to be applied in war, war-like situations and in the event of undesirable incidents in peacetime

[4751] DSB is continuing to work on preparing joint regulations on Civil Defence

[4752] The proposed regulations deal with both the rights and obligations of those subject to military service, and the municipalities' joint responsibility for storing the Civil Defence's materiel

[4753] A separate provision is also proposed on notification in war, when war threatens and in peacetime, and a separate provision on evacuation in war or warlike situations

[4754] The Food Emergency Preparedness Act The Food Emergency Preparedness Act came into force on 1 January

[4755] The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries is administratively responsible for the act

[4756] The act regulates the relationship between public authorities and businesses in preparing and implementing cooperation routines and measures for crises with significant consequences for access to goods and services in Norway

[4757] The purpose of the law is to alleviate the supply-related consequences of crises by strengthening access to goods and services and ensuring the necessary prioritization and redistribution of goods and services through cooperation between public authorities and businesses

[4758] Contact with the business community should be based on cooperation and volunteerism to the greatest extent possible

[4759] The additional financial costs or losses incurred by businesses in preparing and implementing special measures under the Act shall be compensated by the authority responsible for the measure

[4760] It has been decided that the Ministry of Health and Care Services and the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, in addition to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries and the Ministry of Agriculture and Food, shall have regulatory authority under the Food Emergency Preparedness Act

[4761] These ministries can thus regulate the supply of goods and services within industries for which these ministries have professional responsibility

[4762] For the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, it is particularly envisaged that regulations may be needed to regulate the relationship with businesses that operate asylum reception centres if there is a mass influx of asylum seekers and it has not been possible to enter into adequate voluntary agreements

[4773] Challenges and government policy

[4774] The purpose of preventive security under the Security Act is to counter threats to national security and other vital national security interests

[4775] The Preventive Security Service Act (Security Act) and regulations are intended to protect information and objects against espionage, sabotage and terrorist acts

[4776] The law regulates the selection and classification of information and objects, as well as requirements for protective measures to eliminate or reduce such risks

[4777] The protective measures include organizational, personnel, technological and physical measures

[4778] To create good preventive security, the measures must be seen in context

[4779] The security framework has changed significantly since the Security Act came into force in 2001. Increased flow of goods, services and labor across national borders, together with technological developments, has created changed framework conditions

[4780] Norway has become one of the world's most digitalized countries, and our digital assets have increased significantly

[4781] Developments have led to civilian actors, both public and, not least, private, increasingly managing vital assets such as critical infrastructure, societal functions and sensitive information

[4782] Technological developments are challenging security work, including through new ways of producing, sharing and storing socially important information

[4783] It has become more difficult to keep track of the dependencies that exist across sectors, businesses and infrastructures

[4784] It is therefore challenging for the individual business to assess what consequences the loss of its own values may have in a holistic, national perspective, and thus challenging to identify and classify its own values

[4785] Interconnection of ICT

[4786] systems increase the vulnerabilities that expose assets to threat actors

[4787] This makes us vulnerable, both to accidents and human failure, but also to security-threatening activities against Norwegian interests

[4788] Chapter 6 describes challenges related to ICT security and digital vulnerabilities and the government's policy in this area

[4789] Measures to strengthen ICT security will in many cases also be preventive security measures, and the two chapters should therefore be seen in context

[4813] Need for changes to the Security Act

[4814] There has been no comprehensive revision of the Security Act since it came into force

[4815] However, the risk and threat landscape facing society has changed significantly since then

[4816] In 2013, a working group was established for a comprehensive revision of the law

[4817] The work revealed fundamental challenges regarding what the Security Act should regulate, including the relationship between the Security Act and other security-related sectoral regulations

[4818] It was decided to divide the work on revising the law into two phases

[4819] In the first phase, some specific, minor changes were to be identified that could be quickly implemented without prior analysis

[4820] Phase two involves a new comprehensive revision of the Security Act

[4821] The legislation should ensure a comprehensive, robust and future-oriented preventive framework, as well as take into account technological development, demographic changes and the changing security landscape

[4822] On 8 June 2016, the Storting passed Act of 12 August 2016 No. 78 on amendments to the Security Act; that is, the first phase of the legislative work

[4823] The legislative resolution was based on Recommendation

[4824] L (2015–2016) and Prop

[4825] L (2015–2016), and entails a number of changes to the Security Act, including: – reduction of the number of clearance authorities, to one central clearance authority in the civil sector and one equivalent in the defence sector – new provisions on notification, and authority to make decisions, in the event of a risk of security-threatening activities in procurements for critical infrastructure – change from assignment-based to time-limited supplier clearances in connection with security-graded procurements In addition, current practice in certain areas was legislated, including – NSM's responsibility for the national response function for serious computer attacks against critical infrastructure (NorCERT) – NSM's responsibility for the alert system for digital infrastructure (VDI) – the framework for the NorCERT and VDI functions' processing of personal data – security monitoring of information systems approved for processing security-graded information

[4826] The adopted amendments to the Security Act with a reduction in the number of clearance authorities are a central measure in preventive personnel security

[4827] The change essentially means that one clearance authority is established in the defense sector and one in the civilian sector

[4828] The new civil clearance authority will be a new agency directly subordinate to the Ministry of Justice and Public Security

[4829] S (2016–2017) for the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, the government proposes that the new clearance authority be established in 2017, with operations

[4830] One of the main priorities for NSM in the coming years is to be a proactive and accessible professional authority for personnel safety

[4831] The change in the number of clearance authorities will lay the foundation for increased competence and quality in case processing, as well as increase legal certainty for the individual and ensure equal treatment of cases
