[4909] Risk in a safe society

[4910] The work on social security cannot be viewed from a limited, national perspective

[4911] The threats and risks facing Norway are largely linked to developments outside our borders

[4912] Close cooperation with other countries is necessary to both prevent and manage the challenges

[4913] Cross-border challenges require cross-border cooperation

[4914] For the government, it is important to highlight cooperation with our neighboring countries in the Nordic region, and international cooperation in the High North

[4915] NATO and the EU are important partners for Norway in the areas of civil security, emergency preparedness and crisis management in a regional context

[4916] The UN has a leading role in a global context

[4917] In recent years, our transatlantic cooperation, particularly with US authorities, has also become more important

[4918] International work is an integral part of most areas of societal security addressed in this report

[4919] For example, it is difficult to imagine an effective rescue service without the main rescue center having daily and ongoing contact with its international partners

[4920] The work on CBRNE preparedness cannot be done without also looking at the practices of other countries and participating in international cooperation

[4921] International work is therefore discussed in many chapters of this report

[4922] This chapter discusses some specific cooperation forums, agreements or obligations that apply to social security work in general

[4923] The Government will: – continue the good Nordic cooperation, especially within the Haga cooperation – be an active participant in the EU’s coordination mechanism for civil preparedness – work for cross-sectoral, Norwegian participation within the new program area on disaster prevention within the framework of EEA funds – contribute to revitalizing guidelines on humanitarian-military cooperation under the auspices of the UN – actively work for international standards within civil security

[4924] Nordic cooperation

[4925] Nordic cooperation is important to the government, also within the field of social security

[4926] The White Paper on Nordic cooperation, Report to the Storting 6 (2015–2016), states that “Nordic cooperation is a high priority for the government and is constantly changing”, and the government’s political platform states that “The government will strengthen Nordic cooperation on crisis and emergency preparedness work”

[4927] Nordic cooperation within public security has traditionally been good

[4928] The Haga Declaration from 2009 stated that the Nordic countries should jointly investigate and specify cooperation within rescue services, training and education, preparedness against weapons of mass destruction (CBRNE), crisis communication with the population, the use of volunteers, and research and development

[4929] The declaration also contributed to increased awareness of the overall Nordic ability to resist and handle accidents and crises

[4930] In 2013, a new platform for Nordic cooperation in the field of public safety was established (the Hague II Declaration

[4931] The goal of this declaration was a robust Nordic region through, among other things, prevention, handling and recovery from serious incidents

[4932] It was also a goal to achieve a Nordic region without borders, so that bureaucratic and practical obstacles to cross-border cooperation would be avoided

[4933] The Haga II Declaration drew attention to the fact that Nordic cooperation within societal security could contribute to greater impact in the EU and other international forums

[4934] Nordic emergency preparedness cooperation has also been considered in other forums

[4935] A Nordic declaration of solidarity has been negotiated, and several reports on Nordic and Baltic emergency preparedness cooperation have been prepared

[4936] The government is committed to continuing the good Nordic cooperation, especially within the framework of the Haga cooperation

[4937] This involves following up on Haga II through joint Nordic projects that stem from the conclusions of the annual meetings of the Nordic ministers responsible for civil security

[4949] Rescue cooperation in the north

[4950] Throughout history, it has been important for Norway to have good rescue and emergency preparedness agreements with our neighboring countries

[4951] The High North is characterized by long distances and scattered resources

[4952] Personnel and equipment in a neighboring country may be closer to an accident than national resources

[4953] The ocean areas in the north are changing, and the melting ice brings opportunities for greater economic activity in the area, both within petroleum activities, shipping, fisheries and tourism

[4954] This provides many opportunities, but also challenges related to rescue, safety and emergency preparedness

[4955] Cooperation between countries in the region is therefore very important

[4956] Cooperation with Russia on search and rescue in the High North has been important for many years, and will continue to be important in the future

[4957] In 1995, Norway and Russia signed an agreement on cooperation in search and rescue in the Barents Sea

[4958] The agreement originally originated

[4959] From the Norwegian perspective, it is the Main Rescue Centre of the North

[4960] Norway is responsible for organizing and coordinating search and rescue efforts in the Barents Sea, as well as organizing exercises with the same purpose

[4961] Annual exercises are arranged between Norway and Russia in accordance with the agreement

[4962] Norway is also a party to an agreement from 2008 on cooperation on prevention, preparedness and response to crisis situations in the Euro-Arctic Barents region

[4963] The other parties are Sweden, Finland and Russia

[4964] The concept of crisis is broadly defined, and encompasses life, health, the environment and material assets

[4965] The agreement applies to the northernmost parts of the land areas of the three Nordic countries, and the northwestern regions of Russia

[4966] The agreement is practiced through the "Barents Rescue" exercise series, which is held every two years through

[4967] In April this year, the contracting parties agreed to arrange the exercise every three years

[4968] This will make it possible to base the next exercise on the experiences from the previous one

[4969] Responsibility for conducting the exercise rotates between the four countries

[4970] In September 2013, Norway was the host country for the exercise, and in 2015 the exercise was organized in Finland

[4971] The next exercise will be in 2017 in Russia, and planning is well underway

[4972] When it comes to sea and air rescue, the UN's maritime and aviation organizations, IMO and ICAO, have divided the world's sea and air areas into rescue zones

[4973] Norway therefore has a responsibility far beyond its territorial borders

[4974] In 2011, Norway signed an agreement with Canada, Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Russia, Sweden and the USA on cooperation on search and rescue in connection with aviation and maritime traffic in the Arctic

[4975] Norway's area of responsibility for search and rescue was thus expanded by Norway taking responsibility further east towards the Russian area of responsibility, and north of Svalbard all the way up to the pole, see Figure 15.1. The agreement, which entered into force on 19 January 2013, establishes a more binding rescue cooperation, including a better regional organisation of search and rescue in the Arctic

[4976] The background to the agreement is that increased activity and traffic in the Arctic requires strengthened rescue cooperation between the countries responsible for search and rescue in Arctic waters

[4977] It is particularly the long distances, the harsh climate and the relatively few rescue resources that motivated the agreement

[4978] Some exercises have been carried out based on the agreement

[4998] EU Coordination Mechanism for Civil Protection and Crisis Management

[4999] Civil protection work in the EU is anchored in the Lisbon Treaty and operationalised through the EU's coordination mechanism for civil preparedness and crisis management, the Union Civil Protection Mechanism

[5000] Mechanism" in which Norway participates through the EEA Agreement

[5001] The purpose of the EU's civil protection mechanism is to facilitate broad cooperation in Europe within civil protection

[5002] The scheme requires that the participating states join forces to make their resources available to disaster-stricken countries, both inside and outside Europe

[5003] The scheme is intended to make it easier to request assistance where unique resources are required, or in cases where own resources are being depleted

[5004] Participation in the EU coordination mechanism thus also contributes to increasing national preparedness for all types of civil incidents, including on Norwegian territory

[5005] The Government is concerned that our association with the EU Coordination Mechanism constitutes a central pillar in our expanded national preparedness and has committed Norway to participate in the Coordination Mechanism until 2020. A strengthened international crisis management capability, increased predictability, and availability of resources and improved transport support schemes provide increased added value for Norway

[5006] Participation in this collaboration is valuable in terms of the opportunities for receiving specialists, European assistance in the event of major incidents nationally, but also in that the prevention perspective in third countries is emphasized

[5007] The scheme also provides opportunities to finance exercises and projects, train Norwegian personnel, exchange expertise and experiences, and provide access to relevant situation analyses and information products. European cooperation thus helps to strengthen Norway's efforts for civil security, both nationally and internationally

[5008] If Norway chooses to respond to requests for assistance from the coordination mechanism, participation also allows us to apply for reimbursement of up to 85 percent of our own costs related to the dispatch of emergency assistance such as material, personnel or other forms of assistance to incidents, as described in Table 15.2. The EU increasingly sees civil protection as an integral part of the work to increase internal security in Europe

[5009] The large migration flows in 2015, closely followed by the terrorist attacks in Paris and Brussels, have reinforced the need for solidarity and information exchange between countries

[5010] The work of mapping risk and reducing vulnerability in a regional and European perspective is therefore important for the EU

[5011] It is an initiative the government wants Norway to continue to be an active participant in

[5033] Cooperation with the UN

[5034] The UN plays a key role in coordinating humanitarian responses to natural disasters and complex crises, mainly through the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA

[5035] A successful humanitarian response requires close cooperation between UN organizations, NGOs, military actors and national authorities

[5036] The Government's overall goal is to support the UN's coordinating role in humanitarian crises to ensure an effective response

[5037] As international military actors have taken on a more important role in humanitarian crises, OCHA's scheme to promote coordination between civilian and military actors has also gained in importance

[5038] Some events have made clear how important international military support can be

[5039] In complex crises, security challenges can characterize the humanitarian approach

[5040] For example, during the earthquake in Nepal, it was difficult to reach affected people, partly due to a lack of security

[5041] The cooperation between civilian and military actors is nevertheless challenging

[5042] OCHA administers a set of guidelines that are intended to ensure that international military support in humanitarian crises is based on respect for humanitarian principles

[5043] This means a clear division of roles between civilian and military contributions and mandates

[5044] The use of military support should be a last resort, in other words, when civilian resources are exhausted, unavailable or practically difficult to use

[5045] Norway has itself promoted this approach in its own international military operations and played an important role in the development of the guidelines

[5046] As a step in revitalizing the guidelines, the UN has initiated a process of developing new standards for humanitarian-military cooperation

[5047] The standards will be launched at a conference in Oslo in the fall of

[5048] Cooperation between the EU and the UN in disaster response is constantly increasing in scope

[5049] To avoid duplication of systems and capacities, Norway, among others, has been a driving force for a clear division of responsibilities between these two organizations

[5050] The International Humanitarian Partnership (IHP) is an informal humanitarian collaboration between a number of governmental emergency response organizations in Europe

[5051] Norway has actively participated in the IHP network since the IHP countries agreed to put together joint “modules”, consisting of equipment and crew, and transport solutions when organizations such as the European Free Trade Association Financial Mechanism Office

[5117] Standards are a necessary and important tool for ensuring good security in critical infrastructure and critical societal functions

[5127] Economic and administrative consequences

[5128] St. 10 Risk in a safe society Economic and administrative consequences In the government's political platform, Safety in everyday life and strengthened preparedness are highlighted as one of the government's eight important priority areas

[5129] This white paper explains the government's policy for work on social security for the next four years

[5130] Social security is a broad field that affects most sectors and many different areas of society

[5131] The report does not aim to provide an exhaustive account of everything that is done of importance for societal security, but highlights some important, cross-sectoral areas

[5132] Significant parts of the social security work take place in each individual sector, based on relevant sector legislation and specific requirements for the ministries' social security work

[5133] The work should be an integrated part of ordinary management

[5134] If the risk and vulnerability picture changes, as we see several examples of, for example, related to ICT security, it is important that the measures and the policy instruments are adjusted accordingly

[5135] Changes in the use of instruments, and any measures implemented as a result of changes in the risk and vulnerability picture, shall be covered within the current budget limits

[5136] If measures result in expenditure increases above the state budget, the government will return to this in connection with the annual budget proposals

[5137] Measures for improved learning after exercises and incidents have consequences for internal management and prioritization in relevant businesses

[5138] The same applies to measures related to culture and management

[5139] An important prerequisite for better learning and collaboration is dialogue, leadership support and perseverance in implementing interagency work

[5140] This requires time, attention and prioritization from the organizations affected

[5141] The work must be prioritized within ordinary budget limits

[5142] The government has an ambition to strengthen social security work in several key areas

[5143] The report refers, among other things, to a number of strategies, action plans, etc. for the coming years that could entail additional expenses

[5144] The measures will initially be covered within the current budget framework

[5145] The government will return to any expenses or savings that exceed the current budget limits in connection with the annual budget proposals

[5146] It is therefore not possible to set a time when the measures might be implemented

[5178] Other measures

[5179] Several countries are conducting extensive and serious espionage against Norway

[5180] Certain countries have the capacity to inflict significant damage on Norway and Norwegian interests if they succeed in their operations

[5181] The Police Security Service (PST) currently does not have the capacity to prevent and investigate digital espionage and sabotage attempts from other states in a satisfactory manner

[5182] In the 2017 state budget, the government has proposed to increase the allocation in 2017 to PST by NOK 7 million to strengthen PST's preventive work, so that they are better able to handle the serious developments related to threats in the digital space

[5183] PST processes large amounts of data

[5184] PST needs systems that can make the service more efficient in everyday life, during extraordinary events and in crises

[5185] In the 2017 state budget, the government has proposed allocating NOK 9 million in 2017 for a technology upgrade for PST, including better tools for analysis

[5186] New technology systems will better enable PST to prevent a terrorist attack on Norwegian soil and provide better decision-making support to the government, police and defense

[5187] With new technology systems, PST will be able to move more quickly from analysis to actions that prevent terror

[5188] Decision-making bases will be able to be prepared both more quickly and with higher quality than is the case today

[5189] This was also one of the conditions that the evaluations after the terrorist attacks on July 22, 2011 pointed out

[5190] Better tools for analysis will also help strengthen privacy and the EOS Committee's legal control of the service, because it ensures traceability and transparency of data

[5191] ID work ID work will be strengthened in 2016 through increased use and storage of biometrics

[5192] In 2016, the Storting adopted amendments to sections 100 and 100a of the Immigration Act, which provide authority to routinely record and process biometric personal information in the form of fingerprints and facial photographs of all third-country nationals applying for a residence permit and visa to Norway

[5193] In the 2017 State budget, the government proposes to allocate NOK 81 million to the police and the Directorate of Immigration to strengthen the control of the identity of persons entering and residing in the kingdom, as well as to prevent and combat illegal residence and crime based on false ID and misuse of ID

[5194] Including expanded use of biometrics, more mobile handheld devices that enable identity verification, establishing a loss and verification system for public and private actors, as well as preparing national ID cards for foreign citizens and verification of foreign ID documents

[5198] Safety in everyday life – the local police reform), the government has received approval for the fire and rescue service's emergency services to be located together with the police's operations centers

[5199] Furthermore, the geographical boundaries of the emergency service will be adapted to the new police districts, but at the same time so that a 110 centre can cover more than one police district

[5200] The co-location process is closely linked to the Police Directorate's progress plan for establishing new police districts

[5201] A reduction in the number of 110 centres, by co-locating them with the police operations centres, will ensure that operators can strengthen their competence by handling more incidents

[5202] Experience from co-located emergency call centers also indicates that co-location provides better services for the public, especially during major incidents involving multiple emergency services

[5203] In the 2017 state budget, the government has proposed increasing the allocation by NOK 35 million to co-locate two additional 110 centers with the police operations center

[5207] When establishing a new vocational school, the fire and rescue service will

[5208] increase operational handling capacity, higher quality of preventive work and the municipalities will be provided with important expertise within public safety work

[5212] Work against antibiotic resistance In January 2016, the Ministry of Health and Care Services published an Action Plan against Antibiotic Resistance in the Health Service with the goal of reducing antibiotic use in the population by 30 percent by the end of

[5213] The Ministry of Health and Care Services earmarked NOK 6 million in 2016 to follow up on this action plan, and the government is also proposing this in the state budget

[5214] In addition, the regional competence centers for infection control have been strengthened with approximately NOK 3.5 million to assist in the implementation of antibiotic stewardship programs in health authorities

[5215] In March 2016, the Ministry of Agriculture and Food published an Action Plan against Antibiotic Resistance within the Ministry of Agriculture and Food's sectoral responsibility, which specifies measures to reduce the use of antibiotics in livestock by at least 10 percent and the use of antibiotics in pets by at least 30 percent compared to consumption

[5216] In the proposed state budget for 2017, the government proposes to strengthen the work against antibiotic resistance by increasing the allocations to the Norwegian Food Safety Authority and the Veterinary Institute in the Ministry of Agriculture and Food's budget by a total of NOK 10 million

[5221] Appendix 1 Central crisis management in Norway

[5222] Basic principles The national social security work is based on the basic principles of responsibility, equality, proximity and cooperation

[5223] – The responsibility principle, which means that the organization that is responsible for a subject area in a normal situation is also responsible for the necessary emergency preparedness preparations and for handling extraordinary events in the area. – The similarity principle, which means that the organization one operates with during crises should initially be as similar as possible to the organization one has on a daily basis

[5224] – The subsidiarity principle, which means that crises should be handled organizationally at the lowest possible level

[5225] – The principle of cooperation, which means that authorities, businesses or agencies have an independent responsibility to ensure the best possible cooperation with relevant actors and businesses in the work of prevention, preparedness and crisis management

[5226] The principles are discussed in more detail in chapter

[5227] The Storting's plenary session sets important frameworks for military and civil preparedness, for example through emergency preparedness legislation and the annual budget decisions

[5228] Important foreign and security policy, defense policy and emergency preparedness issues are handled by the Extended Foreign and Defense Committee (DUUFK

[5229] The committee consists of the ordinary members of the Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, the President of the Storting and the leaders of the party groups

[5230] The chair convenes the committee when he or she deems it necessary, or when the Prime Minister, the Minister for Foreign Affairs or one third of the committee members request it

[5231] The same applies when the Minister of Defence requests it in important preparednessrelated issues, or when the Minister of Justice and Preparedness requests a discussion of issues concerning terrorist preparedness

[5232] The negotiations are secret unless otherwise expressly decided

[5233] The Government has the ultimate responsibility for preparedness in Norway, including the overall political responsibility for both the management and handling of preventive preparedness work and crises that arise

[5234] The government is dealing with a number of emergency matters, both through the budget process and in discussions of matters in government conferences

[5235] According to our state customs, each minister has constitutional responsibility in his or her area, within the laws and appropriations granted by the Storting

[5236] This means that the individual minister retains his constitutional responsibility even in a crisis situation

[5237] If the Prime Minister so wishes, a matter may, instead of being considered in plenary session in the government, be considered in the Government Security Committee (RSU

[5238] The RSU consists of the Prime Minister, the Minister of Justice and Emergency Preparedness, the Minister of Defense, the Minister of Finance and the Minister of Foreign Affairs

[5239] In addition, other ministers may be invited if the matters affect their areas of responsibility

[5240] RSU will primarily be relevant for matters of a defense, security policy or emergency nature where the content indicates limited dissemination of information

[5241] In some cases, it will follow from the Constitution, legislation or decision-making regulations that necessary formal decisions must be made by the government through a resolution of the King in Council

[5242] This applies, for example, to crises that are of such a serious nature that it is appropriate to implement powers in accordance with emergency legislation, submit proposals to the Storting, or declare command authority for Norwegian military forces

[5243] A significant degree of flexibility is planned when it comes to organizing the work

[5244] In many situations it will be appropriate for civil servants to

[5245] Instructions for the ministries' work on civil security and emergency preparedness, the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness' coordination role, supervisory function and central crisis management

[5246] St. 10 Risk in a safe society works from affected ministries and affected agency heads participate in meetings in the government, RSU and the Crisis Council, see discussion below

[5247] The Prime Minister leads and coordinates the work of the Government

[5248] These are tasks the Prime Minister would also have in a crisis situation

[5249] The Prime Minister will also play a central role in external communication, contact with other countries' heads of government, international organizations, parliamentary leaders in the Storting, the Royal House, etc

[5250] The Prime Minister's involvement in each crisis will depend on the nature and scope of the crisis

[5251] In crises that fall within the scope of the Emergency Preparedness Act, the Prime Minister has been delegated special powers in situations where it is imperative to make decisions to safeguard society's interests

[5252] The Prime Minister's Office must plan so that the Prime Minister and the Government can carry out their duties even in crisis situations

[5253] The Prime Minister's Office also performs tasks as secretariat for government conferences, the Norwegian Council of State and the King in Council

[5254] The Prime Minister's Office must be able to provide administrative support, secretarial functions and contribute with advice

[5255] The ministries The administrative system for central crisis management builds on the basic principles of societal security

[5256] This means that the department that is responsible for a sector on a daily basis is also responsible for emergency planning and measures in a crisis situation

[5257] In the event of crises, the ministries will obtain situation reports from their own operational agencies and identify and make decisions on necessary measures within their own areas of responsibility to handle the current situation

[5258] They will prepare a basis for decision-making and facilitate overall political clarifications where necessary

[5259] The ministries must be able to handle communication with the media and the public

[5260] The work must be coordinated with other ministries and especially the ministry designated as the lead ministry

[5261] The ministries must ensure that operational actors have the necessary authorizations, so that the need for handling at the government level does not delay the handling of acute situations where there is a danger to life, health or major loss of material assets

[5262] The Crisis Council is the highest administrative coordination body at the ministry level, and was established to strengthen central coordination

[5263] it has five permanent members

[5264] the government councillor at the Prime Minister's Office, the foreign councillor at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the ministerial councillors at the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Health and Social Care, respectively

[5265] If necessary, the council can be expanded to include all other ministries, and representatives of underlying agencies and special expertise environments

[5266] All ministries can take the initiative to convene the Crisis Council

[5267] The Ministry of Leadership chairs the council meetings

[5268] If a lead ministry has not been decided, the council is led by the Ministry of Justice and Public Security

[5269] The crisis council is not only called upon in times of crisis or major incidents

[5270] A system has also been established with regular, periodic meetings of the Crisis Council, approximately every four to six weeks

[5271] It has been appropriate for the purpose of discussing and anchoring overall emergency preparedness and crisis management challenges and reviewing relevant incidents and exercises

[5272] Lead Ministry The lead ministry is responsible for coordinating the handling of a crisis at the ministry level

[5273] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security is the permanent lead ministry in civil national crises, unless otherwise determined

[5274] The Ministry's coordination responsibility and responsibility for the bulk of the civil rescue and emergency preparedness resources in Norway means that the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness will always have a central role in most cross-sectoral national crises

[5275] In some situations, and when it comes to incidents that primarily affect one sector, it will be natural for someone other than the Ministry of Justice and Public Security to hold the lead department role

[5276] The Crisis Council has been given authority by the government to decide which ministry should be the lead ministry in a particular crisis, and the Crisis Council will decide whether the Ministry of Justice and Public Security or another ministry should be the lead ministry

[5277] In case of doubt or disagreement in the Crisis Council, the choice of the lead ministry is decided by the Prime Minister in consultation with the ministers concerned

[5278] The appointment of a lead ministry does not entail changes in constitutional responsibilities, and all ministries retain responsibility and decision-making authority

[5279] Parliament 10 2016–

[5280] Risk in a safe society regulatory authority for their respective areas of responsibility

[5281] In a crisis situation, the lead ministry shall, among other things: – prepare and distribute overall situation reports, including on the basis of information collected from other ministries, reports from operational agencies and the media – identify and assess the need for measures at a strategic level – coordinate that necessary measures within its own area of ​​responsibility are implemented, and ensure the necessary coordination with other ministries and agencies – ensure that coordinated information is provided to the media and the population The Crisis Support Unit and the Civil Situation Centre in the Ministry of Justice and Public Security The Crisis Support Unit (KSE) shall support the lead ministry and the Crisis Council in their coordination functions and is the permanent secretariat for the Crisis Council

[5282] KSE has expertise in strategic crisis management, as well as capacities in the form of infrastructure, such as mobile technical solutions

[5283] Upon request, KSE can assist other ministries with personnel support in their crisis management

[5284] KSE also supports the Ministry of Justice and Public Security's coordination role in the area of public security and public security

[5285] This includes contributions to training activities, as well as advice and guidance on crisis management to the ministries

[5286] The Civil Situation Centre is organised as part of KSE, and is a permanent point of contact for information to and from the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness in the event of extraordinary incidents and crises

[5287] Through the transition to a 24-hour manned presence in the Civil Situation Centre in 2014, the capacity for timely warning and analysis of the situational picture, as a basis for necessary decisions in crises, was significantly strengthened

[5386] Terrorist preparedness PST must take increased initiative and show greater willingness to cooperate and share information with other agencies, including the regular police and the Intelligence Service

[5387] The confidentiality provisions in the legislation should be harmonized with the established regulations for PST's work, so that PST can gain access to relevant information from other agencies in cases where they themselves are allowed to register information or open a case

[5388] Furthermore, confidentiality provisions should not prevent other public agencies from tipping off the PST where the agencies perceive that there is reason to investigate whether terrorist planning is taking place.
